elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决目前缺乏可靠方法预测慢性乙型肝炎患者对治疗反应的问题,因为长期抗病毒治疗可以逆转肝纤维化,但并非所有患者都能实现逆转。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本观点综述讨论了机器学习在改善慢性乙型肝炎患者纤维化逆转预测方面的潜力,重点关注临床工具在捕捉动态纤维化过程方面的局限性。
elements_zh.methods: 作者回顾了机器学习如何应用于分析影像数据、整合临床和病理数据,并通过在抗病毒治疗期间进行连续测量来预测患者对治疗的反应。
elements_zh.main_results: 机器学习在三个领域已显示出早期但有希望的结果:定量影像分析、临床和病理数据的多模态整合,以及基于连续测量的动态预测患者对治疗的反应。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释认为,机器学习的最大价值在于补充现有工具,特别是在识别那些仅通过抗病毒药物治疗难以实现纤维化逆转的患者方面,而不是取代它们。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,机器学习可能有助于提高慢性乙型肝炎治疗的功能性治愈率,并优化个性化治疗策略,从而改善纤维化逆转的预测能力并指导临床决策。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 目前的证据受到限制,因为大多数现有模型都是基于小规模、单一中心的回顾性数据,这可能影响其普适性,需要前瞻性多中心验证。

papers.abstract_zh: 尽管长期抗病毒药物治疗可以逆转慢性乙型肝炎患者的肝纤维化,但个体对治疗的反应差异显著,目前仍缺乏可靠的预测方法。传统的临床工具如肝硬度测量和天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶与血小板比值指数最初设计用于横断面分期,而非纵向预测,其捕捉纤维化逆转动态过程的能力有限。在本观点综述中,我们讨论了机器学习(ML)如何帮助解决这一未满足的需求。我们重点关注了机器学习在三个方面的早期但有希望的结果:利用机器学习进行图像的定量分析、通过多模态模型整合病理和临床数据,以及基于抗病毒药物治疗期间的连续测量动态预测治疗反应。我们认为,机器学习的最大价值并不在于取代现有评估工具,而在于补充它们,特别是在早期识别那些仅通过抗病毒药物治疗难以实现纤维化逆转的患者方面。然而,我们也提醒,目前大多数模型都是基于小规模、单中心的回顾性队列研究开发的,其临床应用需要前瞻性多中心验证、提高模型的可解释性以及遵循标准化的报告框架。

papers.title: Characteristics and clinical significance of hepatitis B virus RNA/DNA decoupling in patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection: a cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background A quantitative measure for assessing transcription-replication decoupling between serum hepatitis B virus (HBV) RNA and HBV DNA in patients with chronic HBV infection is currently lacking, and the clinical significance of this phenomenon remains to be clarified. This study constructed an HBV RNA/DNA decoupling index (HDI) and systematically evaluated its clinical associations. Methods A single-centre cross-sectional design was adopted, and 1210 patients with chronic HBV infection were enrolled (370 untreated and 840 receiving nucleos( t )ide analogue [NAs] therapy). The HDI was calculated as log10(HBV RNA) − log10(HBV DNA). Patients were stratified by treatment status and disease stage. Spearman correlation, Kruskal-Wallis H test, and multivariate linear and logistic regressions were performed. Results HBV RNA and HBV DNA were strongly correlated in untreated patients ( rs = 0.866), whereas the association weakened markedly in treated patients ( rs = 0.593). The HDI was highest in the low-level viraemia group and rose with disease stage ( H = 376.619 , P < 0.001). In HCC prediction, models incorporating HBV DNA or the HDI both improved discrimination over demographic variables alone (AUCs 0.783 and 0.776 vs 0.757), with the HDI-containing model performing comparably to the DNA-containing model. Conclusions The HDI quantitatively characterises HBV transcription-replication decoupling and is independently associated with disease stage and HCC risk. It may serve as a complementary tool to existing HBV serological monitoring.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 目前缺乏评估慢性 HBV 感染患者血清 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) RNA 和 HBV DNA 之间转录复制解偶联的定量方法,该现象的临床意义仍有待阐明。本研究构建了 HBV RNA/DNA 解偶联指数 (HDI) 并系统评估了其临床关联。方法采用单中心横断面设计,纳入1210例慢性乙型肝炎患者(其中370例未经治疗,840例接受核苷类似物[NAs]治疗)。HDI 计算为 log10(HBV RNA) – log10(HBV DNA)。根据 治疗 状态和疾病阶段对患者进行分层。进行了 Spearman 相关、Kruskal-Wallis H 检验以及多元线性和逻辑回归。结果 未经治疗的患者中 HBV RNA 和 HBV DNA 呈强相关性(rs = 0.866),而在接受治疗的患者中这种相关性显着减弱(rs = 0.593)。HDI在低水平病毒血症组最高,并随疾病分期而升高(H = 376.619,P < 0.001)。在 HCC 预测中,纳入 HBV DNA 或 HDI 的模型均改善了对单独人口变量的区分(AUC 0.783 和 0.776 vs 0.757),其中包含 HDI 的模型与包含 DNA 的模型表现相当。结论 HDI 定量表征了 HBV 转录-复制解偶联,并且与疾病分期和 HCC 风险独立相关。它可以作为现有乙肝血清学监测的补充工具。

papers.title: Prevalence of hepatitis delta virus (HDV) among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive blood donors followed at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) in Cte dIvoire
papers.abstract: Chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection exacerbates hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related liver disease.In Côte d'Ivoire, HDV is systematic not systematically screened among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)positive blood donors, and most regional estimates rely on anti-HDV serology, which indicates exposure but not active replication.This study aimed to determine HDV RNA replication positivity among HBsAgpositive blood donors followed at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) of the National Blood Transfusion Centre of Côte d'Ivoire (CNTSCI), using nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR).A cross-sectional study based on a non-probability convenience sample was conducted in March 2021.HDV RNA was detected by nested RT-PCR targeting two genomic regions (nucleotides 888-1122 and 313-485).Of 51 donors included, 75% were male (n = 38) and and mean age was 37 ± 9 years.HBV DNA results were available for 43 donors (84%).Among them, HDV RNA positivity was 88.9% (32/36) in those with detectable HBV viraemia and 100% (7/7) in those with undetectable viral load, giving an overall positivity 90.7% (39/43).This figure applies only to donors with available viral load data not the entire cohort of 51 donors.HDV RNA was also detected in donors receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) with suppressed HBV viraemia.Given the convenience sample of donors already in follow-up care, findings are hypothesis-generating rather than population-level estimates.These results support larger representative studies and systematic HDV screening during follow-up of individuals with chronic HBV infection.Key words: Hepatitis B virus/hepatitis delta virus (HBV/HDV) co-infection, nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), molecular epidemiology, convenience sample, transfusion medicine, West Africa.

Received 3 August, 2026; Accepted 13 October, 2026 Chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection exacerbates hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related liver disease. In Côte d’Ivoire, HDV is systematic not systematically screened among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)- positive blood donors, and most regional estimates rely on anti-HDV serology, which indicates exposure but not active replication. This study aimed to determine HDV RNA replication positivity among HBsAg- positive blood donors followed at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) of the National Blood Transfusion Centre of Côte d’Ivoire (CNTSCI), using nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). A cross-sectional study based on a non-probability convenience sample was conducted in March 2021. HDV RNA was detected by nested RT-PCR targeting two genomic regions (nucleotides 888–1122 and 313–485). Of 51 donors included, 75% were male (n = 38) and and mean age was 37 ± 9 years. HBV DNA results were available for 43 donors (84%). Among them, HDV RNA positivity was 88.9% (32/36) in those with detectable HBV viraemia and 100% (7/7) in those with undetectable viral load, giving an overall positivity 90.7% (39/43). This figure applies only to donors with available viral load data not the entire cohort of 51 donors. HDV RNA was also detected in donors receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) with suppressed HBV viraemia. Given the convenience sample of donors already in follow-up care, findings are hypothesis-generating rather than population-level estimates. These results support larger representative studies and systematic HDV screening during follow-up of individuals with chronic HBV infection. Key words: Hepatitis B virus/hepatitis delta virus (HBV/HDV) co-infection, nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), molecular epidemiology, convenience sample, transfusion medicine, West Africa. INTRODUCTION Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains one of the most widespread infectious agents worldwide. An estimated 254 million people were living with chronic HBV infection in 2022, resulting in approximately 1.1 million deaths, while only 13% of carriers had been diagnosed and 3% had received treatment (World Health Organization [WHO], 2024). Sub-Saharan Africa bears a disproportionate share of this burden, with hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) prevalence exceeding 8% in many areas and estimated at 9 to 12% among the general adult population in Côte d’Ivoire (WHO, 2021). A meta-analysis involving more than 3.5 million African blood donors reported a pooled HBsAg seroprevalence of 10.09% in West Africa, the highest among the continent’s five regions (Quintas et al., 2024). This substantial burden is consistent with findings indicating that HBsAg prevalence among blood donors at the National Blood Transfusion Centre of Côte d’Ivoire (CNTSCI) remained stable over two decades (Seri et al., 2018). Hepatitis delta virus (HDV), first described by Rizzetto in 1977 (Rizzetto et al., 1980), is a defective RNA virus that depends on HBV surface antigen for its replication and transmission. Consequently, HDV infection occurs only in HBsAg-positive individuals, either through simultaneous HBV/HDV coinfection or through HDV superinfection in individuals with pre-existing chronic HBV infection. Approximately 90% of individuals with chronic HBV infection who acquire HDV superinfection progress to chronic HDV infection, whereas simultaneous HBV/HDV coinfection is usually resolved, although serological markers may persist without ongoing viral replication (Rizzetto et al., 2021). This distinction is important when comparing anti-HDV antibody prevalence, which indicates previous or current exposure, with HDV RNA positivity, which provides evidence of active viral replication. HBV/HDV coinfection is associated with more severe liver disease than HBV monoinfection, increasing the risk of cirrhosis by approximately two- to three-fold and the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma by approximately two-fold. Cirrhosis may develop in 70 to 80% of affected patients within 5 to 10 years (Fattovich et al., 2000; Negro, 2014; Noureddin and Gish, 2014). Globally, an estimated 15–20 million HBsAg-positive individuals are thought to have HDV infection, although these estimates may be inflated when subpopulation weighting is not adequately considered (Rizzetto, 2015; Polaris Observatory Collaborators, 2024). Data on HDV infection in sub-Saharan Africa remain limited and heterogeneous. Reported anti-HDV seroprevalence ranges from approximately 7% in pooled estimates for West Africa to more than 25% in Central Africa (Stockdale et al., 2017). Country-specific estimates also vary considerably, ranging from 1 to 54% in Cameroon (Besombes et al., 2020), 7 to 22% in Mauritania (Mansour et al., 2012; Lunel-Fabiani et al., 2013), and 8 to 9% in Nigeria (Opaleye et al., 2016). In Senegal, active HDV replication confirmed by RNA testing was detected in 61.5% of anti-HDV-seropositive individuals, despite an Dechi et al. 21 overall anti-HDV seroprevalence of only 1.5% (Wembulua et al., 2025). These findings illustrate the distinction between antibody-based estimates of exposure and RNA- based evidence of active infection. Before the present study, published data on HBV/HDV coinfection in Côte d’Ivoire were very limited. Regarding treatment, pegylated interferon had long remained the principal therapeutic option, despite its limited efficacy (Wedemeyer et al., 2011). The approval of bulevirtide by the European Medicines Agency introduced a new treatment option for chronic HDV infection (Asselah et al., 2020), although access remains limited in resource-constrained settings. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of active HDV RNA replication among HBsAg-positive blood donors receiving follow-up care at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) of the CNTSCI, using nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) targeting two distinct HDV genomic regions. The secondary objectives were to describe the sociodemographic and virological characteristics of this population and examine the relationship between HDV RNA positivity and HBV viraemia. MATERIALS AND METHODS Study setting and design This was a cross-sectional, descriptive and analytical study conducted in March 2021 at the CNTSCI, specifically within the CMSDS. Laboratory analyses were performed at the molecular biology platform of the Immunology Laboratory of the UFR of Medical Sciences (UFR-SM) at Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny. Study population, sampling strategy and inclusion criteria The target population consisted of voluntary blood donors regularly followed at the CMSDS with confirmed positive HBsAg serology. Recruitment used a non-probabilistic, exhaustive convenience sampling strategy: all HBsAg-positive donors attending scheduled CMSDS follow-up visits during the study period and satisfying the inclusion criteria were consecutively invited to participate. Inclusion criteria were: (i) being a voluntary blood donor followed at the CMSDS; (ii) presenting a confirmed positive HBsAg result; and (iii) having provided consent to participate in the study. Donors whose biological samples were insufficient or of poor quality were excluded. Viral RNA extraction A preliminary centrifugation step of 1 mL of aliquoted plasma at 14,000 rpm for 1 hour at 4°C yielded a pellet enriched in viral particles, which served as the starting template for HDV RNA extraction. Extraction was performed using the QIAamp Viral RNA Mini Kit (Qiagen, Germany) according to the manufacturer's instructions. Extracts were stored at −80°C. The extraction protocol comprised the following successive steps: viral lysis, nucleic acid precipitation, RNA capture on a silica column, washing, and RNA elution. Viral lysis: 140 μL of the plasma pellet was added to 560 μL of AVL buffer containing carrier RNA. The mixture was vortexed for 15 s and then incubated for 10 min at room temperature. Precipitation and capture: After the addition of 560 μL of absolute ethanol and centrifugation, the lysate was transferred onto a QIAamp silica membrane column for selective binding of nucleic acids. Two successive washes (AW1 and AW2 buffers) removed contaminants. Final elution was performed with 60 μL of molecular-biology-grade water. An exogenous RNA internal control was added to each sample to monitor extraction efficiency, reverse transcription, and PCR inhibition. HBV DNA quantification Plasma HBV DNA was quantified using the COBAS® 4800 system (Roche Diagnostics, Switzerland), with a lower limit of detection/quantification of 10 IU/mL. HBV viral load was defined as detectable when >10 IU/mL and undetectable when <10 IU/mL. The same assay and threshold were applied to all donors with an available viral-load result. Study variables Sociodemographic data collected included sex, age, and educational level. Virological and therapeutic data comprised HBV viral load, antiviral treatment status (tenofovir disoproxil fumarate [TDF] or no treatment), and the qualitative HDV RNA (nested RT-PCR) result. Statistical analysis Data were entered using Microsoft Excel software and analysed using SPSS V27 statistical software International Business Machines Corporation (IBM). Qualitative variables were expressed as frequencies and percentages. Quantitative variables were described using the mean and standard deviation (SD). HDV RNA prevalence was calculated with its 95% confidence interval (95% CI), computed on the denominator of donors with an available HBV viral-load result, as distinct from the full enrolled cohort. Associations were tested using the chi-squared test or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate given expected cell counts, with statistical significance set at P < 0.05. No a sample size calculation was performed. Ethical considerations This study was conducted in accordance with the principles of the Declaration of Helsinki. Data were collected anonymously, and all participants provided written informed consent. The study forms part of the CNTSCI's epidemiological surveillance activities. analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence of hepatitis delta virus (HDV) RNA replication among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive blood donors in Côte d'Ivoire. A cross-sectional design was used, with a convenience sample of 51 donors, of whom 75% were male and the mean age was 37 ± 9 years. HDV RNA was detected using nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) targeting two genomic regions. Among 43 donors with HBV DNA results, 88.9% had detectable HDV RNA in those with HBV viraemia, and 100% had HDV RNA positivity in those with undetectable HBV viral load, resulting in an overall positivity of 90.7%. These results suggest a high prevalence of HDV co-infection among HBV-positive individuals and support the need for systematic HDV screening in follow-up care. However, the findings are hypothesis-generating due to the convenience sample used.

papers.source_body_en: Chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection exacerbates hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related liver disease.In Côte d'Ivoire, HDV is systematic not systematically screened among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)positive blood donors, and most regional estimates rely on anti-HDV serology, which indicates exposure but not active replication.This study aimed to determine HDV RNA replication positivity among HBsAgpositive blood donors followed at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) of the National Blood Transfusion Centre of Côte d'Ivoire (CNTSCI), using nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR).A cross-sectional study based on a non-probability convenience sample was conducted in March 2021.HDV RNA was detected by nested RT-PCR targeting two genomic regions (nucleotides 888-1122 and 313-485).Of 51 donors included, 75% were male (n = 38) and and mean age was 37 ± 9 years.HBV DNA results were available for 43 donors (84%).Among them, HDV RNA positivity was 88.9% (32/36) in those with detectable HBV viraemia and 100% (7/7) in those with undetectable viral load, giving an overall positivity 90.7% (39/43).This figure applies only to donors with available viral load data not the entire cohort of 51 donors.HDV RNA was also detected in donors receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) with suppressed HBV viraemia.Given the convenience sample of donors already in follow-up care, findings are hypothesis-generating rather than population-level estimates.These results support larger representative studies and systematic HDV screening during follow-up of individuals with chronic HBV infection.Key words: Hepatitis B virus/hepatitis delta virus (HBV/HDV) co-infection, nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), molecular epidemiology, convenience sample, transfusion medicine, West Africa.
papers.abstract_zh: 慢性丁型肝炎病毒 (HDV) 感染会加剧 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 相关肝病。在科特迪瓦,未对乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 阳性献血者进行系统性筛查,大多数区域估计依赖于抗 HDV 血清学,这表明暴露但不活跃复制。本研究旨在确定 HBsAg 阳性献血者中 HDV RNA 复制阳性情况。科特迪瓦国家输血中心 (CNTSCI) 的献血者医疗随访中心 (CMSDS) 使用巢式逆转录聚合酶链式反应 (RT-PCR)。2021 年 3 月进行了一项基于非概率便利样本的横断面研究。通过针对两个基因组区域(核苷酸 888-1122 和 313-485)的巢式 RT-PCR 检测了 HDV RNA。51 名捐献者中其中,75% 为男性 (n = 38),平均年龄为 37 ± 9 岁。43 名捐献者 (84%) 可获得 HBV DNA 结果。其中,可检测到 HBV 病毒血症的 HDV RNA 阳性率为 88.9% (32/36),病毒载量无法检测到的患者为 100% (7/7),总体阳性率为 90.7% (39/43)。该数字仅适用于具有可用病毒载量数据的捐献者,而不是 51 名捐献者的全部 队列研究。在接受富马酸替诺福韦二吡呋酯 (TDF) 且 HBV 病毒血症受到抑制的捐献者中也检测到 HDV RNA。考虑到已经处于后续护理中的捐献者的方便样本,研究结果是假设生成而不是人群水平估计。这些结果支持更大规模的代表性研究和个体随访期间的系统性 HDV 筛查关键词:乙型肝炎病毒/丁型肝炎病毒(HBV/HDV)合并感染,巢式逆转录聚合酶链反应(RT-PCR),分子流行病学,方便样本,输血医学,西非。

papers.title: Transplant-Free Recovery in Hepatitis B-Associated Acute Liver Failure Presenting With Cerebral Edema and Decerebrate Posturing.
papers.abstract: Acute liver failure (ALF) complicated by cerebral edema and intracranial hypertension carries a high mortality. We report a 31-year-old woman with acute hepatitis B-associated ALF who presented with grade IV encephalopathy, decerebrate posturing, and diffuse cerebral edema in the setting of severe hyperammonemia (ammonia 296 μmol/L). Invasive intracranial pressure monitoring was deferred because of profound coagulopathy. Despite a Model for End-Stage Liver Disease score of 29 and ineligibility for liver transplantation due to active substance use, she achieved complete neurologic and hepatic recovery with aggressive medical management. This case highlights that severe cerebral edema in ALF may be reversible with early recognition and multidisciplinary intensive care management, even in patients who are not transplant candidates.

papers.title: Semi-quantitative ultrasound scoring reveals hepatic structural recovery and immune modulation during tenofovir alafenamide therapy in chronic hepatitis B
papers.abstract: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic response to tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) using a semi-quantitative ultrasound (US) scoring system, and to investigate the correlation between sonographic changes and immune function restoration. Methods A total of 100 CHB patients who received TAF monotherapy (25 mg/day) for at least 24 months were retrospectively enrolled. A seven-parameter semi-quantitative US score, encompassing liver echogenicity, capsular contour, margin shape, vessel clarity, portal vein diameter (PVD), spleen thickness (ST), and splenic vein velocity (SVV), was calculated at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. Concurrently, serum hepatitis B virus (HBV) deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), peripheral T-cell subsets, including cluster of differentiation 3-positive (CD3 + ), CD4 + , CD8 + T cells, CD4+/CD8+ ratio, and natural killer (NK) cell activity were measured. Correlations between US scores and biochemical/immune parameters were analyzed. Results At 24 months, all patients achieved HBV DNA <20 IU/mL, with ALT and AST normalization rates of 92% and 95%, respectively. The comprehensive US score decreased significantly from 7.86 ± 1.73 at baseline to 3.37 ± 0.95 at 24 months ( P < 0.001), with the most pronounced improvements observed in capsular smoothness and parenchymal homogeneity. The CD4 + T-cell proportion and CD4 + /CD8 + ratio increased, whereas the CD8 + proportion decreased; NK cell activity rose from 42.7 ± 7.3% to 52.4 ± 6.2% ( P < 0.05). The US score was positively correlated with ALT (r = 0.56) and AST (r = 0.47), and negatively correlated with the CD4 + /CD8 + ratio (r = −0.46) and NK cell activity (r = −0.38) (all P < 0.01). Conclusion These findings indicate that TAF not only suppresses viral replication and normalises liver enzymes but also promotes measurable structural liver improvement, as reflected by declining semi-quantitative US scores. The strong correlations of US scores with biochemical and immune parameters support its utility as a non-invasive imaging biomarker for monitoring treatment efficacy and hepatic repair.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在利用半定量超声(US)评分系统评估替诺福韦艾拉酚胺二甲基磺酸盐(TAF)在慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)患者中的治疗反应,并探讨超声影像变化与免疫功能恢复之间的相关性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 回顾性纳入 100 名接受 TAF 单药治疗(25 毫克/天)至少 24 个月的慢性乙型肝炎患者。
elements_zh.methods: 在基线、12 个月和 24 个月时计算七参数半定量 US 评分,包括肝脏回声性、包膜轮廓、边缘形状、血管清晰度、门静脉直径 (PVD)、脾厚度 (ST) 和脾静脉速度 (SVV)。同时,测量血清 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 脱氧核糖核酸 (DNA)、丙氨酸转氨酶 (ALT)、天冬氨酸转氨酶 (AST)、外周 T 细胞亚群,包括分化簇 3 阳性 (CD3 + )、CD4 + 、CD8 + T 细胞、CD4 + / CD8 + 比率和自然杀伤 (NK) 细胞活性。
elements_zh.main_results: 在24个月时,所有患者均达到HBV DNA <20 IU/mL,ALT和AST的正常化率分别为92%和95%。综合超声评分从基线的7.86 ± 1.73显著下降至24个月的3.37 ± 0.95(P < 0.001),其中包膜平滑度和实质均匀性的改善最为显著。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 分析了美国评分与生化/免疫参数之间的相关性。US评分与ALT(r = 0.56)和AST(r = 0.47)呈正相关,与CD4 + /CD8 + 比值(r = -0.46)和NK细胞活性(r = -0.38)呈负相关(均P < 0.01)。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 超声评分与生化和免疫参数之间的强相关性支持其作为非侵入性影像生物标志物用于监测治疗疗效和肝脏修复的潜力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告局限性。

papers.abstract_zh: 本研究旨在利用半定量超声(US)评分系统评估替诺福韦艾拉酚胺二甲基磺酸盐(TAF)在慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)患者中的治疗反应,并探讨超声影像变化与免疫功能恢复之间的相关性。方法 入选了100例接受TAF单药治疗(25 mg/天)至少24个月的慢性乙型肝炎患者进行回顾性分析。在基线、12个月和24个月时计算了包含肝脏回声、包膜轮廓、边缘形态、血管清晰度、门静脉直径(PVD)、脾脏厚度(ST)和脾静脉血流速度(SVV)的七参数半定量超声评分。同时测量了血清乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)脱氧核糖核酸(DNA)、丙氨酸氨基转移酶(ALT)、天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶(AST)以及外周T细胞亚群,包括分化簇3阳性(CD3+)、CD4+、CD8+ T细胞、CD4+/CD8+比值和自然杀伤(NK)细胞活性。分析了超声评分与生化和免疫参数之间的相关性。结果 在24个月时,所有患者均达到HBV DNA <20 IU/mL,ALT和AST的正常化率分别为92%和95%。综合超声评分从基线的7.86 ± 1.73显著下降至24个月的3.37 ± 0.95(P < 0.001),其中包膜平滑度和实质均匀性的改善最为显著。CD4+ T细胞比例和CD4+/CD8+比值增加,而CD8+ T细胞比例下降;NK细胞活性从42.7 ± 7.3%上升至52.4 ± 6.2%(P < 0.05)。超声评分与ALT(r = 0.56)和AST(r = 0.47)呈正相关,与CD4+/CD8+比值(r = −0.46)和NK细胞活性(r = −0.38)呈负相关(所有P < 0.01)。结论 这些发现表明,TAF不仅抑制病毒复制并使肝酶正常化,还促进可测量的肝脏结构改善,这体现在半定量超声评分的下降。超声评分与生化和免疫参数之间的强相关性支持其作为非侵入性影像生物标志物用于监测治疗疗效和肝脏修复的潜力。

papers.title: Testing for hepatitis C virus and hepatitis B virus/hepatitis D virus: Current scenarios and perspectives in Italy
papers.abstract: Liver disease accounts for approximately 4% of all deaths worldwide, and viral hepatitis affects more than 300 million people. The World Health Organization aims to reduce new hepatitis infections by 90% and deaths by 65% by 2030 through vaccination and screening programs. In Italy, screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) benefits from dedicated government funding, whereas testing for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) is supported by recommendations from scientific societies but does not benefit from dedicated national public health programmes. This expert-opinion review summarises the experience of tertiary-level Italian centres actively engaged in hospital-based testing for HCV, HBV, and HDV and identifies practical pathways to improve testing and linkage to care. This article presents proposals to improve the effectiveness of viral hepatitis management in Italy by: (1) Strengthening coordination between hospital units and integrating information systems between general practitioners and hospitals; (2) Implementing a centralised reporting system and a structured referral network to ensure that patients with positive test results receive appropriate therapies in a timely manner; (3) Providing the resources needed to increase testing in public addiction treatment services (Servizi per le Dipendenze) and prisons; (4) Promoting screening in high-risk populations, including vulnerable and older populations; and (5) Implementing a national awareness campaign on viral hepatitis. These measures could help Italy make concrete progress towards eliminating HCV infection and controlling HBV/HDV infection within the next decade.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on the current testing scenarios for hepatitis B virus (HBV) in Italy, highlighting the lack of dedicated national public health programs for HBV and HDV compared to HCV. It outlines the importance of HBV in global liver disease and mortality, emphasizing the need for improved coordination between hospital units and general practitioners, centralized reporting systems, and enhanced testing in high-risk populations. The review also proposes increasing resources for testing in public addiction treatment services and prisons, and promoting national awareness campaigns on viral hepatitis. papers.title_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒和乙型肝炎病毒/丁型肝炎病毒检测:意大利当前状况与展望
papers.source_body_en: Liver disease accounts for approximately 4% of all deaths worldwide, and viral hepatitis affects more than 300 million people. The World Health Organization aims to reduce new hepatitis infections by 90% and deaths by 65% by 2030 through vaccination and screening programs. In Italy, screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) benefits from dedicated government funding, whereas testing for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) is supported by recommendations from scientific societies but does not benefit from dedicated national public health programmes. This expert-opinion review summarises the experience of tertiary-level Italian centres actively engaged in hospital-based testing for HCV, HBV, and HDV and identifies practical pathways to improve testing and linkage to care. This article presents proposals to improve the effectiveness of viral hepatitis management in Italy by: (1) Strengthening coordination between hospital units and integrating information systems between general practitioners and hospitals; (2) Implementing a centralised reporting system and a structured referral network to ensure that patients with positive test results receive appropriate therapies in a timely manner; (3) Providing the resources needed to increase testing in public addiction treatment services (Servizi per le Dipendenze) and prisons; (4) Promoting screening in high-risk populations, including vulnerable and older populations; and (5) Implementing a national awareness campaign on viral hepatitis. These measures could help Italy make concrete progress towards eliminating HCV infection and controlling HBV/HDV infection within the next decade.

papers.title: Post-treatment Serum Autotaxin and Subsequent Hepatocellular Carcinoma Development During Nucleos(t)ide Analog Therapy for Chronic Hepatitis B: An Exploratory Study.
papers.abstract: Objective The risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) persists despite nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. We investigated whether post-treatment serum autotaxin (ATX), a noninvasive fibrosis-related biomarker, is associated with subsequent HCC development during NA therapy.Methods We measured the serum ATX levels at baseline and at week 48 of NA therapy. Patients were followed for HCC development. The optimal ATX cutoff value was determined using a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, and cumulative HCC incidence was evaluated using the Kaplan-Meier method.Patients This retrospective single-center cohort study included 67 treatment-naïve patients with chronic hepatitis B who received NA therapy for at least 48 weeks.Results The median age was 59 years, and 58.2% of the patients were men. During a median follow-up period of 6.3 years, five patients developed HCC. The serum ATX levels decreased significantly after 48 weeks of NA therapy (0.93 vs. 0.84 mg/L, P < 0.001). Patients who subsequently developed HCC had significantly higher post-treatment ATX levels than those who did not (1.32 vs. 0.84 mg/L, P = 0.010). Among the evaluated fibrosis-related biomarkers, ATX showed the highest discriminative ability for HCC development, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.90. With an ATX/upper limit of normal ratio cutoff of 0.92, patients with elevated ATX levels that showed a significantly higher cumulative incidence of HCC than those with lower levels (10-year incidence: 25.0% vs. 1.96%, log-rank P = 0.001).Conclusions The serum ATX levels decreased after NA therapy, but remained elevated in patients who subsequently developed HCC. Validation of these preliminary findings in larger prospective cohorts is needed.

analysis.summary_en: This exploratory study investigated the association between post-treatment serum autotaxin (ATX) levels and subsequent hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) development in patients with chronic hepatitis B undergoing nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy. These findings may inform the use of ATX as a noninvasive biomarker for HCC risk monitoring in chronic hepatitis B patients.

papers.title: Local Stability and Threshold Analysis of an SEITR Model with Standard Incidence for Hepatitis B Transmission
papers.abstract: This study analyses the SEITR model of hepatitis B virus (HBV) transmission with a standard incidence rate of βSI/N in a population of variable size. The model is reduced to an autonomous system expressed in population proportions. The disease-free and endemic equilibria and their Jacobian matrices are derived, and the basic reproduction number is obtained using the next generation matrix method. The Routh-Hurwitz criterion establishes that the disease-free equilibrium is locally asymptotically stable if R_0 1. For disease-induced mortality μ_2>0, shows that the endemic equilibrium is unique and is locally asymptotically stable. For μ_2=0, the endemic equilibrium exists for R_0>1 and is locally asymptotically stable, with a forward bifurcation occurring at R_0=1. Numerical simulations calibrated to 2022 surveillance data from Ambon City, Indonesia, confirm the analytical results: the critical transmission rate is β^*≈0.432, and the critical vaccination coverage is σ^*≈0.622. The baseline value of R_0≈0.926 lies just below the threshold, resulting in very slow extinction of the infection over hundreds of years. Normalised sensitivity analysis indicates that R_0 is most sensitive to vaccination coverage, followed by the transmission rate and the treatment rate.
papers.journal: AlQalam Journal of Medical and Applied Sciences

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a mathematical analysis of the SEITR model for hepatitis B virus (HBV) transmission, focusing on the local stability of disease-free and endemic equilibria. The model incorporates a standard incidence rate and examines the impact of disease-induced mortality on the stability of the endemic equilibrium. The basic reproduction number (R_0) is calculated using the next generation matrix method, and the Routh-Hurwitz criterion is applied to determine the stability conditions. The findings reveal that the disease-free equilibrium is stable when R_0 < 1, while the endemic equilibrium is stable for R_0 > 1, with a forward bifurcation at R_0 = 1. Sensitivity analysis highlights vaccination coverage as the most influential factor in R_0. Numerical simulations using 2022 surveillance data from Ambon City, Indonesia, confirm these results, identifying critical transmission and vaccination thresholds. The study underscores the importance of vaccination strategies in controlling HBV spread, given the baseline R_0 value of approximately 0.926, which is just below the threshold for infection extinction. However, the slow extinction of the infection over hundreds of years suggests the need for sustained public health interventions.

papers.title_zh: 乙型肝炎标准 发病率 的 SEITR 模型的局部稳定性和阈值分析 传播
papers.source_body_en: This study analyses the SEITR model of hepatitis B virus (HBV) transmission with a standard incidence rate of βSI/N in a population of variable size. The model is reduced to an autonomous system expressed in population proportions. The disease-free and endemic equilibria and their Jacobian matrices are derived, and the basic reproduction number is obtained using the next generation matrix method. The Routh-Hurwitz criterion establishes that the disease-free equilibrium is locally asymptotically stable if R_0 1. For disease-induced mortality μ_2>0, shows that the endemic equilibrium is unique and is locally asymptotically stable. For μ_2=0, the endemic equilibrium exists for R_0>1 and is locally asymptotically stable, with a forward bifurcation occurring at R_0=1. Numerical simulations calibrated to 2022 surveillance data from Ambon City, Indonesia, confirm the analytical results: the critical transmission rate is β^*≈0.432, and the critical vaccination coverage is σ^*≈0.622. The baseline value of R_0≈0.926 lies just below the threshold, resulting in very slow extinction of the infection over hundreds of years. Normalised sensitivity analysis indicates that R_0 is most sensitive to vaccination coverage, followed by the transmission rate and the treatment rate.

papers.title: Development and Performance Evaluation of an Open-System Real-Time Quantitative PCR Assay for Decentralized Hepatitis B Viral Load Testing in Indonesia
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Indonesia remains one of the countries with the highest burdens of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) in Southeast Asia. Despite this substantial disease burden, a major gap in access to quantitative hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA testing potentially delays the diagnosis and treatment of CHB. This study aimed to develop and validate an open-system quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) assay, the INDIGEN HBV DNA qRT-PCR for detecting and quantifying HBV DNA viral load. Methods The assay was designed to target the S region of HBV and calibrated against the HBV World Health Organization (WHO) International Standard. Analytical performance was evaluated for linearity and limit of detection (LoD). A total of 122 HBsAg-positive samples from CHB patients were used to assess the clinical performance of our assay compared to the Xpert® HBV Viral Load (Xpert). Results The assay demonstrated excellent linearity across 1.0–9.0 log10 IU/mL (R2 = 0.9964) with a LoD of 14.8 IU/mL. Compared to Xpert, the developed assay showed 100% specificity and 99.05% sensitivity with strong correlation based on Deming regression analysis. Conclusions The INDIGEN HBV DNA qRT-PCR assay demonstrated robust evaluation performance comparable to the Xpert, supporting its implementation as a reliable open-system assay for decentralized HBV viral load testing in Indonesia.

source_records.abstract: Abstract Background Indonesia remains one of the countries with the highest burdens of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) in Southeast Asia. Despite this substantial disease burden, a major gap in access to quantitative hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA testing potentially delays the diagnosis and treatment of CHB. This study aimed to develop and validate an open-system quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) assay, the INDIGEN HBV DNA qRT-PCR for detecting and quantifying HBV DNA viral load. Methods The assay was designed to target the S region of HBV and calibrated against the HBV World Health Organization (WHO) International Standard. Analytical performance was evaluated for linearity and limit of detection (LoD). A total of 122 HBsAg-positive samples from CHB patients were used to assess the clinical performance of our assay compared to the Xpert® HBV Viral Load (Xpert). Compared to Xpert, the developed assay showed 100% specificity and 99.05% sensitivity with strong correlation based on Deming regression analysis. Conclusions The INDIGEN HBV DNA qRT-PCR assay demonstrated robust evaluation performance comparable to the Xpert, supporting its implementation as a reliable open-system assay for decentralized HBV viral load testing in Indonesia.

papers.title: Frequency of hepatitis B virus mutations associated with resistance to current and emerging drugs for functional cure in publicly available hepatitis B virus sequences
papers.abstract: Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains an immense global health challenge. Despite the availability of antiviral therapies, no curative treatment exists. Only a small proportion of individuals with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) achieve a functional cure. Resistance and vaccine escape mutations (EMs) may compromise current nucleos(t)ide analogs, vaccines and emerging therapies, leading to treatment failure. The present study aimed to assess the frequency of these HBV mutations in >17,000 publicly available patient-derived HBV sequences. Methods Fold-change (FC) data and resistance/escape-associated mutations were retrieved from literature searches. HBV sequences were retrieved from the NCBI Nucleotide and NCBI Virus databases. Human HBV isolates were genotyped using the HBVdb and Stanford HBVseq tools and GenBank data. Genotype-specific alignments were generated using MAFFT v7 and mutations were analyzed across reverse transcriptase (RT), core (C), surface (S) and X regions using in-house Python scripts. Results From 19,192 sequence identifiers retrieved, 17,012 genotyped sequences were analyzed. Genotypes C, B, D and A comprised approximately 85% of the dataset. RT-mutations, L180M + M204V and M204I, were frequent in certain genotypes like A, G, H, AG, and G, respectively. C-mutations, Y38F, I105T, and T109M, were identified in common genotypes. In the S-protein, G145R, E164G, and E164D mutations were the most common and these mutations are known to alter the effectiveness of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs). In general, S-mutations toward the studied mAbs occurred at low-to-moderate frequency. Some substitutions previously suggested to be vaccine escape-associated mutations were highly prevalent, however, these substitutions may be polymorphisms specific to certain genotypes requiring further validation. X-region mutations relevant for treatment based on antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) were uncommon overall. Conclusion HBV isolates with resistance and vaccine escape-associated mutations are present globally and might be genotype-dependent. Therefore, genotype and resistance assessment are crucial before initiating therapy for a favorable outcome in patients, especially when new drugs are introduced to achieve functional cure.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the frequency of hepatitis B virus (HBV) mutations associated with resistance to current and emerging drugs for functional cure in publicly available HBV sequences. The research highlights that resistance and vaccine escape mutations are prevalent in certain genotypes, such as A, G, H, and others, and may impact the effectiveness of antiviral therapies and monoclonal antibodies. The findings emphasize the importance of genotype-specific resistance and vaccine escape mutation assessments in guiding treatment decisions. However, the study does not report specific limitations of the design, and some substitutions may be polymorphisms rather than true escape mutations, requiring further validation. The results have implications for improving surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for HBV infection, particularly in the context of new therapeutic interventions.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 仍然是一个巨大的全球健康挑战。尽管有 抗病毒药物 疗法,但尚不存在治愈性的 治疗。只有一小部分患有 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 的个体达到了 功能性治愈。耐药性和 疫苗 逃逸 突变 (EM) 可能会损害当前的核苷(酸)类似物、疫苗 和新兴疗法,导致 治疗 失败。本研究旨在评估超过 17,000 个公开的患者来源的 HBV 序列中这些 HBV 突变 的频率。方法从文献检索中检索倍数变化(FC)数据和与抗性/逃逸相关的突变。HBV 序列取自 NCBI 核苷酸和 NCBI 病毒数据库。使用 HBVdb 和斯坦福大学 HBVseq 工具以及 GenBank 数据对人类 HBV 分离株进行基因分型。使用 MAFFT v7 生成基因型特异性比对,并使用内部 Python 脚本跨逆转录酶 (RT)、核心 (C)、表面 (S) 和 X 区域分析 突变。结果 从检索到的 19,192 个序列标识符中,分析了 17,012 个基因分型序列。基因型 C、B、D 和 A 约占数据集的 85%。RT-突变、L180M + M204V 和 M204I 分别在 A、G、H、AG 和 G 等某些基因型中常见。C-突变、Y38F、I105T 和 T109M 在常见基因型中被鉴定。在 S 蛋白中,G145R、E164G 和 E164D 突变 是最常见的,并且已知这些 突变 会改变单克隆抗体 (mAb) 的有效性。一般来说,针对所研究的单克隆抗体的 S-突变 发生频率为低至中等。先前认为与 疫苗 逃逸相关的 突变 的一些替换非常普遍,然而,这些替换可能是特定于某些基因型的多态性,需要进一步验证。总体而言,与基于反义寡核苷酸 (ASO) 的 治疗 相关的 X 区 突变 并不常见。结论 具有耐药性的 HBV 分离株和 疫苗 逃逸相关的 突变 在全球范围内存在,并且可能具有基因型依赖性。因此,在开始治疗以获得良好结果之前,基因型和耐药性评估至关重要,特别是在引入新药以实现 功能性治愈 时。

papers.title: Hepatitis B splicing-generated protein prevents tumor initiation but shapes a pro-tumor immune microenvironment in established HCC.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) plays a key role in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) through both direct oncogenic and indirect immune-mediated mechanisms. Expression of the main HBV spliced transcript, sp1RNA, gradually increases in chronic carriers prior to HCC onset. However, sp1RNA and related Hepatitis B Splicing-generated Protein (HBSP) contributions to hepatic carcinogenesis and tumor microenvironment have not been investigated. METHODS: HBV-related HCC tumors from 57 patients were classified according to HBV expression (RT)-qPCR and profiled using Nanostring immuno-oncology panel. The functional impact of HBSP expression was evaluated in transgenic male mice (TgHBSP) subjected to diethylnitrosamine (DEN)-induced HCC. A second model using orthotopic allografts of HBSP-expressing cells was developed. Liver tissues and immune infiltrates were characterized at 48 h, 6- and 10-month post-DEN injection. RESULTS: In HBV-related HCC patients, sp1RNA expression was associated with worse overall survival and reduced monocyte/macrophage gene signature within tumors. In TgHBSP mice, tumor incidence was reduced at both 6- and 10-month post-DEN administration, associated with sustained p38-MAPK activation at the initiation stage of cancer. Despite lower tumor incidence, tumors arising in TgHBSP mice were twice as large at endpoint. papers.title: Trajectories of serum hepatitis B surface antigen predict HBeAg clearance in treated children with chronic hepatitis B
papers.abstract: Background The association between the early dynamics of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and its subsequent clearance has been observed in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). However, its relationship with other clinical outcomes remains poorly understood. Objective This study aimed to investigate the longitudinal trajectories patterns of HBsAg and their associations with hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) clearance in pediatric patients with CHB undergoing antiviral treatment. Methods A large retrospective cohort study was conducted on 402 pediatric patients with HBeAg-positive CHB. Latent class trajectory models (LCTM) were applied to examine HBsAg trajectories within the first six months of initiating antiviral therapy. Cox proportional hazard models were used to assess the associations between HBsAg trajectories and HBeAg clearance. Results Among the 402 participants, the median age was 5 years, with 249 (61.94%) being male. During a median follow-up of 19.03 months, 216 participants (53.73%) achieved HBeAg clearance. LCTM revealed three distinct HBsAg trajectory patterns: ‘trajectory 1’ (sustained stability, n=43, 10.7%), ‘trajectory 2’ (slow decline, n=195, 48.5%), and ‘trajectory 3’ (rapid decline, n=164, 40.8%). Patients in trajectories 2 and 3 had significantly higher probabilities of HBeAg clearance compared to those in trajectory 1 (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] = 3.99, 95% CI, 2.20-7.22 for trajectory 2; aHR = 7.21, 95% CI, 3.65-14.24 for trajectory 3). Conclusions There is significant heterogeneity in the longitudinal changes of HBsAg levels among pediatric CHB patients with antiviral treatment. Approximately half of the patients exhibited a substantial HBsAg decline, which was associated with a higher likelihood of HBeAg clearance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the longitudinal trajectories patterns of HBsAg and their associations with hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) clearance in pediatric patients with chronic hepatitis B undergoing antiviral treatment. The association between the early dynamics of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and its subsequent clearance has been observed in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB).
analysis.study_design_and_population: A large retrospective cohort study was conducted on 402 pediatric patients with HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B. During a median follow-up of 19.03 months, 216 participants (53.73%) achieved HBeAg clearance.
analysis.methods: Latent class trajectory models (LCTM) were applied to examine HBsAg trajectories within the first six months of initiating antiviral therapy. Cox proportional hazard models were used to assess the associations between HBsAg trajectories and HBeAg clearance.
analysis.main_results: LCTM revealed three distinct HBsAg trajectory patterns: ‘trajectory 1’ (sustained stability, n=43, 10.7%), ‘trajectory 2’ (slow decline, n=195, 48.5%), and ‘trajectory 3’ (rapid decline, n=164, 40.8%). analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified significant heterogeneity in the longitudinal changes of HBsAg levels among pediatric CHB patients with antiviral treatment. Approximately half of the patients exhibited a substantial HBsAg decline, which was associated with a higher likelihood of HBeAg clearance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the development of more personalized treatment strategies for pediatric patients with chronic hepatitis B by identifying distinct HBsAg trajectory patterns linked to HBeAg clearance.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a retrospective design, which may introduce bias and limit the ability to establish causality. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and potential confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the longitudinal trajectories of HBsAg in pediatric patients with chronic hepatitis B undergoing antiviral treatment and their association with HBeAg clearance. Using latent class trajectory models, three distinct HBsAg patterns were identified: sustained stability, slow decline, and rapid decline. Patients in the slow and rapid decline trajectories had significantly higher probabilities of HBeAg clearance compared to those in the sustained stability trajectory. The study highlights the heterogeneity in HBsAg dynamics and suggests that these patterns may be useful for predicting treatment outcomes. However, the retrospective design limits the strength of the evidence, and the findings should be interpreted cautiously due to potential confounding factors.

Methods A large retrospective cohort study was conducted on 402 pediatric patients with HBeAg-positive CHB. Results Among the 402 participants, the median age was 5 years, with 249 (61.94%) being male. During a median follow-up of 19.03 months, 216 participants (53.73%) achieved HBeAg clearance. Approximately half of the patients exhibited a substantial HBsAg decline, which was associated with a higher likelihood of HBeAg clearance.

papers.title: Birth in the Neonatal Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) Vaccination Era and Hepatitis B Surface Antigen Seroclearance in People With HIV-1 and HBV Coinfection on Tenofovir-containing Antiretroviral Therapy.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The impact of long-term tenofovir-containing antiretroviral therapy (ART) on hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) seroclearance in people with HIV-1 (PWH) and HBV coinfection remains under-defined, particularly in HBV-hyperendemic regions with universal neonatal vaccination programs. METHODS: HBsAg-positive PWH receiving tenofovir-containing ART between 2011 and 2023 were followed until December 2025. Demographics, HBV serologic markers, plasma HBV DNA, and liver fibrosis stage were collected. Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify factors associated with HBsAg seroclearance. Clinical and hepatic outcomes were compared with seroclearance status. RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 9.4 years, 35 (8.4%) of 415 PWH achieved HBsAg seroclearance during a total of 3600 person-years of tenofovir-containing ART, corresponding to an incidence rate of 0.97 per 100 person-years. Among them, 37.1% (13/35) tested positive for anti-HBs at the time of seroclearance. In multivariable analysis, birth in universal neonatal HBV vaccination era (after July 1986) (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 13.56, 95% confidence interval [CI] 6.08-30.28, P < .001), baseline HBsAg ≤250 IU/mL (aHR 7.36, 95% CI 3.29-16.50, P < .001), and higher baseline ALT level (aHR 1.00 per 1-U/L increase, 95% CI 1.00-1.01, P < .001) were independently associated with HBsAg seroclearance. None of PWH who achieved HBsAg seroclearance developed seroreversion, cirrhosis, or hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), whereas 6.6% and 2.1% of PWH without seroclearance developed cirrhosis and HCC, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Despite long-term tenofovir-containing ART, HBsAg seroclearance was uncommon (0.97% annually) among PWH with HBV coinfection. Birth in the neonatal HBV vaccination era and lower baseline HBsAg level were 2 independent predictors of HBsAg seroclearance.

analysis_en.study_design_and_population: HBsAg-positive people with HIV-1 (PWH) receiving tenofovir-containing ART between 2011 and 2023 were followed until December 2025. The study included 415 PWH with HBV coinfection.

papers.title_zh: 新生儿 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 疫苗接种 时代的出生和 HIV-1 和 HBV 合并感染者接受含替诺福韦抗逆转录病毒治疗的乙型肝炎表面抗原血清清除。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: The impact of long-term tenofovir-containing antiretroviral therapy (ART) on hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) seroclearance in people with HIV-1 (PWH) and HBV coinfection remains under-defined, particularly in HBV-hyperendemic regions with universal neonatal vaccination programs. METHODS: HBsAg-positive PWH receiving tenofovir-containing ART between 2011 and 2023 were followed until December 2025. Demographics, HBV serologic markers, plasma HBV DNA, and liver fibrosis stage were collected. Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify factors associated with HBsAg seroclearance. Clinical and hepatic outcomes were compared with seroclearance status. RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 9.4 years, 35 (8.4%) of 415 PWH achieved HBsAg seroclearance during a total of 3600 person-years of tenofovir-containing ART, corresponding to an incidence rate of 0.97 per 100 person-years. Among them, 37.1% (13/35) tested positive for anti-HBs at the time of seroclearance. In multivariable analysis, birth in universal neonatal HBV vaccination era (after July 1986) (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 13.56, 95% confidence interval [CI] 6.08-30.28, P < .001), baseline HBsAg ≤250 IU/mL (aHR 7.36, 95% CI 3.29-16.50, P < .001), and higher baseline ALT level (aHR 1.00 per 1-U/L increase, 95% CI 1.00-1.01, P < .001) were independently associated with HBsAg seroclearance. None of PWH who achieved HBsAg seroclearance developed seroreversion, cirrhosis, or hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), whereas 6.6% and 2.1% of PWH without seroclearance developed cirrhosis and HCC, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Despite long-term tenofovir-containing ART, HBsAg seroclearance was uncommon (0.97% annually) among PWH with HBV coinfection. Birth in the neonatal HBV vaccination era and lower baseline HBsAg level were 2 independent predictors of HBsAg seroclearance.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查长期含替诺福韦的抗逆转录病毒治疗 (ART) 对 HIV-1 和 HBV 合并感染者乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 血清清除的影响,特别是在具有通用新生儿 疫苗接种 计划的 HBV 高流行地区。

analysis_zh.methods: 收集人口统计学、HBV 血清学标志物、血浆 HBV DNA 和肝纤维化阶段。Cox 比例风险模型用于识别与 HBsAg 血清清除相关的因素。
analysis_zh.main_results: 经过中位随访 9.4 年,415 名感染者中的 35 名(8.4%)在总共 3600 人年的含替诺福韦 ART 治疗期间实现了 HBsAg 血清清除,相当于每 100 人年 0.97 的 发病率 率。其中,37.1%(13/35)在血清清除时抗-HBs检测呈阳性。

papers.title: Translational Multiplexed Raman Pathological Imaging for Precise Diagnosis of HBV-Associated Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Multiplexed vibrational imaging holds great potential for tissue molecular analysis, yet fully standardized workflows suitable for routine clinical histopathology remain scarce. Herein, we report a clinically applicable methodology using monodisperse triple-bond Raman polymer nanoparticles (∼50 nm). This approach integrates one-step labeling and single-scan acquisition to achieve high-performance multiplexed Raman imaging of 5 protein markers in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tissues. Targeting hepatitis B virus (HBV)-associated HCC, our biomarker panel combines the viral protein HBx with 4 clinically used indicators: AFP, GS, GPC3, and CD34. We further reveal a clinically critical dissociation: several high-grade HBV-HCC specimens exhibit markedly elevated oncogenic markers with comparatively low HBx expression, consistent with antiviral therapy suppressing viral protein production without reversing tumor aggressiveness. Taking advantage of the ultranarrow, well-resolved signals generated by triple-bond tags within the biological silent region (1800-2800 cm-1), we achieve high-fidelity spatial mapping and quantitative analysis. Unlike conventional pathological methods relying on morphological observation, clinical manifestations, or single-marker detection, this technique simultaneously evaluates viral etiology, tumor progression, and metastatic potential, effectively reducing misclassification risk in patients with discordant viral and oncogenic profiles, and completes the entire assay within approximately 24 h. This study establishes a rapid and reliable histopathological platform that integrates pathogen identification and comprehensive cancer characterization, demonstrating substantial value for both cancer research and clinical diagnostics.

papers.title_zh: 转化多重拉曼病理成像用于 HBV 相关肝细胞癌的精确 诊断。
papers.source_body_en: Multiplexed vibrational imaging holds great potential for tissue molecular analysis, yet fully standardized workflows suitable for routine clinical histopathology remain scarce. papers.abstract_zh: 多重振动成像在组织分子分析方面具有巨大潜力,但适合常规临床组织病理学的完全标准化工作流程仍然很少。在此,我们报告了一种使用单分散三键拉曼聚合物纳米颗粒(∼50 nm)的临床适用方法。该方法集成了一步标记和单次扫描采集,可实现肝细胞癌 (HCC) 组织中 5 种蛋白质标记物的高性能多重拉曼成像。针对 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 相关 HCC,我们的生物标志物组合将病毒蛋白 HBx 与 4 个临床使用的指标相结合:AFP、GS、GPC3 和 CD34。我们进一步揭示了临床上关键的分离:几个高级别 HBV-HCC 标本表现出显着升高的致癌标志物,而 HBx 表达相对较低,这与 抗病毒药物 疗法抑制病毒蛋白产生而不逆转肿瘤侵袭性一致。利用生物沉默区域(1800-2800 cm-1)内三键标签产生的超窄、高分辨率信号,我们实现了高保真空间映射和定量分析。与依赖形态学观察、临床表现或单标志物检测的传统病理方法不同,该技术同时评估病毒病原学、肿瘤进展和转移潜力,有效降低病毒和致癌谱不一致患者的错误分类风险,并在约24小时内完成整个检测。这项研究建立了一个快速、可靠的组织病理学平台,整合了病原体识别和全面的癌症表征,展示了对癌症研究和临床诊断的巨大价值。

papers.title: Hepatitis B Virus Reactivation and Antiviral Prophylaxis Practices in Patients with Malignancies Receiving Chemotherapy: A Real-World Retrospective Study
papers.abstract: Background and Objectives: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation is a potentially life-threatening complication in patients receiving chemotherapy and immunosuppressive therapy. Real-world data regarding reactivation despite antiviral prophylaxis remain limited. Materials and Methods: We retrospectively evaluated patients with malignancies who received chemotherapy at Kocaeli University Faculty of Medicine Hospital between 2013 and 2017. Demographic characteristics, malignancy type, virological markers, laboratory findings, chemotherapy regimens, antiviral prophylaxis strategies, and HBV reactivation rates were analyzed. Results: A total of 294 patients were included in this study, of whom 18 (6.1%) experienced HBV reactivation. Reactivation was significantly more common in patients with hematologic malignancies (11.1%) than in patients with solid tumors (3.2%). Bone marrow transplantation was associated with a higher observed frequency of HBV reactivation. HBV reactivation was observed in a subset of patients receiving antiviral prophylaxis. Delayed initiation of antiviral treatment and irregular antiviral use were documented in some patients who developed HBV reactivation. Conclusions: Malignancies and intensive immunosuppressive therapies were associated with an increased risk of HBV reactivation despite prophylactic strategies. The results of our study also highlight the importance of HBV screening before chemotherapy, timely initiation of potent antiviral prophylaxis, and extended post-treatment monitoring in high-risk populations.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation is a potentially life-threatening complication in patients receiving chemotherapy and immunosuppressive therapy. The study aimed to evaluate the prevalence and risk factors of HBV reactivation in patients with malignancies undergoing chemotherapy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective study evaluated patients with malignancies who received chemotherapy at Kocaeli University Faculty of Medicine Hospital between 2013 and 2017. The study included a total of 294 patients, with a focus on those who experienced HBV reactivation.
analysis.methods: The study retrospectively analyzed demographic characteristics, malignancy type, virological markers, laboratory findings, chemotherapy regimens, antiviral prophylaxis strategies, and HBV reactivation rates. Data were collected from medical records and reviewed for relevant clinical and virological parameters.
analysis.main_results: A total of 294 patients were included in this study, of whom 18 (6.1%) experienced HBV reactivation. Reactivation was significantly more common in patients with hematologic malignancies (11.1%) than in patients with solid tumors (3.2%). Bone marrow transplantation was associated with a higher observed frequency of HBV reactivation. HBV reactivation was observed in a subset of patients receiving antiviral prophylaxis.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that malignancies and intensive immunosuppressive therapies were associated with an increased risk of HBV reactivation despite prophylactic strategies. This study highlights the need for targeted antiviral prophylaxis in high-risk populations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings emphasize the importance of HBV screening before chemotherapy, timely initiation of potent antiviral prophylaxis, and extended post-treatment monitoring in high-risk populations. These insights can inform clinical practices to reduce the risk of HBV reactivation in patients with malignancies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for missing data. However, the evidence is strong as it is based on real-world data from a well-defined population and includes specific rates and risk factors.

analysis.summary_en: This real-world retrospective study investigated the prevalence and risk factors of hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation in patients with malignancies undergoing chemotherapy. The study included 294 patients, of whom 18 (6.1%) experienced HBV reactivation. Reactivation was more common in hematologic malignancies (11.1%) than in solid tumors (3.2%), and bone marrow transplantation was associated with a higher frequency of reactivation. The authors concluded that malignancies and intensive immunosuppressive therapies increase the risk of HBV reactivation despite prophylactic strategies. The study highlights the importance of HBV screening, timely antiviral prophylaxis, and extended monitoring in high-risk populations. The evidence is strong due to its real-world data and clear reporting of rates and risk factors, though the retrospective design may limit its generalizability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 再激活是接受化疗和免疫抑制治疗的患者潜在的危及生命的并发症。该研究旨在评估接受化疗的恶性肿瘤患者的 患病率 和 HBV 再激活的危险因素。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性研究评估了 2013 年至 2017 年间在科贾埃利大学医学院医院接受化疗的恶性肿瘤患者。该研究总共包括 294 名患者,重点关注那些经历过 HBV 再激活的患者。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究回顾性分析了人口特征、恶性肿瘤类型、病毒学标志物、实验室检查结果、化疗方案、抗病毒药物 预防策略和 HBV 再激活率。从医疗记录中收集数据并审查相关临床和病毒学参数。

papers.title_zh: 接受化疗的恶性肿瘤患者的 乙型肝炎病毒 再激活和 抗病毒药物 预防实践:真实世界回顾性研究
papers.source_body_en: Background and Objectives: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation is a potentially life-threatening complication in patients receiving chemotherapy and immunosuppressive therapy. Real-world data regarding reactivation despite antiviral prophylaxis remain limited. Materials and Methods: We retrospectively evaluated patients with malignancies who received chemotherapy at Kocaeli University Faculty of Medicine Hospital between 2013 and 2017. Demographic characteristics, malignancy type, virological markers, laboratory findings, chemotherapy regimens, antiviral prophylaxis strategies, and HBV reactivation rates were analyzed. Results: A total of 294 patients were included in this study, of whom 18 (6.1%) experienced HBV reactivation. Reactivation was significantly more common in patients with hematologic malignancies (11.1%) than in patients with solid tumors (3.2%). Bone marrow transplantation was associated with a higher observed frequency of HBV reactivation. HBV reactivation was observed in a subset of patients receiving antiviral prophylaxis. Delayed initiation of antiviral treatment and irregular antiviral use were documented in some patients who developed HBV reactivation. Conclusions: Malignancies and intensive immunosuppressive therapies were associated with an increased risk of HBV reactivation despite prophylactic strategies. The results of our study also highlight the importance of HBV screening before chemotherapy, timely initiation of potent antiviral prophylaxis, and extended post-treatment monitoring in high-risk populations.

papers.title: Catastrophic Health Expenditure among Patients Managing Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection: Evidence from Federal University Teaching Hospital, Lafia, Nigeria
papers.abstract: This study examines catastrophic health expenditure (CHE) among patients managing chronic Hepatitis B virus (CHBV) infection in Federal University Teaching Hospital, Lafia, Nasarawa State, Nigeria.The study covers a 12-month recall period ending in 2026, drawing on hospital-based cross-sectional survey data from 108 adult CHBV patients attending the Gastroenterology Unit of the teaching hospital.The study adopts a prevalence-based Cost-of-Illness framework, benchmarking total annual patient expenditure against household income using the World Health Organization's catastrophic health expenditure thresholds (outof-pocket payments exceeding 10 percent of household income or 40 percent of capacity to pay), and tests bivariate associations between income, insurance enrolment, and treatment interruption using chi-square analysis.The findings show that CHBV management imposes an average annual economic burden of ₦738,049.26per patient, an amount that exceeds the WHO catastrophic threshold at every observed household income level, from below 30.75 percent of annual income among the highest earners to several times annual income among the lowest earners.Consistent with this, 83 percent of patients reported financial stress and 41 percent had delayed or discontinued treatment for financial reasons, with household income significantly associated with treatment interruption.while health insurance enrolment was low, reflecting the shallow depth of coverage even among the insured.Based on the findings, the study recommends that government and health insurance providers expand comprehensive, adequately resourced coverage for HBV diagnostics and antiviral medication, decentralise chronic HBV care to primary and secondary facilities, and prioritise catastrophic-expenditure monitoring as a routine indicator of financial risk protection in Nigeria's path toward universal health coverage.
papers.journal: Lafia Journal of Economics and Management Sciences

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study investigates the economic burden of chronic Hepatitis B virus (CHBV) infection and its impact on catastrophic health expenditure (CHE) among patients in Nigeria. The research addresses the growing concern of financial strain associated with managing CHBV, particularly in low-income settings.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a hospital-based cross-sectional survey conducted at Federal University Teaching Hospital, Lafia, Nasarawa State, Nigeria, over a 12-month recall period ending in 2026. It includes 108 adult patients with chronic HBV infection attending the Gastroenterology Unit.
analysis.methods: The study uses a prevalence-based Cost-of-Illness framework to assess the economic burden by comparing total annual patient expenditure with household income. analysis.main_results: The study found that the average annual economic burden of CHBV management is ₦738,049.26 per patient, exceeding the WHO catastrophic threshold at all observed income levels. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the high economic burden of CHBV management contributes to significant financial stress and treatment interruptions, highlighting the need for improved financial protection mechanisms. This study provides novel insights into the financial implications of CHBV in a Nigerian context.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of expanding health insurance coverage and improving access to antiviral medications for CHBV patients in Nigeria. They also emphasize the need for routine monitoring of catastrophic health expenditure as part of broader efforts toward universal health coverage.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a single hospital setting and relies on self-reported data, which may introduce bias. Despite these limitations, the evidence is moderate in strength due to the use of established WHO thresholds and statistical analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the economic burden of chronic Hepatitis B virus (CHBV) infection in Nigeria, focusing on catastrophic health expenditure (CHE) among 108 adult patients. Using a cross-sectional survey and the WHO's CHE thresholds, the research finds that CHBV management imposes an average annual cost of ₦738,049.26 per patient, exceeding the threshold at all income levels. Financial stress and treatment interruptions are prevalent, with 83% of patients reporting financial strain and 41% discontinuing treatment due to cost. The study highlights the need for expanded health insurance coverage and improved financial protection mechanisms for CHBV patients. While the findings are based on a single hospital setting and self-reported data, they provide valuable insights into the financial implications of CHBV in Nigeria, supporting the push for universal health coverage.

elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study is a hospital-based cross-sectional survey conducted at Federal University Teaching Hospital, Lafia, Nasarawa State, Nigeria, over a 12-month recall period ending in 2026. It includes 108 adult patients with chronic HBV infection attending the Gastroenterology Unit.
elements_en.methods: The study uses a prevalence-based Cost-of-Illness framework to assess the economic burden by comparing total annual patient expenditure with household income. It applies the World Health Organization's catastrophic health expenditure thresholds and uses chi-square analysis to test associations between income, insurance enrolment, and treatment interruption.
elements_en.main_results: The study found that the average annual economic burden of CHBV management is ₦738,049.26 per patient, exceeding the WHO catastrophic threshold at all observed income levels. Additionally, 83 percent of patients reported financial stress, and 41 percent delayed or discontinued treatment due to financial reasons.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the high economic burden of CHBV management contributes to significant financial stress and treatment interruptions, highlighting the need for improved financial protection mechanisms. This study provides novel insights into the financial implications of CHBV in a Nigerian context.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of expanding health insurance coverage and improving access to antiviral medications for CHBV patients in Nigeria. They also emphasize the need for routine monitoring of catastrophic health expenditure as part of broader efforts toward universal health coverage.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a single hospital setting and relies on self-reported data, which may introduce bias. Despite these limitations, the evidence is moderate in strength due to the use of established WHO thresholds and statistical analysis.

papers.title_zh: 治疗 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒感染的患者的灾难性健康支出:来自尼日利亚拉菲亚联邦大学教学医院的证据
papers.source_body_en: This study examines catastrophic health expenditure (CHE) among patients managing chronic Hepatitis B virus (CHBV) infection in Federal University Teaching Hospital, Lafia, Nasarawa State, Nigeria.The study covers a 12-month recall period ending in 2026, drawing on hospital-based cross-sectional survey data from 108 adult CHBV patients attending the Gastroenterology Unit of the teaching hospital.The study adopts a prevalence-based Cost-of-Illness framework, benchmarking total annual patient expenditure against household income using the World Health Organization's catastrophic health expenditure thresholds (outof-pocket payments exceeding 10 percent of household income or 40 percent of capacity to pay), and tests bivariate associations between income, insurance enrolment, and treatment interruption using chi-square analysis.The findings show that CHBV management imposes an average annual economic burden of ₦738,049.26per patient, an amount that exceeds the WHO catastrophic threshold at every observed household income level, from below 30.75 percent of annual income among the highest earners to several times annual income among the lowest earners.Consistent with this, 83 percent of patients reported financial stress and 41 percent had delayed or discontinued treatment for financial reasons, with household income significantly associated with treatment interruption.while health insurance enrolment was low, reflecting the shallow depth of coverage even among the insured.Based on the findings, the study recommends that government and health insurance providers expand comprehensive, adequately resourced coverage for HBV diagnostics and antiviral medication, decentralise chronic HBV care to primary and secondary facilities, and prioritise catastrophic-expenditure monitoring as a routine indicator of financial risk protection in Nigeria's path toward universal health coverage.

papers.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver and antiviral response in chronic hepatitis B: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) frequently coexists with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). However, its association with antiviral treatment responses and long-term clinical outcomes in patients with CHB remains unclear. AIM To systematically evaluate the impact of MAFLD on antiviral treatment responses and long-term clinical outcomes in patients with CHB. METHODS This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. PubMed, the Cochrane Library, EMBASE, and Web of Science were searched for studies published up to November 30, 2025. Meta-analyses were performed to assess associations between MAFLD and antiviral treatment responses or clinical outcomes. Subgroup analyses were conducted according to antiviral regimen and MAFLD diagnostic approach, and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate robustness. RESULTS Thirty-two studies were included, of which 20 evaluated antiviral treatment efficacy and 13 assessed clinical outcomes in patients with CHB and concomitant MAFLD (one study reported both treatment responses and clinical outcomes). MAFLD was associated with a higher rate of hepatitis B surface antigen seroclearance at 48 weeks [odds ratio (OR) = 1.41, 95%CI: 1.28-1.55], although this association was attenuated at 96 weeks (OR = 1.44, 95%CI: 0.96-2.16). No significant association was observed between MAFLD and hepatitis B e antigen seroclearance at any time-point. MAFLD was consistently associated with lower rates of alanine aminotransferase normalization and hepatitis B virus DNA clearance throughout the treatment duration. MAFLD was associated with a significantly increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) despite antiviral therapy (OR = 1.50, 95%CI: 1.01-2.24). Subgroup analyses according to the antiviral regimen revealed distinct patterns, partly explaining the heterogeneity in the overall analyses. Subgroup analyses suggested that the antiviral regimen and MAFLD diagnostic approach partly explained the heterogeneity, particularly for hepatitis B virus DNA clearance and HCC. CONCLUSION MAFLD was associated with lower virological and biochemical response rates, higher odds of hepatitis B surface antigen seroclearance at week 48, particularly among patients receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy, and higher odds of HCC in patients with CHB, but not with hepatitis B e antigen seroclearance. These findings support metabolic risk assessment in CHB management and highlight the need for standardized MAFLD/metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease definitions.
