news.content: Advanced Search Home News Releases Multimedia Meetings Login Register News Release 19-Nov-2026 A simplified GADA model improves detection of HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma in a study of 23,098 patients The four-variable model, tailored to patients with HBV-related chronic liver disease, retained strong performance across ten external validation centers Peer-Reviewed Publication Chinese Medical Journals Publishing House Co., Ltd. Facebook X LinkedIn WeChat Bluesky Message WhatsApp Email image: (A) Modeling cohort. (B) Internal validation cohort. (C) External validation cohort. AUC, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve; AFP, alpha-fetoprotein; AFP-L3%, lens culinaris agglutinin-reactive AFP; DCP, des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin. Credit: Chinese Medical Journal. view more Credit: Prof. Fengmin Lu from Peking University Health Science Center, China; Dr. Lijuan Liu from Fujian Medical University, China; and Dr. Mei Zhang from Medical College of Shihezi University, China Image source link: https://www.ovid.com/jnls/cmj/fulltext/10.1097/cm9.0000000000004244~development-and-validation-of-gada-model-for-diagnosing BEIJING, CHINA—Researchers from Peking University and collaborating hospitals across China have developed and validated GADA, a simplified model for detecting hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Derived from the established GALAD framework, GADA combines gender, age, des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin (DCP; also known as PIVKA-II), and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP). In more than 23,000 participants, it showed strong diagnostic performance for both overall and early-stage HCC. The study is forthcoming in the Chinese Medical Journal. Why a China-specific model was needed Chronic HBV infection causes more than 40% of HCC cases worldwide and is associated with approximately 86% of HCC cases in China. The epidemiology of HCC in China therefore differs substantially from that in many Western cohorts, where hepatitis C, alcohol-related liver disease, and metabolic liver disease contribute more prominently. The GALAD model integrates gender, age, AFP, AFP-L3%, and DCP and has performed well in several Western populations. However, its performance required reassessment in HBV-associated chronic liver disease. AFP-L3% also adds measurement complexity, cost, and sample-volume requirements, and is not readily available in all clinical settings. The study, led by Professor Fengmin Lu was published online on August 17, 2026, in the Chinese Medical Journal. How GADA was developed and validated The investigators analyzed 2,190 adults with HBV-related chronic liver disease at Mengchao Hepatobiliary Hospital of Fujian Medical University. Participants were randomly assigned to a modeling cohort (70%; n = 1,533) and an internal validation cohort (30%; n = 657). A separate prospective external validation cohort enrolled 20,908 participants at ten hospitals across China, including 905 patients with newly diagnosed HCC and 20,003 patients without HCC (17,802 with chronic hepatitis B and 2,201 with HBV-related cirrhosis). Altogether, 23,098 participants were included. AFP and DCP provided complementary diagnostic information, whereas AFP-L3% contributed limited additional utility in this HBV-focused population. The researchers therefore developed the four-variable GADA score: Z = –11.111 + 1.122 x gender + 0.073 x age + 2.660 x log10(DCP) + 0.578 x log10(AFP) Gender is coded as 1 for male and 0 for female. Strong and reproducible diagnostic performance Cohort AUC (95% CI) Sensitivity Specificity Modeling 0.940 (0.927–0.952) 82.57% 91.53% Internal validation 0.935 (0.914–0.953) 82.04% 92.65% External validation 0.919 (0.916–0.923) 86.00% 81.88% In the modeling cohort, GADA outperformed the original GALAD model (AUC 0.940 vs. 0.907). In the external validation cohort, it also outperformed AFP alone (AUC 0.748) and DCP alone (AUC 0.841). Center-specific AUCs ranged from 0.895 to 0.977, supporting robustness across geographically and clinically diverse settings. For early-stage HCC meeting the Milan criteria, GADA achieved AUCs of 0.858 in the modeling cohort, 0.868 in the internal validation cohort, and 0.903 in the external validation cohort. In the external cohort, sensitivity was 88.16% and specificity was 74.50%. Clinical significance GADA was designed for the setting in which the clinical need is greatest in China: distinguishing HBV-related HCC from chronic hepatitis B and HBV-related cirrhosis. By removing AFP-L3% while preserving strong diagnostic accuracy, the model may reduce testing complexity and improve accessibility, including in hospitals with more limited laboratory resources. The model should be viewed as an adjunct to established HCC surveillance and diagnostic pathways, not as a replacement for imaging or clinical assessment. Prospective evaluation in routine surveillance populations and calibration of operational thresholds across laboratories will be important before broad implementation. Reference DOI: 10.1097/CM9.0000000000004244 About Professor Fengmin Lu from Peking University Health Science Center, China Prof. Fengmin Lu is Director of the Peking University Infectious Disease Research Center, Professor in the Department of Microbiology at Peking University Health Science Center, and a jointly appointed Professor at the Center for Infectious Diseases, Peking University Third Hospital. His research focuses on the molecular mechanisms of HBV-related hepatocarcinogenesis, occult HBV infection, and biomarkers. He led the development and multicenter validation of the GADA model. He has led more than 20 national research projects, received two Second-Class National Science and Technology Progress Awards, published nearly 200 papers, and holds 25 authorized invention patents, seven of which have been commercialized. Funding This work was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (No. 82272433) and the Fujian Provincial Key Laboratory of Hepatic Drug Research (No. 2022-YF-0050). news.title_zh: 在一项针对 23,098 名患者的研究中,简化的 GADA 模型改善了 HBV 相关肝细胞癌的检测 - EurekAlert!
news.source_body_en: A study published on November 19, 2026, by EurekAlert! highlights the development of a simplified GADA model for detecting HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in China. The model, derived from the established GALAD framework, combines gender, age, des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin (DCP), and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) to improve diagnostic accuracy. It was tested on 23,098 participants across three cohorts: modeling (1,533), internal validation (657), and external validation (20,908). The GADA model showed strong performance, with AUCs ranging from 0.858 to 0.977 and sensitivity of 86.00% and specificity of 81.88% in the external validation. The model is designed to distinguish HBV-related HCC from chronic hepatitis B and HBV-related cirrhosis, reducing testing complexity and improving accessibility in resource-limited settings. However, it is recommended as an adjunct to existing diagnostic methods rather than a replacement. The study is forthcoming in the Chinese Medical Journal and emphasizes the need for further evaluation and calibration before widespread use.
news.content_zh: EurekAlert! 于 2026 年 11 月 19 日发表的一项研究!强调了中国用于检测 HBV 相关肝细胞癌 (HCC) 的简化 GADA 模型的开发。该模型源自已建立的 GALAD 框架,结合了性别、年龄、脱γ-羧基凝血酶原 (DCP) 和甲胎蛋白 (AFP),以提高诊断准确性。它在三个 队列研究 的 23,098 名参与者身上进行了测试:建模 (1,533)、内部验证 (657) 和外部验证 (20,908)。GADA模型在外部验证中表现出强大的性能,AUC范围为0.858至0.977,敏感性为86.00%,特异性为81.88%。该模型旨在区分 HBV 相关 HCC、慢性乙型肝炎 和 HBV 相关肝硬化,降低检测复杂性并提高资源有限环境中的可及性。然而,建议将其作为现有诊断方法的辅助手段,而不是替代方法。该研究即将发表在《中华医学杂志》上,并强调在广泛使用之前需要进一步评估和校准。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 20, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Area Disadvantage Outweighs Personal Socioeconomic Status in Chronic Hepatitis B Liver Fibrosis by November 18, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Area Disadvantage Outweighs Personal Socioeconomic Status in Chronic Hepatitis B Liver Fibrosis Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram In a nationwide multicentre investigation examining adults living with chronic hepatitis B across twenty-four clinical centres in Türkiye, the severity of histologically staged liver fibrosis was found to correlate far more consistently with area-level socioeconomic disadvantage in a patient’s current place of residence than with individual socioeconomic measures or birthplace background. Chronic viral hepatitis remains a substantial driver of progressive hepatic injury, yet the extent to which broader geographical deprivation shapes the clinical severity at which liver disease is diagnosed has remained insufficiently characterised. By evaluating biopsy-confirmed liver tissue alongside detailed socioeconomic data, investigators identified a pronounced spatial gradient in disease stage that persisted even after rigorous statistical adjustments for demographic profiles, personal income, and healthcare engagement markers. These findings suggest that broader living environments and structural barriers exert a substantial influence on disease detection and progression, underscoring the vital importance of place-based social epidemiological factors in explaining disparities across the chronic hepatitis B continuum of care. Chronic hepatitis B continues to represent a formidable worldwide public health priority, serving as a primary underlying cause of irreversible liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Global epidemiological assessments from 2022 estimated that 254 million people were living with chronic hepatitis B virus infection, resulting in approximately 1.2 million incident infections and 1.1 million deaths within that year alone. Within this challenging international context, Türkiye represents a clinically relevant setting, where national seroprevalence studies indicate that hepatitis B surface antigen positivity spans between 4.0% and 4.6% of the general population, accompanied by notable geographic and demographic variation. Although clinical protocols emphasise regular surveillance to avert end-stage hepatic sequelae, socioeconomic inequalities can severely disrupt the trajectory between diagnosis and clinical management. Fibrosis severity at presentation effectively functions as an objective biological correlate of delayed care, highlighting that patients who face pronounced social vulnerabilities frequently enter specialized hospital infrastructure only after significant and potentially irreversible structural liver damage has already become established. To investigate these dynamics systematically, the researchers screened 1,259 adult candidates aged 18 years or older who had undergone diagnostic liver biopsy during routine clinical care between 1 January 2019 and 31 December 2024 across 24 participating centres throughout Türkiye. All included individuals presented with chronic infection confirmed by the persistence of hepatitis B surface antigen for at least six months. From this initial group, 147 patients declined participation in structured face-to-face interviews, 134 lacked definitive histopathological biopsy reports, and 22 were excluded because of comorbid conditions known to independently exacerbate liver fibrosis, such as coinfection with hepatitis C virus, hepatitis D virus, or human immunodeficiency virus, chronic alcohol consumption, active malignancy, or hereditary conditions such as Wilson disease or haemochromatosis. The resulting analytic cohort comprised 956 adults with complete biopsy and socioeconomic assessments. Within this cohort, 53.7% were male, the median age was 46.0 years, the median age at diagnosis was 27.0 years, and the median age at biopsy was 41.0 years. Discover more Check Symptoms Study Biology Find Treatments socioeconomic status Socioeconomic Status Assessment of area-level socioeconomic context was grounded in the official İl SEGE-2025 framework, operationalised as the provincial socioeconomic development index across all eighty-one administrative provinces of Türkiye. This framework synthesises 52 objective indicators across eight core dimensions, including demography, employment, education, healthcare infrastructure, innovation, fiscal structure, territorial accessibility, and overall living quality, classifying provinces into six development tiers where level 1 denotes the highest socioeconomic development and level 6 denotes the most severe deprivation. Concurrently, comprehensive personal data were gathered through post-biopsy face-to-face interviews, capturing formal educational attainment, employment status, household occupancy, monthly income, receipt of governmental social assistance, health insurance coverage, and residential stability. In addition, healthcare accessibility was measured directly through reported travel times to secondary or tertiary centres equipped for chronic viral hepatitis management, alongside documented durations of clinical follow-up prior to tissue sampling, providing a robust empirical framework capable of isolating structural geographic disparities from private economic circumstances. Histological evaluation served as the primary clinical outcome, with hepatic fibrosis graded according to the standardized Ishak scoring system spanning from stage 0 through stage 6. Within the full analytic cohort of 956 patients, mild fibrosis corresponding to Ishak stages 0 through 2 was identified in 73.1% of participants, moderate fibrosis covering stages 3 and 4 was documented in 21.7%, and advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis encompassing stages 5 and 6 was found in 5.2%. In primary multivariable ordinal logistic regression across the entire range of fibrosis stages, a one-level decline in provincial socioeconomic development was independently associated with an adjusted odds ratio of 1.97 for reaching higher fibrosis stages (95% confidence interval: 1.82 to 2.15; P < 0.001). Concurrently, older age at biopsy (adjusted odds ratio: 1.12 per 10-year increment; P = 0.019), longer travel time to a specialized care centre (adjusted odds ratio: 1.53 per category increase; P < 0.001), and longer duration of residence in the current locality (adjusted odds ratio: 1.21 per 5-year increase; P = 0.023) independently predicted greater fibrosis severity. To rigorously interrogate potential confounding in comparisons between regions of extreme development, the research team implemented propensity score matching and overlap weighting focused strictly on participants living in tier 1 and tier 6 provinces. In the 1:1 nearest-neighbour matched cohort balanced for age at biopsy and exact sex across 127 paired individuals, participants residing in the most disadvantaged socioeconomic environment exhibited markedly higher fibrosis burdens. Specifically, median Ishak fibrosis scores were 1.0 in tier 1 compared with 3.0 in tier 6, and the prevalence of significant fibrosis, defined as Ishak stage 3 or higher, reached 66.1% in tier 6 compared with merely 7.1% in tier 1. Stratified conditional logistic regression revealed that residence in tier 6 conferred an odds ratio of 26.00 for significant liver fibrosis relative to tier 1 (95% confidence interval: 8.21 to 82.37; P < 0.001). Overlap weighting demonstrated matching stability, producing a weighted significant fibrosis prevalence of 63.6% in tier 6 versus 6.6% in tier 1, corresponding to a weighted odds ratio of 24.75 (95% confidence interval: 8.96 to 68.36; P < 0.001). Sequential sensitivity regression models further reinforced the robustness of these observed associations when introducing additional layers of statistical control. Among participants residing in the extreme provincial tiers, the unadjusted contrast in significant fibrosis yielded an odds ratio of 28.83 after controlling for age and sex, which remained largely unchanged at an odds ratio of 28.17 following the inclusion of individual-level socioeconomic indicators such as household income and schooling. When access-related factors, including travel duration and pre-biopsy surveillance continuity, were incorporated into the model, the odds ratio remained pronounced at 18.98 (95% confidence interval: 8.43 to 42.72; P < 0.001). Crucially, formal interaction tests demonstrated no evidence of effect modification across age (P = 0.425), sex (P = 0.110), or equivalised household income (P = 0.695). Moreover, the relative index of inequality calculated across the ridit-ranked personal income distribution was not statistically associated with significant fibrosis (odds ratio: 0.63, 95% confidence interval: 0.21 to 1.87; P = 0.401), showing that personal financial resources alone did not explain the substantial regional disparity. Model-derived predicted probabilities clearly illustrated the clinical gap separating populations situated at opposite ends of the geographic socioeconomic spectrum. For a 40-year-old male with an average equivalised household income, the model-estimated probability of presenting with significant liver fibrosis was 69.3% (95% confidence interval: 59.8% to 77.4%) in tier 6 provinces, compared with only 7.4% (95% confidence interval: 3.3% to 15.6%) in tier 1 environments. Similarly, when assessing individuals earning a standardized household income of 30,000 Turkish liras monthly at the median cohort age of 41 years, the predicted probability of significant fibrosis stood at 70.3% (95% confidence interval: 61.0% to 78.2%) in the most disadvantaged provinces, while remaining at 8.7% (95% confidence interval: 4.4% to 16.4%) in the most developed provinces. Across both geographical groupings, estimated risks rose steadily with advancing age, yet the trajectories across income brackets ran strictly parallel, demonstrating that elevated income provided little apparent mitigation against the adverse structural conditions present in underdeveloped provinces. Further insight into the dominance of contemporary living conditions over historical origin emerged from reciprocal subgroup evaluations categorising patients by birthplace and migration destination. Among 370 individuals born in the most disadvantaged tier 6 provinces, the prevalence of significant liver fibrosis varied dramatically according to their current place of residence (chi-square P < 0.001). Those who remained in tier 6 exhibited the highest prevalence of significant fibrosis at 72.1%, whereas individuals who had migrated to moderately developed tier 4 or tier 5 provinces showed lower rates of 31.2% and 23.1%, respectively, and those residing in highly developed tier 1, 2, or 3 settings had rates of 8.3%, 7.0%, and 7.9%. Conversely, among participants born in affluent tier 1 provinces, significant fibrosis occurred in only 3.7% of those who remained in tier 1, compared with 55.0% among those who relocated to tier 6. This reciprocal symmetry firmly indicates that cumulative liver injury correlates with current residential conditions rather than early-life regional origin. To synthesize these interconnected dynamics, the researchers developed a conceptual directed acyclic graph illustrating how regional socioeconomic deprivation exerts downstream pressures through extended travel burdens and fragmented clinical surveillance, culminating in advanced histological fibrosis at biopsy. Nevertheless, the authors emphasised important methodological caveats, noting that the cohort was observational, hospital-based, and reliant on routine clinical biopsies rather than a population-wide screening protocol. Central pathology re-review was unavailable, and interviews were conducted after biopsy with a median interval of 60 months, meaning personal variables captured circumstances at interview. Detailed viral loads, antiviral treatment regimens, and metabolic comorbidities were also unmeasured in these models. Despite these limitations, the nationwide evidence demonstrates that structural geographic disadvantage, rather than personal socioeconomic status alone, remains intimately tied to advanced liver fibrosis in chronic hepatitis B, highlighting the imperative for targeted public health investments that expand specialist clinical access and follow-up continuity in underserved regions. Chronic viral hepatitis remains a substantial driver of progressive hepatic injury, yet the extent to which broader geographical deprivation shapes the clinical severity at which liver disease is diagnosed has remained insufficiently characterised. By evaluating biopsy-confirmed liver tissue alongside detailed socioeconomic data, investigators identified a pronounced spatial gradient in disease stage that persisted even after rigorous statistical adjustments for demographic profiles, personal income, and healthcare engagement markers. These findings suggest that broader living environments and structural barriers exert a substantial influence on disease detection and progression, underscoring the vital importance of place-based social epidemiological factors in explaining disparities across the chronic hepatitis B continuum of care. Chronic hepatitis B continues to represent a formidable worldwide public health priority, serving as a primary underlying cause of irreversible liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Global epidemiological assessments from 2022 estimated that 254 million people were living with chronic hepatitis B virus infection, resulting in approximately 1.2 million incident infections and 1.1 million deaths within that year alone. Within this challenging international context, Türkiye represents a clinically relevant setting, where national seroprevalence studies indicate that hepatitis B surface antigen positivity spans between 4.0% and 4.6% of the general population, accompanied by notable geographic and demographic variation. Although clinical protocols emphasise regular surveillance to avert end-stage hepatic sequelae, socioeconomic inequalities can severely disrupt the trajectory between diagnosis and clinical management. Fibrosis severity at presentation effectively functions as an objective biological correlate of delayed care, highlighting that patients who face pronounced social vulnerabilities frequently enter specialized hospital infrastructure only after significant and potentially irreversible structural liver damage has already become established. To investigate these dynamics systematically, the researchers screened 1,259 adult candidates aged 18 years or older who had undergone diagnostic liver biopsy during routine clinical care between 1 January 2019 and 31 December 2024 across 24 participating centres throughout Türkiye. All included individuals presented with chronic infection confirmed by the persistence of hepatitis B surface antigen for at least six months. From this initial group, 147 patients declined participation in structured face-to-face interviews, 134 lacked definitive histopathological biopsy reports, and 22 were excluded because of comorbid conditions known to independently exacerbate liver fibrosis, such as coinfection with hepatitis C virus, hepatitis D virus, or human immunodeficiency virus, chronic alcohol consumption, active malignancy, or hereditary conditions such as Wilson disease or haemochromatosis. The resulting analytic cohort comprised 956 adults with complete biopsy and socioeconomic assessments. Within this cohort, 53.7% were male, the median age was 46.0 years, the median age at diagnosis was 27.0 years, and the median age at biopsy was 41.0 years. Discover more Check Symptoms Study Biology Find Treatments socioeconomic status Socioeconomic Status Assessment of area-level socioeconomic context was grounded in the official İl SEGE-2025 framework, operationalised as the provincial socioeconomic development index across all eighty-one administrative provinces of Türkiye. This framework synthesises 52 objective indicators across eight core dimensions, including demography, employment, education, healthcare infrastructure, innovation, fiscal structure, territorial accessibility, and overall living quality, classifying provinces into six development tiers where level 1 denotes the highest socioeconomic development and level 6 denotes the most severe deprivation. Concurrently, comprehensive personal data were gathered through post-biopsy face-to-face interviews, capturing formal educational attainment, employment status, household occupancy, monthly income, receipt of governmental social assistance, health insurance coverage, and residential stability. In addition, healthcare accessibility was measured directly through reported travel times to secondary or tertiary centres equipped for chronic viral hepatitis management, alongside documented durations of clinical follow-up prior to tissue sampling, providing a robust empirical framework capable of isolating structural geographic disparities from private economic circumstances. Histological evaluation served as the primary clinical outcome, with hepatic fibrosis graded according to the standardized Ishak scoring system spanning from stage 0 through stage 6. Within the full analytic cohort of 956 patients, mild fibrosis corresponding to Ishak stages 0 through 2 was identified in 73.1% of participants, moderate fibrosis covering stages 3 and 4 was documented in 21.7%, and advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis encompassing stages 5 and 6 was found in 5.2%. In primary multivariable ordinal logistic regression across the entire range of fibrosis stages, a one-level decline in provincial socioeconomic development was independently associated with an adjusted odds ratio of 1.97 for reaching higher fibrosis stages (95% confidence interval: 1.82 to 2.15; P < 0.001). Concurrently, older age at biopsy (adjusted odds ratio: 1.12 per 10-year increment; P = 0.019), longer travel time to a specialized care centre (adjusted odds ratio: 1.53 per category increase; P < 0.001), and longer duration of residence in the current locality (adjusted odds ratio: 1.21 per 5-year increase; P = 0.023) independently predicted greater fibrosis severity. To rigorously interrogate potential confounding in comparisons between regions of extreme development, the research team implemented propensity score matching and overlap weighting focused strictly on participants living in tier 1 and tier 6 provinces. In the 1:1 nearest-neighbour matched cohort balanced for age at biopsy and exact sex across 127 paired individuals, participants residing in the most disadvantaged socioeconomic environment exhibited markedly higher fibrosis burdens. Specifically, median Ishak fibrosis scores were 1.0 in tier 1 compared with 3.0 in tier 6, and the prevalence of significant fibrosis, defined as Ishak stage 3 or higher, reached 66.1% in tier 6 compared with merely 7.1% in tier 1. Stratified conditional logistic regression revealed that residence in tier 6 conferred an odds ratio of 26.00 for significant liver fibrosis relative to tier 1 (95% confidence interval: 8.21 to 82.37; P < 0.001). Overlap weighting demonstrated matching stability, producing a weighted significant fibrosis prevalence of 63.6% in tier 6 versus 6.6% in tier 1, corresponding to a weighted odds ratio of 24.75 (95% confidence interval: 8.96 to 68.36; P < 0.001). Sequential sensitivity regression models further reinforced the robustness of these observed associations when introducing additional layers of statistical control. Among participants residing in the extreme provincial tiers, the unadjusted contrast in significant fibrosis yielded an odds ratio of 28.83 after controlling for age and sex, which remained largely unchanged at an odds ratio of 28.17 following the inclusion of individual-level socioeconomic indicators such as household income and schooling. When access-related factors, including travel duration and pre-biopsy surveillance continuity, were incorporated into the model, the odds ratio remained pronounced at 18.98 (95% confidence interval: 8.43 to 42.72; P < 0.001). Crucially, formal interaction tests demonstrated no evidence of effect modification across age (P = 0.425), sex (P = 0.110), or equivalised household income (P = 0.695). Moreover, the relative index of inequality calculated across the ridit-ranked personal income distribution was not statistically associated with significant fibrosis (odds ratio: 0.63, 95% confidence interval: 0.21 to 1.87; P = 0.401), showing that personal financial resources alone did not explain the substantial regional disparity. Model-derived predicted probabilities clearly illustrated the clinical gap separating populations situated at opposite ends of the geographic socioeconomic spectrum. For a 40-year-old male with an average equivalised household income, the model-estimated probability of presenting with significant liver fibrosis was 69.3% (95% confidence interval: 59.8% to 77.4%) in tier 6 provinces, compared with only 7.4% (95% confidence interval: 3.3% to 15.6%) in tier 1 environments. Similarly, when assessing individuals earning a standardized household income of 30,000 Turkish liras monthly at the median cohort age of 41 years, the predicted probability of significant fibrosis stood at 70.3% (95% confidence interval: 61.0% to 78.2%) in the most disadvantaged provinces, while remaining at 8.7% (95% confidence interval: 4.4% to 16.4%) in the most developed provinces. Across both geographical groupings, estimated risks rose steadily with advancing age, yet the trajectories across income brackets ran strictly parallel, demonstrating that elevated income provided little apparent mitigation against the adverse structural conditions present in underdeveloped provinces. Further insight into the dominance of contemporary living conditions over historical origin emerged from reciprocal subgroup evaluations categorising patients by birthplace and migration destination. Among 370 individuals born in the most disadvantaged tier 6 provinces, the prevalence of significant liver fibrosis varied dramatically according to their current place of residence (chi-square P < 0.001). Those who remained in tier 6 exhibited the highest prevalence of significant fibrosis at 72.1%, whereas individuals who had migrated to moderately developed tier 4 or tier 5 provinces showed lower rates of 31.2% and 23.1%, respectively, and those residing in highly developed tier 1, 2, or 3 settings had rates of 8.3%, 7.0%, and 7.9%. Conversely, among participants born in affluent tier 1 provinces, significant fibrosis occurred in only 3.7% of those who remained in tier 1, compared with 55.0% among those who relocated to tier 6. This reciprocal symmetry firmly indicates that cumulative liver injury correlates with current residential conditions rather than early-life regional origin. To synthesize these interconnected dynamics, the researchers developed a conceptual directed acyclic graph illustrating how regional socioeconomic deprivation exerts downstream pressures through extended travel burdens and fragmented clinical surveillance, culminating in advanced histological fibrosis at biopsy. Nevertheless, the authors emphasised important methodological caveats, noting that the cohort was observational, hospital-based, and reliant on routine clinical biopsies rather than a population-wide screening protocol. Central pathology re-review was unavailable, and interviews were conducted after biopsy with a median interval of 60 months, meaning personal variables captured circumstances at interview. Detailed viral loads, antiviral treatment regimens, and metabolic comorbidities were also unmeasured in these models. Despite these limitations, the nationwide evidence demonstrates that structural geographic disadvantage, rather than personal socioeconomic status alone, remains intimately tied to advanced liver fibrosis in chronic hepatitis B, highlighting the imperative for targeted public health investments that expand specialist clinical access and follow-up continuity in underserved regions. analysis.brief_en: A nationwide study in Türkiye examined the relationship between socioeconomic factors and liver fibrosis severity in adults with chronic hepatitis B. The research, published on November 20, 2026, found that area-level socioeconomic disadvantage had a stronger correlation with fibrosis stages than individual socioeconomic status or birthplace background. Median Ishak fibrosis scores were 1.0 in the most developed provinces (tier 1) and 3.0 in the most deprived (tier 6), with significant fibrosis prevalence at 66.1% in tier 6 versus 7.1% in tier 1. Chronic hepatitis B remains a major global health concern, contributing to liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, and socioeconomic inequalities can disrupt the trajectory between diagnosis and clinical management.

news.content_zh: 土耳其的一项全国性研究调查了 慢性乙型肝炎 成人患者的社会经济因素与肝纤维化严重程度之间的关系。该研究于 2026 年 11 月 20 日发表,发现地区社会经济劣势与纤维化阶段的相关性比个人社会经济地位或出生地背景更强。该研究分析了 1,259 名参与者,其中 956 名被纳入最终的 队列研究 中。最发达省份(第 1 级)的 Ishak 纤维化评分中位数为 1.0,最贫困省份(第 6 级)为 3.0,第 6 级显着纤维化 患病率 为 66.1%,第 1 级为 7.1%。这些发现强调了地理和结构性社会经济因素在疾病进展和检测中的作用,强调在管理中需要基于地方的社会流行病学考虑慢性乙型肝炎。该研究使用了严格的统计方法,包括倾向评分匹配,以将地理差异与私人经济环境分开。慢性乙型肝炎 仍然是全球主要的健康问题,导致肝硬化和肝细胞癌,社会经济不平等可能会扰乱 诊断 和临床管理之间的轨迹。

The research, which brought together multiple lines of evidence, sought to clarify potential causal mechanisms and common molecular pathways linking the viral infection with pulmonary malignancy. To investigate the epidemiological relationship between the conditions, investigators conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis pooling eleven independent effect estimates drawn from ten published studies. Across the combined cohort, individuals with hepatitis B virus infection exhibited a modest positive association with lung cancer, corresponding to a pooled relative effect of 1.18 with a 95 percent confidence interval spanning 1.07 to 1.30 and a p-value of 0.003. Geographic subgroup analyses revealed notable regional variation in this epidemiological pattern. In cohorts evaluating East Asian populations, the pooled relative effect stood at 1.19 with a 95 percent confidence interval ranging from 1.10 to 1.29 and a p-value of 0.001. Conversely, the meta-analysis found no statistically significant epidemiological association between viral infection and lung cancer within the European and United States subgroup. Discover more Research assistant services Postdoc opportunities Research report templates Learn Engineering Track Biotech To assess potential causality and determine the directional nature of the connection, the researchers performed two-sample Mendelian randomization analyses using genome-wide association study datasets from both East Asian and European populations. The investigative protocol incorporated reverse and multivariable models to examine whether genetically predicted susceptibility to infection independently influenced cancer risk while accounting for major confounding factors. In the primary inverse-variance weighted Mendelian randomization analysis of East Asian datasets, genetically predicted susceptibility to hepatitis B virus infection was linked to a higher risk of developing lung cancer, yielding an odds ratio of 1.226 with a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.152 to 1.305 and a p-value below 0.0001. No corresponding genetic association emerged when evaluating the European datasets. The observed association in East Asian populations remained robust even after statistical adjustment for established respiratory risk factors. In multivariable Mendelian randomization accounting for tobacco smoking and major pulmonary comorbidities, the odds ratio for lung cancer remained elevated at 1.131, supported by a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.077 to 1.188 and a p-value below 0.001. To explore biological features that might be shared between hepatitis B infection and pulmonary tumorigenesis, researchers evaluated transcriptomic expression profiles using differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, functional enrichment methods, and machine-learning algorithms. These computational workflows identified three specific genes—PTTG1, DTL, and TPX2—as candidate cross-disease expression signatures. Discover more Tour Colleges Cancer research funding Donate to Research Find Conferences Health Experimental transcriptomic data demonstrated that PTTG1, DTL, and TPX2 were consistently upregulated in datasets representing both hepatitis B infection and lung cancer. Functional profiling indicated that these three candidate signature genes are primarily involved in cell-cycle regulation and proliferative biological processes, offering preliminary molecular targets for future research into how viral infection and lung cancer pathogenesis interact. Taken together, the researchers concluded that the study provides epidemiological and complementary genetic evidence supporting an association between hepatitis B virus infection susceptibility and lung cancer risk, with the clearest evidence observed in East Asian populations. This distinction between geographic cohorts was evident across both investigative methodologies. While East Asian datasets yielded statistically significant positive associations in observational pooling and two-sample Mendelian randomization, no statistically significant association was observed in the European and United States meta-analysis subgroup, and no corresponding genetic association was observed in European datasets. These integrated findings help address key questions in cancer epidemiology, where prior studies had suggested a link between hepatitis B virus infection and lung cancer but left the potential causal relationship and shared molecular features unclear. By conducting reverse and multivariable analyses alongside primary Mendelian randomization models, the investigators assessed both the direction and robustness of the connection. Furthermore, the authors noted that the exploratory transcriptomic and machine-learning analyses identified overlapping molecular signatures predominantly tied to cell-cycle regulation and proliferative processes, establishing candidate directions for further investigation into the biological relationship between hepatitis B virus infection and lung cancer. news.title_zh: 研究表明东亚人乙型肝炎感染与肺癌风险升高有关 - Bioengineer.org
news.source_body_en: A study published on November 19, 2026, by Bioengineer.org found a significant association between hepatitis B virus infection and an increased risk of lung cancer, particularly in East Asian populations. The research integrated epidemiological data, genetic analysis, and transcriptomics to explore potential causal mechanisms and shared molecular pathways. The pooled relative effect of hepatitis B infection on lung cancer risk was 1.18 (95% CI 1.07 to 1.30, p-value 0.003), with a stronger correlation observed in East Asian cohorts (1.19, 95% CI 1.10 to 1.29, p-value 0.001). Mendelian randomization analyses further supported this link, showing an odds ratio of 1.226 (95% CI 1.152 to 1.305, p-value < 0.0001) for East Asian populations. The association remained significant even after adjusting for tobacco smoking and other respiratory risk factors. However, no such association was found in European or U.S. populations, indicating geographic variation. The study identified three genes—PTTG1, DTL, and TPX2—as potential cross-disease expression signatures, involved in cell-cycle regulation and proliferative processes. These findings contribute to understanding the epidemiological and genetic links between hepatitis B infection and lung cancer, though they do not establish causality or suggest immediate public health interventions.

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 20, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Cancer Simplified GADA Model Accurately Detects Hepatitis B Related Liver Cancer by November 19, 2026 in Cancer, Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Simplified GADA Model Accurately Detects Hepatitis B Related Liver Cancer Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A multicenter investigation across China has validated GADA, a simplified four-variable statistical model designed to identify hepatocellular carcinoma in patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection. Developed by researchers from Peking University and collaborating clinical centers, the diagnostic tool integrates patient sex, age, des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin, and alpha-fetoprotein. Across a collective study population exceeding 23,000 individuals, the scoring system demonstrated strong discriminative performance for both overall liver cancer and early-stage disease, offering an alternative surveillance framework tailored specifically to populations with high burdens of viral hepatitis. Hepatocellular carcinoma represents a major global health challenge, with chronic hepatitis B infection responsible for more than 40 percent of cases worldwide and approximately 86 percent of cases diagnosed in China. This epidemiological pattern contrasts sharply with many Western clinical populations, where liver cancer arises more frequently from chronic hepatitis C infection, alcohol-related liver damage, and metabolic dysfunction. While the previously established GALAD algorithm integrates sex, age, alpha-fetoprotein, lens culinaris agglutinin-reactive alpha-fetoprotein, and des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin to detect liver tumors, its accuracy required dedicated re-evaluation in cohorts dominated by chronic viral hepatitis. The inclusion of lens culinaris agglutinin-reactive alpha-fetoprotein, known as AFP-L3%, introduces practical hurdles in routine healthcare environments. Measuring AFP-L3% requires specialized laboratory platforms, increases operational testing expenses, necessitates larger biological sample volumes, and remains unavailable across many secondary medical facilities. During the initial development phase, the investigative team determined that alpha-fetoprotein and des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin contributed robust and complementary diagnostic signals, whereas measuring AFP-L3% yielded minimal incremental clinical benefit among individuals with hepatitis B-related liver pathology. Discover more Research assistant services Postdoc opportunities Research report templates Learn Engineering Track Biotech To construct the streamlined diagnostic tool, investigators analyzed 2,190 adult patients presenting with chronic hepatitis B-related liver disease at Mengchao Hepatobiliary Hospital of Fujian Medical University. This cohort was randomly divided into a modeling dataset comprising 1,533 participants and an internal validation group containing 657 individuals. The resulting GADA mathematical formula calculates a predictive risk score by combining numerical coefficients: Z equals negative 11.111, plus 1.122 multiplied by sex coded as one for male or zero for female, plus 0.073 multiplied by age, plus 2.660 multiplied by the common logarithm of des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin, plus 0.578 multiplied by the common logarithm of alpha-fetoprotein. To rigorously verify model generalizability, researchers conducted a prospective external validation study enrolling 20,908 participants across ten medical centers throughout China. This external evaluation group included 905 patients diagnosed with new primary liver cancer alongside 20,003 control participants without malignancies, consisting of 17,802 individuals diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B and 2,201 patients with confirmed hepatitis B-related cirrhosis. Combining the initial developmental cohorts and the multi-hospital prospective trial yielded an overall evaluated study cohort of 23,098 individuals. Statistical evaluation demonstrated consistent diagnostic accuracy across all study phases. In the modeling cohort, the GADA tool achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.940 with a 95 percent confidence interval spanning 0.927 to 0.952, yielding 82.57 percent sensitivity and 91.53 percent specificity. Within the internal validation dataset, the model produced an area under the curve of 0.935, demonstrating 82.04 percent sensitivity and 92.65 percent specificity. In the large prospective external validation cohort, GADA maintained an area under the curve of 0.919, achieving 86.00 percent sensitivity and 81.88 percent specificity. Comparative analyses revealed that the streamlined four-variable equation consistently outperformed individual standard blood tests and older algorithms. In the developmental cohort, GADA surpassed the five-variable GALAD model, which registered an area under the curve of 0.907. Across the external validation network, GADA demonstrated superior diagnostic capacity compared to alpha-fetoprotein alone, which achieved an area under the curve of 0.748, as well as des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin alone, which registered an area under the curve of 0.841. Across individual participating hospitals, center-specific performance metrics remained stable, with areas under the curve ranging from 0.895 to 0.977 across diverse clinical settings. Discover more Tour Colleges Cancer research funding Donate to Research Find Conferences Get Health Tips The scoring system also maintained discriminative power when evaluating early-stage malignancy restricted to the Milan criteria. For these early-stage lesions, GADA yielded areas under the curve of 0.858 in the derivation cohort, 0.868 in the internal validation cohort, and 0.903 in the prospective multicenter group. Among early-stage cases in the external validation cohort, the formula identified 88.16 percent of tumors while maintaining a specificity of 74.50 percent, indicating dependable capacity to detect nascent neoplasms before advanced progression. Investigators noted that GADA was engineered specifically to address clinical demands in settings where differentiating hepatocellular carcinoma from chronic hepatitis and cirrhosis presents substantial diagnostic difficulty. Omitting the complex AFP-L3% biomarker enables broader deployment in regional clinical laboratories with limited analytical infrastructure. However, the study authors emphasize that the algorithm is intended as a clinical adjunct to support established surveillance pathways, rather than an outright substitute for abdominal imaging or multidisciplinary medical evaluation, pending prospective implementation trials and cross-laboratory assay calibration. news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 20, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Short-Course Steroids Linked to Improved Early Hepatitis B Liver Failure Outcomes by November 17, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 7 mins read 0 Short-Course Steroids Linked to Improved Early Hepatitis B Liver Failure Outcomes Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Hospitalized patients presenting with early- or pre-stage hepatitis B virus-related liver failure who received short-course intravenous methylprednisolone alongside conventional supportive care experienced significantly higher rates of four-week clinical recovery and lower overall complication rates than those treated with standard therapy alone, according to a ten-year retrospective cohort study conducted at the Affiliated Hospital of North Sichuan Medical College in Nanchong, China. The investigation evaluated medical records from 143 qualifying patients treated between January 2015 and December 2025, comparing 43 individuals who received adjunctive glucocorticoid treatment against a control cohort of 100 individuals managed exclusively with conventional medical regimens. Across the entire cohort, all participants received foundational antiviral coverage alongside liver-protective medications and symptom-directed inpatient management, providing a standardized baseline from which researchers could assess the physiological and prognostic associations of temporary corticosteroid administration during the critical initial phases of hepatic decompensation. The clinical rationale driving the study centers on the complex immunopathogenesis of hepatitis B virus-induced liver failure, which remains the leading etiology of acute hepatic collapse across China and continues to carry severe short-term mortality risks. In the earliest phases of acute deterioration, excessive immune activation and severe inflammatory cascades trigger widespread hepatocyte necrosis even while patients retain a degree of baseline synthetic functional reserve. Because this early window represents a potentially reversible interval, clinicians have long theorized that timely immunosuppression could halt rapid hepatocyte destruction and create permissive conditions for tissue regeneration. Glucocorticoids have been utilized in liver failure management for more than five decades due to their potent anti-inflammatory properties; however, their clinical adoption has remained fiercely debated because of persistent concerns regarding secondary bacterial and fungal infections, gastrointestinal bleeding, and the potential reactivation of viral replication. To rigorously examine these dynamics, the investigators applied diagnostic criteria defined by the Chinese national guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of liver failure. Eligible individuals met specific pre-stage or early-stage diagnostic benchmarks, which required severe systemic fatigue accompanied by marked gastrointestinal manifestations, significantly elevated transaminase levels, and progressive jaundice characterized by a daily total bilirubin increase of at least 17.1 micromoles per liter or absolute concentrations between 85.5 and 171 micromoles per liter. Coagulation parameters formed a critical threshold, requiring prothrombin time activity between 40 percent and 50 percent for pre-stage disease, or between 30 percent and 40 percent for early-stage disease, in the complete absence of preexisting extrahepatic organ failure. Patients presenting with confounding hepatic insults, including viral co-infections, alcoholic liver injury, drug-induced toxicity, or autoimmune disease, were systematically excluded, as were those with significant cardiopulmonary or renal comorbidities, malignancies, or previous exposure to artificial liver support and immunosuppressants. Discover more Study Biology Get Fit Guides Steroids steroids steroid Patients assigned to the conventional control arm received nucleos(t)ide analogue antiviral therapy consisting of daily entecavir at 0.5 milligrams, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate at 300 milligrams, or tenofovir alafenamide at 25 milligrams, paired with hepatoprotective agents, albumin and fresh frozen plasma infusions, and targeted complication prophylaxis. Patients in the glucocorticoid arm received identical antiviral and supportive regimens with the addition of intravenous methylprednisolone at doses ranging between 40 and 80 milligrams per day for three to seven days, followed by individual tapering or discontinuation based on clinical response, with total exposure restricted to two weeks or less. Attending clinicians selected initial methylprednisolone dosing based on baseline inflammatory activity and disease severity rather than body weight, administering 40 milligrams daily for milder inflammation and 80 milligrams daily for pronounced inflammation, while co-administering proton pump inhibitors to mitigate upper gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding risks. The primary short-term endpoint was four-week clinical improvement, evaluated as a prespecified composite measure that required the concurrent fulfillment of three strict clinical and biochemical criteria: marked symptom alleviation with complete resolution of hepatic encephalopathy based on the West Haven grading system, clinically documented resolution of ascites and jaundice, and central laboratory verification of total bilirubin falling to five times the upper limit of normal or lower alongside prothrombin time activity reaching at least 40 percent in early-stage patients or 50 percent in pre-stage patients. At the end of four weeks, 81.4 percent of patients in the glucocorticoid group achieved this composite threshold compared to 54.0 percent in the conventional group, representing a statistically significant difference. In multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, baseline coagulation, bilirubin, and viral load, glucocorticoid therapy remained an independent predictor of recovery with an odds ratio of 4.21, while baseline prothrombin time activity was also independently protective with an odds ratio of 1.04 per one percent increase. Discover more Check Symptoms Soothe Digestion Save on Rx To capture continuous physiological trajectories during the first month of hospitalization, the researchers utilized linear mixed-effects models evaluating longitudinal measurements of total bilirubin, prothrombin time activity, and serum albumin adjusted for age, sex, and baseline values. For total bilirubin, downward trajectories were observed across both groups, and while the interaction between treatment group and time did not reach statistical significance, adjusted total bilirubin concentrations remained lower overall in the methylprednisolone cohort across the monitoring period, displaying the widest between-group margin at week one before gradually converging by week four. news.content: 한국어日本語Login 한국어日本語 Search 한국어日本語Login HOMESHANGHAI DAILYCHINA BIZ BUZZEVENTSARTICLESCOMMUNITY F&B City News Hai Lights Hai Guide Lifestyle SH Health Directory Shanghai City News Service Submit Event Home > Articles > China Market for New Hepatitis B Drugs Is Large, Actual Sales Prospects Smaller [Biopharma] China Market for New Hepatitis B Drugs Is Large, Actual Sales Prospects Smaller by Tan Weiyun November 16, 2026 [Biopharma] Share Article: Caption: GSK's bepirovirsen, sold under the brand name Hibsago, won US regulatory approval in October. Seventy-five million people make for a compelling market. Finding patients who will actually take a new medicine is a more demanding business. That is the challenge facing UK pharma giant GSK as it prepares to bring its hepatitis B drug to China – a development Chinese drugmakers are watching closely as they develop their own new treatments for the viral liver disease. GSK's bepirovirsen, sold under the brand name Hibsago, won US regulatory approval in October, offering some patients the possibility of stopping medication while keeping the infection under control. At the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases meeting in Denver earlier this month, Chinese drugmakers Hengrui Pharma and Brii Biosciences presented research pursuing the same broad ambition. For companies hoping to build a business around that promise, China's vast patient population is only the starting point. The nearer-term opportunity lies within a much smaller group already receiving care, and narrows further once the requirements of a new treatment are applied. GSK's own investor presentation illustrates the gap. Of an estimated 75 million people living with chronic hepatitis B in China, about 44 million have been diagnosed and around six million are on treatment. The company said in October that bepirovirsen remained under priority review in China, with a regulatory decision expected in the first half of 2027. Even those six million currently on treatment cannot simply be counted as prospective customers. Under its US approval, Hibsago is available to adults without cirrhosis who have received antiviral treatment for at least six months, have suppressed virus levels and have hepatitis B surface antigen levels of 3,000 international units per milliliter. The antigen is a viral protein measured in blood. China's eventual prescribing rules will determine eligibility there. The published figures do not establish how many Chinese patients would qualify. Nor do they tell companies how many eligible patients would choose treatment, obtain coverage or pay for it themselves. For a patient whose infection is already controlled with daily pills, the attraction is the chance to stop treatment. But that possibility comes with additional treatment and monitoring, without any guarantee of success. In the trials supporting US approval, 24 percent of patients receiving bepirovirsen met the criteria to stop their existing antiviral medication. Twenty-four weeks after stopping all hepatitis B treatment, 19 percent had maintained viral control with no detectable surface antigen – an outcome known as a "functional cure." Most patients did not reach that endpoint. The drug also carries a boxed warning for serious liver reactions and low platelet counts. Hou Jinlin, director of the Department of Infectious Diseases at Nanfang Hospital and a lead investigator in GSK's global phase III bepirovirsen trials, said the studies enrolled patients with surface antigen levels above 100 and up to 3,000 units. He explained that earlier research suggested patients with very low antigen levels could sometimes achieve clearance with existing treatment, while those with higher levels were harder to treat. He made the comments in an interview with the Yicai news group last week. "New drugs usually face high price barriers when they are first approved," Hou told Yicai, adding that reimbursement negotiations and lower costs as the industry matures could improve access. The economics may prove as demanding as the medicine. Credit: Imaginechina In Japan, Hibsago was listed in October at 183,015 yen (about US$1,150) per 150 milligram syringe. At the standard dosage, a 24-week course requires 52 syringes, putting the drug cost at roughly 9.5 million yen, before any insurance coverage. In the US, prescription discount platform GoodRx listed a coupon price of US$12,989 for five syringes as of November 12, although GSK has yet to disclose an official US list price. The two figures reflect different pricing systems and do not indicate what the drug might cost in China. With relatively inexpensive antivirals already keeping the virus under control for many patients, a new treatment will need to justify not only its price but also the cost of monitoring and the likelihood of a lasting response. GSK has already chosen a partner to help reach those patients in China. In May, it signed an exclusive agreement with Chia Tai Tianqing, a subsidiary of Sino Biopharmaceutical, whose commercial network covers more than 5,000 medical centers. The Chinese company will handle imports, distribution, hospital access and promotion in mainland China, while GSK retains regulatory, quality and drug-safety responsibilities. The deal puts an established hospital network behind a medicine that requires doctors to identify suitable patients and follow them through treatment. It also gives the Chinese company a stake in GSK's launch while others work on potential alternatives. Hengrui's HRS-5635 is among them. A phase II study of the experimental RNA-based medicine appeared in the same November 7 conference session as GSK's late-stage research. Hengrui's interim report lists the program as having entered phase III development in China. Brii, meanwhile, is testing whether combining an RNA-based drug with treatments that stimulate the immune system can help more patients respond. Its program includes BRII-179, a therapeutic vaccine intended for people already infected with hepatitis B. One finding from Brii's Denver presentation speaks directly to the challenge of expanding treatment options. In its phase II Enrich study, 11 of 53 participants with starting surface antigen levels above 1,000 and up to 3,000 units per milliliter maintained antigen loss 24 weeks after the study treatment ended. These patients are considered harder to treat, but their antigen levels still fall within the range covered by GSK's US approval. The small study group does not establish a broader eligible market or superiority over GSK. It does, however, offer a potential route to improving responses among patients less likely to benefit from existing approaches. Brii is also investigating whether it can shorten the interferon component of its combination treatment. If confirmed in further trials, a less burdensome course could make a difference to patients weighing a new treatment against the daily pills they already take. But Brii faces a hurdle beyond clinical performance. A dispute with US-based Vir Biotechnology over the transfer of manufacturing responsibilities for elebsiran, a key component of its combination therapy, has complicated its development plans. Brii said in August that it was not advancing an elebsiran-containing hepatitis B regimen into phase III while the arbitration remained unresolved. For later entrants, these are potential points of distinction. Better response rates, simpler treatment or fewer safety concerns could give doctors a reason to choose another medicine. But each advantage will need evidence from larger studies. Percentages drawn from different trials cannot settle the comparison. There is also a distinction between winning patients already in care and reaching those who have yet to start treatment. The former requires identifying suitable candidates within existing clinics. The latter entails more diagnosis, referral and sustained engagement with the health system. That makes the 75 million figure a measure of the disease's burden, rather than a ready-made sales forecast. GSK has secured a route into thousands of Chinese medical centers. Hengrui and Brii are still assembling the evidence for medicines that could follow. Their prospects will depend on the choices made inside those clinics: Who qualifies, who is willing to try and who can afford a chance to put the pill bottle away. news.content_zh: 文章于2026年11月16日发表,讨论了将葛兰素史克公司的乙肝药物贝匹妥单抗(Hibsago)引入中国市场所面临的挑战。尽管中国有大量乙肝患者,约75 million人患有慢性乙肝,约六百万人在接受治疗,但由于严格的适应症要求,该药物的实际市场可能较小。在美国,该药物于2026年10月获批,允许部分患者在病毒水平被抑制且表面抗原水平低于3000国际单位每毫升时停药。然而,在试验中仅有24%的患者达到这些标准,19%的患者在24周后实现\"功能性治愈\"。该药物带有严重的肝反应和血小板减少的黑框警告。葛兰素史克已与智飞生物合作在中国分销该药物,但文章指出,该药物的经济因素,包括高昂的成本和报销困难,可能会限制其推广。中国监管决策预计将在2027年上半年做出,文章强调在该药物广泛使用之前需要进一步研究和成本考量。

Log in here » While most Canadians have heard of the term hepatitis B, the truth is that the majority of people in this country know very little about the potentially serious liver disease. In fact, a study released earlier this year showed nearly nine in 10 Canadians have little to no awareness of chronic hepatitis B, despite the fact that the long-term viral infection affects more than 262,000 people in this country. So, what exactly is hepatitis B? In simple terms, it is a chronic viral infection of the liver that is spread through the bloodstream. It can lead to cirrhosis, in which healthy liver tissue is replaced by scar tissue, and can create a much higher risk of liver cancer and other complications such as ascites and jaundice. What makes hepatitis B particularly insidious is the fact that it is essentially a silent condition. In most cases, an individual afflicted with the disease does not display any symptoms, especially during the early or chronic stages of the infection. “It’s really a testament to how strong the liver is in most patients, even with a chronic viral infection. You have to have at least 90 per cent of the function of the liver affected before patients display any symptoms like swelling of the abdomen or jaundice or fatigue,” says Dr. Scott Fung, director of education for the Toronto Centre for Liver Disease and an Associate Professor of Medicine at the University of Toronto. “That’s why most patients with hepatitis B don’t complain of any major symptoms and they’re often quite surprised when they are diagnosed through blood testing that they have a chronic infection.” Dr. Fung says that’s why it’s important for adult Canadians to be screened for hepatitis B: they may already have it and not even know it. He’s not alone in that opinion. In 2025, the Canadian Association for the Study of the Liver (CASL) came up with new guidelines that endorse universal screening for all adult Canadians for hepatitis B at least once in their lifetime, regardless of where they were born. There are a number of different testing options available to Canadians. However, the recommended and most effective test is known as the hepatitis B triple-panel. Dr. Fung says triple-panel screening is particularly effective because even if a person tests negative for the surface antibody, it means there is still an opportunity for health prevention and promotion, including the injection of a safe and effective hepatitis B vaccination. Beyond initial screening for those with known hepatitis B infection, more advanced blood tests are increasingly important for long-term management. Quantitative hepatitis B surface antigen (qHBsAg) testing – a simple blood test that tracks how active the virus is in the liver over time – helps doctors see whether treatment is working and better gauge a patient’s risk of serious complications such as cirrhosis and liver cancer. However, the only catch is that access to quantitative hepatitis B surface antigen testing, recommended as standard of care by CASL, remains uneven and often difficult to navigate in many parts of the country, including here in Manitoba. Yet qHBsAg testing is not routinely available through many provincial laboratory systems, meaning that people who live with hepatitis B may need closer monitoring but still be unable to access the testing needed to inform those decisions. “For many of our patients, the real challenge is getting consistent screening and follow-up for chronic hepatitis B. If access to tests like quantitative HBsAg is limited, it becomes much harder to understand how active the virus is and to make informed decisions about long-term treatment,” says Dr. Fung. That’s why ensuring both basic screening and more advanced tests such as qHBsAg are available is essential, so people living with CHB can be diagnosed, monitored and supported consistently. For patients, these tests are straightforward blood draws that can be done during routine lab visits, but they play a critical role in deciding who needs closer follow-up and which treatments are most appropriate. From a public-health perspective, investing in quantitative HBsAg testing is a practical, affordable step. When this simple blood test is funded and integrated into provincial laboratory systems, it helps clinicians better monitor chronic hepatitis B over time, guide treatment decisions and reduce costly hospitalizations for advanced liver disease, while aligning provincial practice with national CHB guidelines. Dr. Fung also recommends that patients bring up the issue of hepatitis B screening with their personal healthcare provider. “The whole point behind universal screening is you don’t have to think about a patient’s risk factors, and the patient may not even remember what their risk factors are for hepatitis B,” adds Dr. Fung. The good news is that even if someone tests positive for chronic hepatitis B, the condition can be effectively managed. For people who need treatment, antiviral medications can suppress the virus and help reduce the risk of liver complications. Dr. Fung’s suggestion is that patients who receive a positive test result should work with their doctor to develop a plan on how to manage their condition. That should include follow-up testing to determine how their liver is performing in terms of producing proteins, metabolizing various toxins, the level of scarring or stiffness in the patient’s liver and what the risk is of developing complications such as liver cancer. Dr. Fung explains it’s important for people who have been impacted by hepatitis B to understand that, thanks to advances in research and antiviral treatments, the disease doesn’t have to have life-altering consequences. “We’ve been told many of these patients are suffering in silence. They have no voice and often isolate at home. They avoid certain social activities,” he says. “Once they’ve been diagnosed with hepatitis B, that should no longer be the case because we have effective treatments. It’s a highly treatable disease. We can help the patient lower their risk of complications and lower the risk of transmissibility to others. But we need to help overcome some of the social barriers that many of these patients face.” This article is produced by the Advertising Department of the Winnipeg Free Press, in collaboration with GSK

Globally, health systems are severely impacted by both hepatitis B and hepatitis C viruses, with substantial burdens observed in low-income and middle-income nations. In Ethiopia, both viruses remain more common despite preventive interventions including the hepatitis B vaccine, universal precautions, and occupational safety procedures. Because little information had been available regarding infection frequency and related variables among Ethiopian medical waste handlers, this systematic review and meta-analysis was designed to ascertain viral prevalence and identify contributing factors in this workforce. To locate available publications, the authors searched multiple academic databases, including PubMed, Science Direct, Cochrane, Hinari, and Google Scholar, alongside grey literature and university repository sites. From this literature search, five studies comprising a total sample size of 1,211 participants were included in the systematic review and meta-analysis. The authors extracted and sorted the study data using Microsoft Excel version 13 before transferring the dataset to STATA/MP 17.0 for statistical analysis. To evaluate the methodological quality of each included study, the investigators utilized the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. In synthesizing the data, the pooled prevalence of the hepatitis B and C virus was examined using a Der Simonian random-effects model with a 95 percent confidence interval. The investigators evaluated publication bias using Egger’s test and assessed statistical heterogeneity across the included studies using the I-squared statistic. Furthermore, the possible causes of heterogeneity were explored through both subgroup analysis and meta-regression models. Across all statistical evaluations, p-values of less than 0.05 were considered statistically significant. Discover more Check Symptoms medical waste Medical Waste Book Care Services Rent Dumpsters The meta-analysis revealed significant heterogeneity among the included studies, as illustrated in the Galbraith plot, with an I-squared value of 96.21 percent and a p-value of less than 0.001. Subgroup analyses were conducted to examine how specific study characteristics influenced the reported infection rates. When the authors examined studies conducted until the year 2020, the prevalence of hepatitis B and/or hepatitis C viruses was 11.3 percent. However, when evaluating primary investigations that enrolled less than 260 participants, the researchers found that the pooled prevalence of the hepatitis B and/or hepatitis C virus was 14.90 percent. Beyond establishing overall and subgroup prevalence, the study investigated factors associated with viral infection among medical waste handlers. The analysis determined that having multiple sexual partners and experiencing prior exposure to sharp objects were associated with hepatitis B virus and/or hepatitis C virus infection. The researchers highlighted that these associations demonstrate the critical role played by both behavioral and occupational factors in hepatitis transmission. Based on these findings, the authors concluded that effective intervention requires addressing both the behavioral and occupational risks identified in the study. Reducing infection risk among medical waste handlers requires promoting safe sexual practices and strengthening infection prevention and control measures in healthcare settings.
