SpecialtyTopics Spotlight - Free In-Person Regional Events Focused on Oncology and Population Health Advertisement News|Articles|November 18, 2026 Hepatitis B Screening Gaps Persist as Functional Cure Option Arrives Author(s)Laura Joszt, MA Fact checked by: Ashley Gallagher, MA Listen 0:00 / 0:00 Key Takeaways Universal adult HBV screening remains inconsistent in primary care, driving missed diagnoses; EHR triple-panel order sets and automated inpatient/ED screening with navigators can improve capture and linkage. Reflex quantitative HBsAg testing after positive surface antigen could identify functional-cure candidates earlier, but commercial lab build-outs and EHR integration barriers delay routine adoption. Specialists are incorporating quantitative HBsAg at baseline and longitudinally to gauge proximity to functional cure, though access varies when ordering requires external laboratories. Bepirovirsen eligibility and trial design are shifting practice toward initiating NAs in gray-zone, low-HBsAg patients and treating beyond ALT thresholds using fibrosis, age, HBV DNA, and HCC risk. Weekly bepirovirsen administration and safety labs for ~6 months necessitate specialty pharmacy coordination, standing lab orders, telehealth/ECHO support, and patient counseling on modest cure probability and stigma relief. SHOW MORE New York hepatitis B experts say screening gaps and weekly monitoring demands could limit who benefits from the first functional cure therapy. Advertisement Quantitative hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) testing is becoming a routine way to find patients who could be candidates for a functional cure of chronic hepatitis B (CHB), but gaps in screening, referral, and monitoring capacity may limit who benefits, according to participants at The American Journal of Managed Care®'s Population Health Roundtable in New York, New York. The discussion preceded the October 20 FDA approval of bepirovirsen (Hibsago; GSK), the first antisense oligonucleotide for CHB.1 The treatment is indicated for adults without cirrhosis who are on suppressed antiviral therapy with HBsAg of 3000 IU/mL or less, and pooled phase 3 data showed functional cure in 19% of treated patients vs 0% of those given placebo.2 Faculty said the weekly injections and lab monitoring of bepirovirsen could strain health systems without specialty pharmacy and care coordination support. Where Screening and Linkage to Care Break Down Although the CDC recommends a universal one-time adult screening of hepatitis B,3 faculty said it rarely happens outside hepatology. One hepatologist described the pattern in referrals: "I'm getting referrals from people with elevated transaminases who have been screened for hepatitis C and not hepatitis B." One participant suggested an electronic health record (EHR) order set that bundles the full triple panel of surface antigen, surface antibody, and core antibody. Another cautioned about alert fatigue, and one health system scaled back hepatitis C screening pop-up prompts and moved reminders to a sidebar instead. Su Wang, MD, MPH, FACP, of RWJBarnabas Health, described a model that sidesteps primary care gaps: automated surface antigen screening in emergency departments and hospitals, paired with patient navigators. The program has relied on grant funding and local champions. "You get this one-on-one navigator who has been able to get 80% to 90% of people into care. I think that's a good approach," she said. Panelists discussed asking commercial laboratories to build reflex quantitative HBsAg testing after a positive surface antigen result, although one participant noted this can be difficult to set up. Without it, patients managed in primary care may never learn whether they are candidates for the functional cure. How Specialists Are Using Quantitative HBsAg Testing Participants Tatyana Kushner, MD, MSCE, Weill Cornell Medicine (moderator) Kristina Chacko, MD, FAASLD, Montefiore-Einstein Center for Transplantation Ype P. de Jong, MD, PhD, Weill Cornell Medicine Saikiran M. Kilaru, MD, NYU Langone Health Tibor Krisko, MD, Weill Cornell Medicine Mark Makhinson, PharmD, Mount Sinai Health System Rebecca Roediger, MD, Weill Cornell Medicine Mark S. Sulkowski, MD, Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine Su Wang, MD, MPH, FACP, RWJBarnabas Health Few patients arrive at specialty clinics with a quantitative HBsAg result, the specialists said. Mark S. Sulkowski, MD, of Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, has tested patients at initial evaluation and annually for 4 years and said the result shows how close treated patients may be to functional cure. Ype P. de Jong, MD, PhD, of Weill Cornell Medicine, now orders it at return visits for all patients with CHB. One panelist said that once the test is available in the EHR, ordering is simple, but it did take his health system nearly 2 years to get it added. Another said that having to order through commercial laboratories had limited how often he tested. Because participants in the phase 3 trial for bepirovirsen had to be on nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy, faculty said they are starting NAs in gray-zone patients with low HBsAg who previously declined treatment. Several also treat beyond guideline thresholds, calling alanine aminotransferase (ALT) cutoffs outdated and weighing fibrosis, age, viral load, and family history of liver cancer instead. What Weekly Bepirovirsen Monitoring Demands From Health Systems Patients used to a daily pill and twice yearly visits will face about 6 months of weekly injections and labs to monitor ALT flares and low platelet counts once on bepirovirsen. Mark Makhinson, PharmD, of Mount Sinai Health System, noted that most of the large health systems at the roundtable, in the New York–New Jersey area, have robust specialty pharmacy programs that handle prior authorization, financial assistance, and monthly adherence checks through in-house specialty pharmacies. "I think it's really positive, but...that is likely not the norm everywhere," Makhinson said. Sulkowski said the group is working to rebuild the hepatitis C–era pharmacy partnerships that have largely been dismantled and to concentrate prescribing among a few bepirovirsen champions rather than all 15 clinicians who treat hepatitis B. Advanced practice providers would handle follow-up, with 340B Drug Pricing Program revenue justifying the hires. Wang suggested standing weekly lab orders, telehealth support, and ECHO-style learning networks to extend capacity beyond specialists. A roughly 1-in-5 chance of functional cure is progress, the participants said, but it calls for candid conversations with patients about the odds. One panelist wants real-world data in their own patient population before committing patients to roughly 20% odds of cure. Wang said one benefit goes unmeasured in trials: relief from the stigma of living with hepatitis B. "Patients, they feel infectious; [then] they worry about giving it to their family members, and there's a shame about that," Wang said. "Being able to say, 'I lost my surface antigen' is very liberating for them." References McCormick B. Bepirovirsen approval offers new option for chronic HBV treatment. AJMC®. October 21, 2026. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 20, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Cancer Simplified GADA Model Accurately Detects Hepatitis B Related Liver Cancer by November 19, 2026 in Cancer, Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Simplified GADA Model Accurately Detects Hepatitis B Related Liver Cancer Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A multicenter investigation across China has validated GADA, a simplified four-variable statistical model designed to identify hepatocellular carcinoma in patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection. Developed by researchers from Peking University and collaborating clinical centers, the diagnostic tool integrates patient sex, age, des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin, and alpha-fetoprotein. Across a collective study population exceeding 23,000 individuals, the scoring system demonstrated strong discriminative performance for both overall liver cancer and early-stage disease, offering an alternative surveillance framework tailored specifically to populations with high burdens of viral hepatitis. Hepatocellular carcinoma represents a major global health challenge, with chronic hepatitis B infection responsible for more than 40 percent of cases worldwide and approximately 86 percent of cases diagnosed in China. This epidemiological pattern contrasts sharply with many Western clinical populations, where liver cancer arises more frequently from chronic hepatitis C infection, alcohol-related liver damage, and metabolic dysfunction. While the previously established GALAD algorithm integrates sex, age, alpha-fetoprotein, lens culinaris agglutinin-reactive alpha-fetoprotein, and des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin to detect liver tumors, its accuracy required dedicated re-evaluation in cohorts dominated by chronic viral hepatitis. The inclusion of lens culinaris agglutinin-reactive alpha-fetoprotein, known as AFP-L3%, introduces practical hurdles in routine healthcare environments. Measuring AFP-L3% requires specialized laboratory platforms, increases operational testing expenses, necessitates larger biological sample volumes, and remains unavailable across many secondary medical facilities. During the initial development phase, the investigative team determined that alpha-fetoprotein and des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin contributed robust and complementary diagnostic signals, whereas measuring AFP-L3% yielded minimal incremental clinical benefit among individuals with hepatitis B-related liver pathology. To construct the streamlined diagnostic tool, investigators analyzed 2,190 adult patients presenting with chronic hepatitis B-related liver disease at Mengchao Hepatobiliary Hospital of Fujian Medical University. This cohort was randomly divided into a modeling dataset comprising 1,533 participants and an internal validation group containing 657 individuals. The resulting GADA mathematical formula calculates a predictive risk score by combining numerical coefficients: Z equals negative 11.111, plus 1.122 multiplied by sex coded as one for male or zero for female, plus 0.073 multiplied by age, plus 2.660 multiplied by the common logarithm of des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin, plus 0.578 multiplied by the common logarithm of alpha-fetoprotein. To rigorously verify model generalizability, researchers conducted a prospective external validation study enrolling 20,908 participants across ten medical centers throughout China. This external evaluation group included 905 patients diagnosed with new primary liver cancer alongside 20,003 control participants without malignancies, consisting of 17,802 individuals diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B and 2,201 patients with confirmed hepatitis B-related cirrhosis. Combining the initial developmental cohorts and the multi-hospital prospective trial yielded an overall evaluated study cohort of 23,098 individuals. Statistical evaluation demonstrated consistent diagnostic accuracy across all study phases. In the modeling cohort, the GADA tool achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.940 with a 95 percent confidence interval spanning 0.927 to 0.952, yielding 82.57 percent sensitivity and 91.53 percent specificity. Within the internal validation dataset, the model produced an area under the curve of 0.935, demonstrating 82.04 percent sensitivity and 92.65 percent specificity. In the large prospective external validation cohort, GADA maintained an area under the curve of 0.919, achieving 86.00 percent sensitivity and 81.88 percent specificity. Comparative analyses revealed that the streamlined four-variable equation consistently outperformed individual standard blood tests and older algorithms. In the developmental cohort, GADA surpassed the five-variable GALAD model, which registered an area under the curve of 0.907. Across the external validation network, GADA demonstrated superior diagnostic capacity compared to alpha-fetoprotein alone, which achieved an area under the curve of 0.748, as well as des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin alone, which registered an area under the curve of 0.841. Across individual participating hospitals, center-specific performance metrics remained stable, with areas under the curve ranging from 0.895 to 0.977 across diverse clinical settings. The scoring system also maintained discriminative power when evaluating early-stage malignancy restricted to the Milan criteria. For these early-stage lesions, GADA yielded areas under the curve of 0.858 in the derivation cohort, 0.868 in the internal validation cohort, and 0.903 in the prospective multicenter group. Among early-stage cases in the external validation cohort, the formula identified 88.16 percent of tumors while maintaining a specificity of 74.50 percent, indicating dependable capacity to detect nascent neoplasms before advanced progression. Investigators noted that GADA was engineered specifically to address clinical demands in settings where differentiating hepatocellular carcinoma from chronic hepatitis and cirrhosis presents substantial diagnostic difficulty. Omitting the complex AFP-L3% biomarker enables broader deployment in regional clinical laboratories with limited analytical infrastructure. However, the study authors emphasize that the algorithm is intended as a clinical adjunct to support established surveillance pathways, rather than an outright substitute for abdominal imaging or multidisciplinary medical evaluation, pending prospective implementation trials and cross-laboratory assay calibration. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 20, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Area Disadvantage Outweighs Personal Socioeconomic Status in Chronic Hepatitis B Liver Fibrosis by November 18, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Area Disadvantage Outweighs Personal Socioeconomic Status in Chronic Hepatitis B Liver Fibrosis Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram In a nationwide multicentre investigation examining adults living with chronic hepatitis B across twenty-four clinical centres in Türkiye, the severity of histologically staged liver fibrosis was found to correlate far more consistently with area-level socioeconomic disadvantage in a patient’s current place of residence than with individual socioeconomic measures or birthplace background. Chronic viral hepatitis remains a substantial driver of progressive hepatic injury, yet the extent to which broader geographical deprivation shapes the clinical severity at which liver disease is diagnosed has remained insufficiently characterised. By evaluating biopsy-confirmed liver tissue alongside detailed socioeconomic data, investigators identified a pronounced spatial gradient in disease stage that persisted even after rigorous statistical adjustments for demographic profiles, personal income, and healthcare engagement markers. These findings suggest that broader living environments and structural barriers exert a substantial influence on disease detection and progression, underscoring the vital importance of place-based social epidemiological factors in explaining disparities across the chronic hepatitis B continuum of care. Chronic hepatitis B continues to represent a formidable worldwide public health priority, serving as a primary underlying cause of irreversible liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Global epidemiological assessments from 2022 estimated that 254 million people were living with chronic hepatitis B virus infection, resulting in approximately 1.2 million incident infections and 1.1 million deaths within that year alone. Within this challenging international context, Türkiye represents a clinically relevant setting, where national seroprevalence studies indicate that hepatitis B surface antigen positivity spans between 4.0% and 4.6% of the general population, accompanied by notable geographic and demographic variation. Although clinical protocols emphasise regular surveillance to avert end-stage hepatic sequelae, socioeconomic inequalities can severely disrupt the trajectory between diagnosis and clinical management. Fibrosis severity at presentation effectively functions as an objective biological correlate of delayed care, highlighting that patients who face pronounced social vulnerabilities frequently enter specialized hospital infrastructure only after significant and potentially irreversible structural liver damage has already become established. To investigate these dynamics systematically, the researchers screened 1,259 adult candidates aged 18 years or older who had undergone diagnostic liver biopsy during routine clinical care between 1 January 2019 and 31 December 2024 across 24 participating centres throughout Türkiye. All included individuals presented with chronic infection confirmed by the persistence of hepatitis B surface antigen for at least six months. From this initial group, 147 patients declined participation in structured face-to-face interviews, 134 lacked definitive histopathological biopsy reports, and 22 were excluded because of comorbid conditions known to independently exacerbate liver fibrosis, such as coinfection with hepatitis C virus, hepatitis D virus, or human immunodeficiency virus, chronic alcohol consumption, active malignancy, or hereditary conditions such as Wilson disease or haemochromatosis. The resulting analytic cohort comprised 956 adults with complete biopsy and socioeconomic assessments. Within this cohort, 53.7% were male, the median age was 46.0 years, the median age at diagnosis was 27.0 years, and the median age at biopsy was 41.0 years. Assessment of area-level socioeconomic context was grounded in the official İl SEGE-2025 framework, operationalised as the provincial socioeconomic development index across all eighty-one administrative provinces of Türkiye. This framework synthesises 52 objective indicators across eight core dimensions, including demography, employment, education, healthcare infrastructure, innovation, fiscal structure, territorial accessibility, and overall living quality, classifying provinces into six development tiers where level 1 denotes the highest socioeconomic development and level 6 denotes the most severe deprivation. Concurrently, comprehensive personal data were gathered through post-biopsy face-to-face interviews, capturing formal educational attainment, employment status, household occupancy, monthly income, receipt of governmental social assistance, health insurance coverage, and residential stability. In addition, healthcare accessibility was measured directly through reported travel times to secondary or tertiary centres equipped for chronic viral hepatitis management, alongside documented durations of clinical follow-up prior to tissue sampling, providing a robust empirical framework capable of isolating structural geographic disparities from private economic circumstances. Histological evaluation served as the primary clinical outcome, with hepatic fibrosis graded according to the standardized Ishak scoring system spanning from stage 0 through stage 6. Within the full analytic cohort of 956 patients, mild fibrosis corresponding to Ishak stages 0 through 2 was identified in 73.1% of participants, moderate fibrosis covering stages 3 and 4 was documented in 21.7%, and advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis encompassing stages 5 and 6 was found in 5.2%. In primary multivariable ordinal logistic regression across the entire range of fibrosis stages, a one-level decline in provincial socioeconomic development was independently associated with an adjusted odds ratio of 1.97 for reaching higher fibrosis stages (95% confidence interval: 1.82 to 2.15; P < 0.001). Concurrently, older age at biopsy (adjusted odds ratio: 1.12 per 10-year increment; P = 0.019), longer travel time to a specialized care centre (adjusted odds ratio: 1.53 per category increase; P < 0.001), and longer duration of residence in the current locality (adjusted odds ratio: 1.21 per 5-year increase; P = 0.023) independently predicted greater fibrosis severity. To rigorously interrogate potential confounding in comparisons between regions of extreme development, the research team implemented propensity score matching and overlap weighting focused strictly on participants living in tier 1 and tier 6 provinces. In the 1:1 nearest-neighbour matched cohort balanced for age at biopsy and exact sex across 127 paired individuals, participants residing in the most disadvantaged socioeconomic environment exhibited markedly higher fibrosis burdens. Specifically, median Ishak fibrosis scores were 1.0 in tier 1 compared with 3.0 in tier 6, and the prevalence of significant fibrosis, defined as Ishak stage 3 or higher, reached 66.1% in tier 6 compared with merely 7.1% in tier 1. Stratified conditional logistic regression revealed that residence in tier 6 conferred an odds ratio of 26.00 for significant liver fibrosis relative to tier 1 (95% confidence interval: 8.21 to 82.37; P < 0.001). Overlap weighting demonstrated matching stability, producing a weighted significant fibrosis prevalence of 63.6% in tier 6 versus 6.6% in tier 1, corresponding to a weighted odds ratio of 24.75 (95% confidence interval: 8.96 to 68.36; P < 0.001). Sequential sensitivity regression models further reinforced the robustness of these observed associations when introducing additional layers of statistical control. Among participants residing in the extreme provincial tiers, the unadjusted contrast in significant fibrosis yielded an odds ratio of 28.83 after controlling for age and sex, which remained largely unchanged at an odds ratio of 28.17 following the inclusion of individual-level socioeconomic indicators such as household income and schooling. When access-related factors, including travel duration and pre-biopsy surveillance continuity, were incorporated into the model, the odds ratio remained pronounced at 18.98 (95% confidence interval: 8.43 to 42.72; P < 0.001). Crucially, formal interaction tests demonstrated no evidence of effect modification across age (P = 0.425), sex (P = 0.110), or equivalised household income (P = 0.695). Moreover, the relative index of inequality calculated across the ridit-ranked personal income distribution was not statistically associated with significant fibrosis (odds ratio: 0.63, 95% confidence interval: 0.21 to 1.87; P = 0.401), showing that personal financial resources alone did not explain the substantial regional disparity. Model-derived predicted probabilities clearly illustrated the clinical gap separating populations situated at opposite ends of the geographic socioeconomic spectrum. For a 40-year-old male with an average equivalised household income, the model-estimated probability of presenting with significant liver fibrosis was 69.3% (95% confidence interval: 59.8% to 77.4%) in tier 6 provinces, compared with only 7.4% (95% confidence interval: 3.3% to 15.6%) in tier 1 environments. Similarly, when assessing individuals earning a standardized household income of 30,000 Turkish liras monthly at the median cohort age of 41 years, the predicted probability of significant fibrosis stood at 70.3% (95% confidence interval: 61.0% to 78.2%) in the most disadvantaged provinces, while remaining at 8.7% (95% confidence interval: 4.4% to 16.4%) in the most developed provinces. Across both geographical groupings, estimated risks rose steadily with advancing age, yet the trajectories across income brackets ran strictly parallel, demonstrating that elevated income provided little apparent mitigation against the adverse structural conditions present in underdeveloped provinces. Further insight into the dominance of contemporary living conditions over historical origin emerged from reciprocal subgroup evaluations categorising patients by birthplace and migration destination. Among 370 individuals born in the most disadvantaged tier 6 provinces, the prevalence of significant liver fibrosis varied dramatically according to their current place of residence (chi-square P < 0.001). Those who remained in tier 6 exhibited the highest prevalence of significant fibrosis at 72.1%, whereas individuals who had migrated to moderately developed tier 4 or tier 5 provinces showed lower rates of 31.2% and 23.1%, respectively, and those residing in highly developed tier 1, 2, or 3 settings had rates of 8.3%, 7.0%, and 7.9%. Conversely, among participants born in affluent tier 1 provinces, significant fibrosis occurred in only 3.7% of those who remained in tier 1, compared with 55.0% among those who relocated to tier 6. This reciprocal symmetry firmly indicates that cumulative liver injury correlates with current residential conditions rather than early-life regional origin. To synthesize these interconnected dynamics, the researchers developed a conceptual directed acyclic graph illustrating how regional socioeconomic deprivation exerts downstream pressures through extended travel burdens and fragmented clinical surveillance, culminating in advanced histological fibrosis at biopsy. Nevertheless, the authors emphasised important methodological caveats, noting that the cohort was observational, hospital-based, and reliant on routine clinical biopsies rather than a population-wide screening protocol. Central pathology re-review was unavailable, and interviews were conducted after biopsy with a median interval of 60 months, meaning personal variables captured circumstances at interview. Detailed viral loads, antiviral treatment regimens, and metabolic comorbidities were also unmeasured in these models. Despite these limitations, the nationwide evidence demonstrates that structural geographic disadvantage, rather than personal socioeconomic status alone, remains intimately tied to advanced liver fibrosis in chronic hepatitis B, highlighting the imperative for targeted public health investments that expand specialist clinical access and follow-up continuity in underserved regions. supplementary_news.content: Chronic Hepatitis B Segment Leads a Market Projected to reach US$6.51 Billion by 2033 | Reaches a Commercial Turning Point as Functional-Cure Therapies Enter Practice The hepatitis B treatment market is entering a new phase as Hibsago (bepirovirsen) has secured approvals in Japan and the United States. The treatment is intended for a defined group of adults with chronic hepatitis B and offers a finite-course approach alongside existing antiviral therapy. Its arrival raises a practical market question: how quickly can health systems identify eligible patients, manage treatment safely and make a new treatment pathway accessible? DataM Intelligence values the global hepatitis B treatment market at US$3.82 billion in 2025 and projects US$6.51 billion by 2033, representing a 6.9% CAGR during 2026-2033. Chronic hepatitis B is the leading type segment, while North America holds the largest regional position and Asia Pacific is forecast to grow fastest. The recent approvals and late-stage pipeline activity could shift competition toward patient identification, treatment duration and clinical monitoring, alongside price and access. Request Executive Sample: https://www.datamintelligence.com/download-sample/hepatitis-b-treatment-market?kailas Recent Developments - November 8, 2026 - Precision BioSciences presented updated Phase 1 ELIMINATE-B data for PBGENE-HBV at the AASLD Liver Meeting. The company reported results from 25 patients and 59 administrations; the candidate remains investigational, with Phase 2 dosing planned for 2027. - November 5, 2026 - GSK outlined new Hibsago analyses at AASLD, including long-term B-Well trial results and work on response prediction and retreatment. These analyses may help clinicians and developers define how response monitoring could shape future treatment strategies. - November 3, 2026 - Health Canada approved Hibsago for eligible non-cirrhotic adults with chronic hepatitis B. GSK said Canadian supply is anticipated in early 2027, making access timing distinct from the approval date. - October 20, 2026 - The U.S. FDA approved Hibsago for use with nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy in eligible adults without cirrhosis. The label requires prior antiviral treatment and suppressed HBV DNA, and includes warnings on hepatic flares and thrombocytopenia that make monitoring part of implementation. - August 24, 2026 - Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare approved Hibsago for chronic hepatitis B patients meeting defined viral-marker criteria after at least six months of nucleos(t)ide analogue treatment. This was the product's first global approval. - May 28, 2026 - GSK reported Phase III B-Well results, published in the New England Journal of Medicine: functional cure was reported in 19% of the overall eligible treatment group versus none in the standard-of-care control group at the primary assessment. The result is clinically significant, but the therapy's defined eligibility and safety profile remain central to uptake. - May 11, 2026 - GSK signed an exclusive collaboration with China's Sino Biopharmaceutical and subsidiary Chia Tai Tianqing to support potential bepirovirsen launch activities. The planned local distribution and hospital-access role targets a market with a substantial chronic hepatitis B burden; the candidate was still under regulatory review in China at that time. Market Disruption The main disruption is a potential change in the treatment value proposition: from indefinite viral suppression to a finite course that may achieve functional cure for some eligible patients. This does not eliminate the role of established antivirals, which remain the standard treatment and are required alongside Hibsago under its U.S. indication. Instead, the shift creates a layered market in which diagnostics, eligibility testing, safety monitoring and follow-up can affect uptake as much as the drug itself. Separately, gene-editing and immune-based candidates are exploring viral reservoirs or immune response, but remain investigational and carry greater clinical and regulatory uncertainty. Segment Analysis Chronic hepatitis B leads the type segmentation because patients may need ongoing care to control viral replication and reduce the risk of liver complications. For manufacturers, the commercial opportunity is tied to finding patients earlier and differentiating treatment options by duration, response and tolerability. In practice, long-term therapy may remain appropriate for many patients, while a finite course will depend on label criteria, physician judgment and follow-up capacity. The report identifies vaccines as the leading treatment category. This reflects its broad segmentation, which includes vaccines alongside antiviral drugs, immune-modulator drugs and surgery. Vaccination is preventive rather than treatment for established chronic infection, so the category should be interpreted within the report's market definition. Antiviral drugs remain central to chronic disease management; new finite-course approaches may add a distinct layer rather than replace them. United States and Japan Market Implications United States Market: FDA approval creates a defined clinical pathway for eligible adults already receiving antiviral therapy, but adoption depends on quantitative HBsAg testing, evaluation of cirrhosis status and management of label warnings. Providers and health systems will need to integrate patient selection and monitoring into existing hepatitis care. Pricing and coverage will also influence how broadly the treatment can be used. Japan Market: Japan's August approval gives the market early experience with a functional-cure treatment, supported by existing screening and treatment efforts. For commercial planning, the next questions are how quickly eligible patients are identified, how the therapy is incorporated into specialist practice and how monitoring and reimbursement affect access. Japan's approval criteria should not be assumed to match the U.S. label exactly. Company Profiles GSK GSK has moved into a new position in chronic hepatitis B through Hibsago, licensed from Ionis Pharmaceuticals. Following approvals in Japan and the United States, the company is also advancing regulatory review in other markets and building local commercial arrangements in China. Gilead Sciences Gilead Sciences competes through established antiviral therapy, including Vemlidy (tenofovir alafenamide), used to treat chronic hepatitis B. Its position reflects the ongoing need for viral suppression and long-term management even as finite-course approaches enter practice. Dynavax Technologies Dynavax Technologies participates in the report's vaccine segment with Heplisav-B, a preventive hepatitis B vaccine for adults. Its role is upstream of treatment for chronic infection, illustrating how the report's broad category brings prevention and disease management into one market frame. Bharat Biotech Bharat Biotech is identified among the report's key companies and has vaccine capabilities, including GeneVac-B. Its relevance is strongest in prevention and immunization supply, complementary to drug developers focused on established chronic infection. Market Outlook The hepatitis B treatment market's commercial direction will depend on whether emerging options can deliver durable responses in routine practice and whether health systems can identify suitable patients. Approval is an important milestone, but access will also hinge on safety monitoring, reimbursement, diagnostic capacity and continuity of follow-up. DataM Intelligence's 2026-2033 market outlook captures a category where established antivirals remain foundational even as new approaches broaden treatment goals. For companies, the strategic challenge is to develop therapies and market-access plans that fit different patient groups, regulatory environments and care infrastructures. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 20, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Cancer Study Links Hepatitis B Infection to Elevated Lung Cancer Risk in East Asians by November 19, 2026 in Cancer Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Study Links Hepatitis B Infection to Elevated Lung Cancer Risk in East Asians Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A comprehensive study integrating epidemiological data, genetic analysis, and transcriptomics has identified a significant association between hepatitis B virus infection and an increased risk of lung cancer, with the strongest correlation observed among East Asian populations. The research, which brought together multiple lines of evidence, sought to clarify potential causal mechanisms and common molecular pathways linking the viral infection with pulmonary malignancy. To investigate the epidemiological relationship between the conditions, investigators conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis pooling eleven independent effect estimates drawn from ten published studies. Across the combined cohort, individuals with hepatitis B virus infection exhibited a modest positive association with lung cancer, corresponding to a pooled relative effect of 1.18 with a 95 percent confidence interval spanning 1.07 to 1.30 and a p-value of 0.003. Geographic subgroup analyses revealed notable regional variation in this epidemiological pattern. In cohorts evaluating East Asian populations, the pooled relative effect stood at 1.19 with a 95 percent confidence interval ranging from 1.10 to 1.29 and a p-value of 0.001. Conversely, the meta-analysis found no statistically significant epidemiological association between viral infection and lung cancer within the European and United States subgroup. To assess potential causality and determine the directional nature of the connection, the researchers performed two-sample Mendelian randomization analyses using genome-wide association study datasets from both East Asian and European populations. The investigative protocol incorporated reverse and multivariable models to examine whether genetically predicted susceptibility to infection independently influenced cancer risk while accounting for major confounding factors. In the primary inverse-variance weighted Mendelian randomization analysis of East Asian datasets, genetically predicted susceptibility to hepatitis B virus infection was linked to a higher risk of developing lung cancer, yielding an odds ratio of 1.226 with a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.152 to 1.305 and a p-value below 0.0001. No corresponding genetic association emerged when evaluating the European datasets. The observed association in East Asian populations remained robust even after statistical adjustment for established respiratory risk factors. In multivariable Mendelian randomization accounting for tobacco smoking and major pulmonary comorbidities, the odds ratio for lung cancer remained elevated at 1.131, supported by a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.077 to 1.188 and a p-value below 0.001. To explore biological features that might be shared between hepatitis B infection and pulmonary tumorigenesis, researchers evaluated transcriptomic expression profiles using differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, functional enrichment methods, and machine-learning algorithms. These computational workflows identified three specific genes—PTTG1, DTL, and TPX2—as candidate cross-disease expression signatures. Experimental transcriptomic data demonstrated that PTTG1, DTL, and TPX2 were consistently upregulated in datasets representing both hepatitis B infection and lung cancer. Functional profiling indicated that these three candidate signature genes are primarily involved in cell-cycle regulation and proliferative biological processes, offering preliminary molecular targets for future research into how viral infection and lung cancer pathogenesis interact. Taken together, the researchers concluded that the study provides epidemiological and complementary genetic evidence supporting an association between hepatitis B virus infection susceptibility and lung cancer risk, with the clearest evidence observed in East Asian populations. This distinction between geographic cohorts was evident across both investigative methodologies. While East Asian datasets yielded statistically significant positive associations in observational pooling and two-sample Mendelian randomization, no statistically significant association was observed in the European and United States meta-analysis subgroup, and no corresponding genetic association was observed in European datasets. These integrated findings help address key questions in cancer epidemiology, where prior studies had suggested a link between hepatitis B virus infection and lung cancer but left the potential causal relationship and shared molecular features unclear. By conducting reverse and multivariable analyses alongside primary Mendelian randomization models, the investigators assessed both the direction and robustness of the connection. Furthermore, the authors noted that the exploratory transcriptomic and machine-learning analyses identified overlapping molecular signatures predominantly tied to cell-cycle regulation and proliferative processes, establishing candidate directions for further investigation into the biological relationship between hepatitis B virus infection and lung cancer. Virus Replication via Phosphatase Activity 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月20日 来源:Journal of Medical Virology 3.7 编辑推荐: 乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染仍是肝硬化和肝细胞癌(HCC)的主要病因。研究人员前期通过对长期HBV感染肝细胞的时序蛋白质组学与转录组学整合分析,鉴定出线粒体跨膜蛋白PGAM5为潜在的HBV限制因子,但其底层机制尚未阐明。本研究在多种HBV复制细胞模型和小鼠模型中 欢迎索取义翘神州凋亡检测试剂盒最新资料 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 RESEARCH ARTICLE Open Access 乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染仍是肝硬化和肝细胞癌(HCC)的主要病因。研究人员前期通过对长期HBV感染肝细胞的时序蛋白质组学与转录组学整合分析,鉴定出线粒体跨膜蛋白PGAM5为潜在的HBV限制因子,但其底层机制尚未阐明。本研究在多种HBV复制细胞模型和小鼠模型中评估了PGAM5的潜在抗HBV活性,并采用多重实验手段检测HBV的转录与复制水平。在HBV复制细胞模型中,PGAM5以剂量依赖方式显著降低HBV抗原、病毒RNA和核心颗粒DNA水平,其抑制效力与具有强效抗HBV活性的干扰素刺激基因(ISG)MyD88相当。机制层面,PGAM5既促进病毒RNA降解,又抑制其合成。抗HBV功能依赖于磷酸酶活性及长亚型PGAM5L的C端结构域,而短亚型PGAM5S无抑制作用。在体内实验中,共递送小鼠PGAM5表达质粒与prcccDNA/pCMV-Cre系统显著抑制HBV抗原分泌,并降低肝内共价闭合环状DNA(cccDNA)水平。在HepG2-NTCP细胞中,PGAM5过表达同样抑制病毒抗原产生,并诱导细胞分裂相关信号通路。综上,这些发现确立PGAM5为抗HBV的宿主限制因子,并界定了其亚型特异性的功能要求及相关信号改变。 研究背景与立题依据 免费索取义翘神州Anti-His 标签单抗详细资料领 取 慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)由乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染引起,是全球肝纤维化、肝硬化和肝细胞癌(HCC)的主要诱因。现有临床方案以核苷(酸)类似物(NUCs)和干扰素为主,前者阻断病毒复制,后者通过干扰素刺激基因(ISG)及抗病毒免疫应答发挥作用,但疗效远未满足治愈需求。HBV为嗜肝DNA病毒,其松弛环状DNA(rcDNA)入核后修复为共价闭合环状DNA(cccDNA),以微染色体形式转录出3.5 kb前基因组RNA(pgRNA)、2.4/2.1 kb preS/S RNA及0.7 kb HBx RNA;cccDNA的持续存在是HBV治愈的核心障碍。cccDNA转录与复制受病毒元件和大量宿主因子共同调控,其中宿主限制因子(如MX2、SAMD4、MyD88)可抑制HBV,而HNF1/4α、CEBP、RXRα等则促病毒复制。线粒体磷酸甘油酸变位酶5(PGAM5)是定位于线粒体内膜的丝氨酸/苏氨酸(Ser/Thr)磷酸酶,参与线粒体动力学与程序性细胞死亡,存在长亚型(PGAM5L)与短亚型(PGAM5S)两种剪接体。前期多组学筛查提示PGAM5可能是非经典抗HBV宿主因子,另有研究称其经MAVS–TBK1–IRF3通路诱导I型干扰素(IFN)发挥抗病毒作用,但PGAM5是否直接限制HBV、依赖何种结构域与酶活、是否走干扰素路线,均缺乏系统实验证据。基于此,研究人员开展本研究以界定PGAM5的抗HBV属性与机制。 主要技术方法概括 研究采用pHBV1.3复制质粒、prcccDNA/pCMV-Cre重组cccDNA(rcccDNA)系统及HBVcircle系统在HepG2、Huh-7、HEK293T、HepAD38、HepG2-NTCP细胞中过表达或敲低PGAM5;通过ELISA检测HBsAg/HBeAg,RT-qPCR与Northern blot检测HBV RNA,Southern blot与NAGE检测核心颗粒DNA及装配衣壳,Actinomycin D追踪pgRNA衰变动力学,荧光素酶报告基因检测Sp1/Sp2/ENI-Xp/ENII-Cp启动子活性,FISH联合免疫荧光观察PGAM5、HBc与pgRNA共定位;体内采用C57BL/6小鼠尾静脉高压注射(HDI)rcccDNA+mPGAM5模型,辅以RNA-seq解析转录组变化。无患者样本队列,所有数据来自细胞系与小鼠模型。 研究结果(按原文小标题浓缩) 3.1 PGAM5 Potently Inhibits HBV Replication in a Dose-Dependent Manner 在前期候选基因验证中,PGAM5抑制HBV抗原与细胞内RNA的效力最强,优于EXOSC6、CAV1、CAV2等其他命中基因。HepG2共转pHBV1.3或rcccDNA后,PGAM5过表达剂量依赖地降低上清HBsAg、HBeAg,减少pgRNA、总RNA及核心颗粒DNA,效果与MyD88相当;rcccDNA体系中还观察到cccDNA模板轻度下降。内源PGAM5定位于线粒体膜,HBV感染初期其信号一过性减弱,而慢性感染患者肝组织转录组中PGAM5持续上调。 3.2 PGAM5 Preferentially Inhibits Episomal HBV Replication but Not Integrated HBV Expression PGAM5在Huh-7、HEK293T中同样抑制游离型(episomal)HBV模板(pHBV1.3、rcccDNA、HBVcircle)的抗原与RNA;但在整合型HBV驱动的HepAD38细胞中,慢病毒过表达PGAM5不影响HBsAg、HBeAg及分泌HBV DNA,而MyD88仍可降低HBsAg。说明PGAM5选择性靶向cccDNA/质粒等游离模板,不作用于染色体整合HBV DNA,且该活性不依赖肝特异性因子。 3.3 PGAM5L, but Not PGAM5S, Reduces HBV RNA Levels by Suppressing Transcription and Promoting RNA Decay 启动子报告显示PGAM5剂量依赖抑制ENII/Cp(pre-C/C)与ENI/Xp(X)活性,对Sp1、Sp2几乎无影响;Actinomycin D衰变实验证实PGAM5加速pgRNA降解(HepAD38中无此效应)。亚型比较中仅PGAM5L抑制抗原并压制Cp/Xp启动子,PGAM5S无效;磷酸酶死突变体PGAM5L-H105A完全丧失抗HBV活性,而ΔTM、ΔKEAP缺失不影响功能;PGAM5抑制剂LFHP-1c则剂量依赖地升高病毒抗原与转录本。结论:抗HBV依赖磷酸酶活性与PGAM5L的C端。 3.4 PGAM5L Associates With HBc and Correlates With Reduced pgRNA-Containing Capsids 共聚焦显示内源PGAM5与线粒体、HBc共定位;过表达PGAM5L(非PGAM5S)使HBc puncta与pgRNA puncta减少,pgRNA阳性衣壳比例下降。NAGE-immunoblot进一步证实PGAM5L降低总装配衣壳与核心蛋白水平,提示PGAM5L通过与HBc相互作用干扰衣壳装配/pgRNA包裹。 3.5 PGAM5 Suppresses HBV Replication in a Recombinant cccDNA Mouse Model C57BL/6小鼠高压共注rcccDNA+mPGAM5后,血清HBsAg、HBeAg剂量依赖下降,肝内cccDNA及骨架DNA(相对mtDNA)经qPCR与Southern blot均显著减少;ALT、AST、体重、肝指数与肝组织形态无异常,显示体内有效且未见明显毒性。 3.6 PGAM5 Upregulates Mitogenesis-Related Transcriptional Changes 在HBV感染的HepG2-NTCP中,PGAM5慢病毒过表达降低HBeAg、上清HBV DNA、胞内pgRNA与总RNA,但HBsAg基本不变(与Sp1/Sp2不受抑一致)。RNA-seq显示CDCA5、CDC20、CDCA8、CCNB1、MKI67等有丝分裂发生基因上调,GO富集于染色体分离、核分裂、细胞周期转换;炎症/细胞因子通路下调。IFN-β与ISRE报告基因未被PGAM5激活,EdU显示无增殖增加——抗HBV不依赖经典干扰素通路,也不靠加速肝细胞分裂。 讨论与结论翻译 讨论部分指出:PGAM5是HBV真正的宿主限制因子,对游离模板(cccDNA/质粒)有效、对整合模板无效;机制上同时压制ENII/Cp与ENI/Xp启动子、加速pgRNA衰变、经HBc互作破坏衣壳完整性,并降低体内cccDNA池。其抗HBV严格依赖磷酸酶活性与PGAM5L C端,PGAM5S无功能;不同于HCV/EV-D68/PDCoV中PGAM5走MAVS–TBK1–IRF3或IRF7路线,本研究系统中PGAM5不触发IFN-β/ISRE,而是伴随有丝分裂发生信号上调却不驱动增殖。HBV感染引起线粒体分布重塑、PGAM5一过性下降而慢性期持续升高,提示阶段依赖性调控。cccDNA下降的具体机制(是否经表观遗传或降解途径)仍未阐明,PGAM5L寡聚化是否参与亦待验证。 结论部分原文对应翻译:总之,研究人员确立PGAM5为重要的宿主限制因子,通过协同调控病毒转录、RNA稳定性与衣壳完整性抑制HBV感染。PGAM5抑制ENII/Cp与ENI/Xp启动子/增强子活性,加速pgRNA降解,并通过与HBc相互作用干扰核心蛋白功能与衣壳装配;磷酸酶活性与长亚型PGAM5L的C端结构域对其抗病毒活性不可或缺。在高压注射rcccDNA小鼠模型中,PGAM5亦降低肝内cccDNA水平。转录组分析提示其作用关联有丝分裂发生信号,而非经典免疫通路。 小 】 时间:2026年11月20日 来源:JHEP Reports 8.7 编辑推荐: 背景与目的:乙型肝炎病毒(Hepatitis B virus, HBV)在慢性感染期间以遗传异质性病毒群体形式持续存在,但共存的基因组之间的连锁变异与互补如何塑造病毒表型仍不清楚。BCP是嵌入X开放阅读框内的关键转录控制元件,而preS1区域除了编码蛋白结构域 HBV)在慢性感染期间以遗传异质性病毒群体形式持续存在,但共存的基因组之间的连锁变异与互补如何塑造病毒表型仍不清楚。BCP是嵌入X开放阅读框内的关键转录控制元件,而preS1区域除了编码蛋白结构域外,还控制LHBs蛋白的转录。研究人员研究了慢性HBV感染期间疾病相关的BCP与5' preS1缺失的基因组连锁及其协同效应。 方法:采用纳米孔测序技术对246例未接受治疗的B基因型和C基因型感染患者的全长HBV基因组进行分析。在HepG2复制模型、NTCP依赖性感染模型和水动力注射小鼠模型中研究了代表性变异体的特性。 结果:在3,886个全长HBV单体型中,连锁的BCP–5' preS1缺失仅在C基因型中被发现,并且在HBeAg阳性慢性乙型肝炎(II期)中的流行率高于HBeAg阳性慢性HBV感染(I期)(26%对9%;p=0.013)。携带者的血清HBV DNA水平高于非携带者(8.57±0.21对8.36±0.30 log10 IU/ml;p=0.028)。在转染的HepG2细胞中,连锁缺失使细胞外HBV DNA相对于野生型增加约8.0倍。这种复制优势源于BCP缺失增加pgRNA产生与5' preS1缺失所产生的突变型聚合酶增强逆转录的互补效应。然而,BCP缺失也通过HBx截短损害了有效感染。在反式提供HBx可恢复细胞中的感染性,并在体内挽救连锁缺失的表型。 结论:远距离连锁的BCP与5' preS1缺失协同增强HBV复制,揭示了异质性HBV群体中连锁变异如何协同塑造病毒进化、持久性和致病性。 影响与意义:HBV突变研究传统上集中于单个基因组区域。然而,异质性病毒群体中的连锁变异可能表现出不同的生物学和临床效应。研究人员的发现表明,低丰度的BCP-5' preS1缺失单体型可通过基因组内协同和基因组间互补获得增强的复制和感染能力,突出了少数HBV变异的潜在临床相关性。基于全长单体型分析可能揭示先前未被认识的、影响持久性和治疗应答的协作性病毒群体,这需要在更大规模的前瞻性队列中进行验证。 乙型肝炎病毒(Hepatitis B virus, HBV)慢性感染仍是全球肝硬化和肝细胞癌的主要病因之一。尽管核苷(酸)类似物能有效抑制病毒复制,但无法清除共价闭合环状DNA(cccDNA)储库。在感染个体内,HBV以错误倾向逆转录产生的异质性群体形式存在。虽已证实共存的HBV变异体之间存在功能互补,但自然循环病毒基因组内远距离突变的基因组连锁及其生物学意义仍待阐明。以往研究多独立分析BCP/preCore及preS区域突变,区域特异性测序无法判断这些突变是否共存于同一病毒基因组。研究人员对未治疗HBeAg阳性患者进行全长纳米孔测序,鉴定出携带连锁BCP与5' preS1缺失的HBV单体型,这些单体型作为病毒准种中的亚群,与其他病毒基因组共存而非成为优势群体。鉴于HBV基因组紧凑且高度重叠,BCP缺失可能同时影响pgRNA/preCore mRNA转录、表面基因转录及HBx表达或功能;5' preS1缺失则同时改变LHBs介导的进入功能及重叠聚合酶的特性。因此,连锁缺失的生物学后果无法从单一区域研究中推断。研究人员重建了临床鉴定的连锁缺失变异体,系统表征其复制、感染性及对核苷(酸)类似物的反应,重点关注单个基因组内连锁突变的功能协同及共存病毒基因组间的互补。 义翘神州通用型Whitlow 218 Linker兔单抗,高效助力CAR流式检测,欢迎索取详细资料>>领 取 研究人员对246例未治疗HBeAg阳性患者(95例I期、151例II期)进行全长HBV纳米孔测序,并对30例C基因型II期患者纵向随访的306个全长克隆序列进行独立验证。经质量控制后获得13,094,000条纳米孔读段,通过聚类策略解析为3,886个全长HBV单体型。全基因组缺失谱分析确定了三个复发缺失热点:BCP(nt1742-1849)、Core(nt2000-2300)和5' preS1(nt2848-2883)。在C基因型II期患者中,连锁BCP-5' preS1缺失为主要连锁缺失模式,占连锁缺失单体型81.0%、支持读段91.9%及克隆66.7%。临床关联分析显示,连锁缺失频率和流行率在II期显著高于I期,携带者血清HBV DNA和ALT水平显著升高。在30例接受拉米夫定联合阿德福韦治疗104周的患者中,5例基线连锁缺失频率≥20%者中有4例未实现HBeAg血清学转换,提示该变异与抗病毒治疗应答不良相关。 接下来,研究人员构建了C基因型1.3-mer HBV复制子,包含BCP突变(Cm)及缺失(Cd1、Cd2、Cd3)、5' preS1缺失(C18)及连锁缺失突变体。转染HepG2细胞后,BCP突变显著减少HBeAg分泌但增加细胞内HBc表达,5' preS1缺失则增加HBeAg和细胞外LHBs水平。Southern blot和qPCR检测显示,BCP突变体产生更高水平的复制性HBV DNA中间体(RC、DSL、SS DNA),连锁缺失时进一步增强;cccDNA检测也显示连锁缺失突变体水平最高。因此,BCP突变是转染模型中增强复制的主要驱动因素,而连锁5' preS1缺失进一步增加病毒DNA合成。 为阐明机制,研究人员分析病毒RNA转录。BCP缺失构建体产生更强的3.5-kb和2.4/2.1-kb RNA信号。通过CP-preC和CP-pg荧光素酶报告基因证实,A1762T/G1764A突变和BCP缺失均降低CP-preC活性但增加CP-pg活性,表明转录向pgRNA偏移。ENHII片段实验表明BCP突变未显著损伤增强子功能。由于BCP缺失产生C端截短HBx,研究人员在HBx敲除背景下比较发现,BCP缺失构建体仍保留增强的复制表型,证明HBx编码序列改变本身不能解释复制增强。对于5' preS1缺失,通过CL1复制子(仅突变L1起始密码子而不改变聚合酶氨基酸序列)证明,仅改变LHBs翻译起始不足以产生复制表型;而通过聚合酶缺陷复制子及反式补充实验证实,15-nt和18-nt间隔区缩短的聚合酶变体显著提高逆转录效率,33-nt缺失则无增强作用。因此,5' preS1缺失通过缩短重叠聚合酶间隔区增强HBV逆转录。 在核苷(酸)类似物敏感性实验中,恩替卡韦(ETV)和替诺福韦艾拉酚胺(TAF)处理后,含BCP缺失的构建体(尤其连锁缺失)残留HBV DNA水平较高。IC50分析显示,连锁缺失不显著影响ETV敏感性,但使TAF的IC50轻度升高。感染实验中,5' preS1缺失增强NTCP依赖性感染,而BCP相关HBx功能缺陷限制有效感染。在稳定表达野生型HBx或K130M/V131I HBx的KXN7细胞系中,HBx缺陷病毒的感染性被反式互补恢复,而C端截短HBx无法挽救。水动力注射小鼠模型证实,单独注射连锁缺失突变体时病毒标志物低于野生型,但与野生型HBV共注射或反式提供HBx后,血清HBsAg、HBV DNA水平显著升高,甚至超过野生型单独注射组。 讨论指出,BCP缺失通过增加pgRNA转录促进复制,5' preS1缺失通过缩短聚合酶间隔区增强逆转录,二者在单个基因组内协同作用。同时,HBx缺陷的连锁缺失基因组依赖共存基因组反式提供的HBx恢复cccDNA转录,实现群体水平互补。临床队列中连锁缺失变异与更高ALT、更高病毒载量及抗病毒治疗应答不良相关,说明低丰度变异具有潜在临床意义。研究结论为:远距离连锁的BCP和5' preS1缺失通过基因组内协同和基因组间互补增强HBV复制,揭示异质性HBV群体中连锁变异协同塑造病毒进化、持久性和致病性的机制。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪! 从2000到2026,27载全因有您;您的每一分支持,都给予我们无穷的动力! 公测期:打赏8元解锁30天免费阅读! supplementary_news.content: 内质网应激抑制慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染中CLEC18的表达及其作为HBsAg血清学转换后免疫恢复生物标志物的信号作用 《Immunity, Inflammation and Disease》:CLEC18 Suppressed by ER Stress in Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection and Signals an Immune Recovery Biomarker After Seroconversion 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月19日 来源:Immunity, Inflammation and Disease 2.7 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 ORIGINAL ARTICLE Open Access 背景:CLEC18是一种新型C型凝集素,在肝脏中高表达并定位于内质网(ER)。既往研究表明,慢性乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染患者血浆CLEC18水平降低,且与核苷(酸)类似物(NUC)治疗的应答相关。已知HBV可诱导内质网应激以促进病毒复制并颠覆宿主免疫应答;然而,内质网应激导致CLEC18下调及分泌受损的机制尚不清楚。材料与方法:研究人员回顾性分析了121例处于慢性HBV感染不同临床阶段的患者及17例健康对照。测定并比较各HBV阶段的血浆CLEC18水平。同时,将HBV质粒转染至Huh7肝癌细胞,并使用衣霉素和毒胡萝卜素诱导内质网应激,以评估未折叠蛋白反应(UPR)激活及细胞内与细胞外CLEC18水平。结果:血浆CLEC18水平在免疫清除期及乙型肝炎表面抗原(HBsAg)血清学转换后显著高于免疫耐受期。在Huh7细胞中,HBV转染或化学诱导内质网应激可激活磷酸化eIF2α、ATF4及XBP-1s,并导致CLEC18在细胞内蓄积,同时其分泌至上清液中的量减少。讨论:慢性HBV感染似乎通过内质网应激介导的分泌受损来抑制循环CLEC18水平,而病毒控制的恢复则伴随血浆CLEC18的回升。因此,CLEC18可作为慢性HBV感染中免疫恢复的生物标志物,而靶向内质网应激以恢复CLEC18转运可能是一种潜在的治疗策略。 研究背景:乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染是一项全球性健康问题,可导致慢性乙型肝炎、肝功能失代偿、肝硬化和肝细胞癌。内质网(ER)应激在HBV感染中发挥重要作用,乙型肝炎表面抗原(HBsAg)和乙型肝炎X抗原(HBxAg)均可在肝脏模型中诱导内质网应激,尤其是涉及HBsAg preS2缺失突变的情况。内质网应激由未折叠或错误折叠蛋白在内质网中蓄积所触发,可促进细胞内HBV DNA和HBsAg的滞留并抑制其分泌。PreS缺失突变在HBV中较为常见,可导致HBsAg在内质网中显著蓄积,从而放大内质网应激、延迟HBV DNA清除并加重肝细胞损伤。CLEC18是一种新型C型凝集素,定位于内质网,由N端多肽、C端C型凝集素结构域(CTLD)、EGF及EGF样结构域以及SCP/TAPS结构域组成,是一种可与岩藻聚糖、β-葡聚糖和半乳聚糖等聚糖结合的分泌蛋白。CLEC18在肝组织和免疫细胞中高表达,作为Toll样受体3(TLR3)的共受体增强干扰素(IFN)产生及干扰素刺激基因(ISG)表达,从而防御病毒感染。既往研究发现HBV感染可抑制肝组织和血浆中的CLEC18,CLEC18可作为预测接受NUC治疗患者HBeAg丢失、血清学转换(SC)及病毒学应答的潜在生物标志物。然而,接受和未接受NUC治疗的HBV患者血浆CLEC18水平的动态变化尚未被表征,且HBV感染下调CLEC18表达的机制尚不清楚。因此,研究人员旨在进一步阐明慢性HBV感染中CLEC18表达的时间动态,评估在有无NUC治疗的患者中HBeAg和HBsAg血清学转换期间CLEC18的变化,并探讨其与丙氨酸氨基转移酶(ALT)所反映的肝脏炎症的关系;同时探究内质网应激如何影响CLEC18的产生和释放。 领取义翘神州CRO技术服务资料 领 取 研究人员开展了以下研究:回顾性分析121例处于不同临床阶段的慢性HBV感染患者及17例健康对照,测定血浆CLEC18水平并在各HBV阶段间进行比较;同时以Huh7肝癌细胞为模型,转染野生型HBV及PreS2缺失型HBV质粒,并使用衣霉素(TM)和毒胡萝卜素(TG)诱导内质网应激,评估未折叠蛋白反应激活及细胞内与细胞外CLEC18水平。研究得出以下结论:慢性HBV感染似乎通过内质网应激介导的分泌受损来抑制循环CLEC18水平,而病毒控制的恢复则伴随血浆CLEC18的回升;CLEC18可作为慢性HBV感染中免疫恢复的生物标志物,靶向内质网应激以恢复CLEC18转运可能是一种潜在的治疗策略。这项研究的重要意义在于揭示了HBV感染中CLEC18下调的机制,并为HBV感染的免疫恢复监测和潜在治疗策略提供了新思路。 关键技术方法:研究人员建立了一个回顾性临床队列(121例慢性HBV感染患者及17例健康对照,样本来源于中国医药大学附设医院,2005年8月至2016年8月),采用自行开发的酶联免疫吸附试验(ELISA)测定血浆CLEC18水平,并以Architect i2000系统检测HBeAg、抗-HBe抗体、HBsAg及抗-HBs抗体,以COBAS AmpliPrep-COBAS TaqMan HBV试验测定HBV DNA。在体外实验中,研究人员构建野生型及PreS2缺失型HBV表达质粒并转染Huh7细胞,使用衣霉素和毒胡萝卜素诱导内质网应激,通过Western blot检测磷酸化eIF2α、ATF4及XBP-1s等未折叠蛋白反应标志物,并以夹心ELISA定量细胞内和上清液中的CLEC18。 研究结果:(1)HBsAg血清学转换期间血浆CLEC18表达:研究人员利用接受NUC治疗的慢性乙型肝炎患者纵向队列(n=21),观察到HBsAg血清学转换时血浆CLEC18水平显著升高,以血清学转换前1年水平为基线,血清学转换时平均升高11.4±4.5倍(p=0.031),HBsAg丢失后1年升高35.3±14.3倍(p=0.03),HBsAg血清学转换后2年升高76.9±26.4倍(p=0.009),表明血浆CLEC18分泌不仅在HBsAg丢失时反弹,且在血清学转换后早期持续上升。(2)患者招募及血浆CLEC18与临床参数的相关性:共纳入121例不同阶段慢性HBV感染患者及17例健康个体,血浆CLEC18在免疫耐受期最低(215.0±24.8 pg/mL),在免疫清除期升高(871.4±290.2 pg/mL),在实现HBsAg血清学转换的患者中无论是否接受NUC治疗均升高(接受NUC治疗者799.0±208.4 pg/mL,未接受NUC治疗者1538.0±863.0 pg/mL),健康个体血浆CLEC18水平显著高于免疫耐受期;相关性分析显示血浆CLEC18水平与ALT水平相关(Pearson相关,p=0.049),而与HBV DNA无显著关联(p=0.42),提示血浆CLEC18反映肝脏炎症而非病毒复制。(3)HBV诱导内质网应激并使CLEC18在肝细胞中蓄积:将野生型和PreS2缺失型HBV质粒转染Huh7细胞后,XBP-1s和ATF4表达较空载体对照明显增加,细胞内CLEC18水平在两种HBV转染后均升高,而上清液中CLEC18水平较对照组降低,表明HBV刺激后增加的细胞内CLEC18蓄积于Huh7细胞并抑制其分泌至上清液。(4)HBV介导的内质网应激增加细胞内CLEC18表达并减少细胞外CLEC18分泌:用衣霉素和毒胡萝卜素处理Huh7细胞24小时后,呈现剂量依赖性未折叠蛋白反应激活,磷酸化eIF2α、ATF4和XBP-1s上调,并伴随细胞内CLEC18增加;上清液中CLEC18随毒胡萝卜素处理剂量依赖性降低(0.5 μM时p=0.0115),表明内质网应激损害CLEC18向细胞外空间的分泌。 讨论部分总结:与免疫耐受期相比,血浆CLEC18在免疫清除期更高,且在HBsAg血清学转换后持续上升,无论NUC治疗状态如何。在慢性HBV感染期间(排除HBsAg血清学转换期),CLEC18与ALT相关而与HBV DNA无关,提示血浆CLEC18反映肝脏炎症而非病毒载量;HBsAg血清学转换后,无论通过NUC治疗还是自发清除,血浆CLEC18水平逐渐升高,表明病毒控制恢复了CLEC18分泌。研究揭示CLEC18在HBV诱导的内质网应激后在细胞内蓄积而不被分泌,这与临床数据显示HBV患者血浆CLEC18水平低于健康对照相一致。机制上,HBV诱导和化学诱导的内质网应激下CLEC18在Huh7细胞中的蓄积提示内质网-高尔基体轴存在潜在检查点,错误折叠的病毒蛋白和凝集素货物竞争分泌机器。鉴于CLEC18作为内质体中的TLR3共受体,内质网滞留可能暂时隔离CLEC18直至稳态恢复,延迟其参与内质体抗病毒信号传导;HBsAg血清学转换后CLEC18分泌的恢复可能放大TLR3依赖的IFN产生,强化病毒控制并促进持续免疫监视。临床上HBV患者血浆CLEC18也较低,但由于细胞模型聚焦于肝细胞而临床数据来自血液样本,不能确定肝脏分泌受损完全解释血清水平降低,体外发现与体内观察之间仍存在差距。尽管血浆CLEC18在慢性HBV感染期间与ALT相关,但临床队列的回顾性和观察性设计不允许推断因果关系;体外发现表明HBV质粒转染和化学诱导的内质网应激损害CLEC18分泌,支持HBV相关细胞应激和肝细胞损伤导致循环CLEC18水平降低的可能性,但不能排除CLEC18表达或转运改变影响抗病毒免疫应答从而促进肝脏炎症的替代可能性,因此CLEC18与肝脏炎症之间的关系可能是双向的。研究局限性包括回顾性设计、单中心亚洲人群、使用肝癌细胞系而非原代人肝细胞、CLEC18也表达于免疫细胞群因此血浆CLEC18可能反映肝脏和免疫细胞两方面的贡献、HBsAg血清学转换患者数量有限不足以进行可靠的ROC分析确定截断值或评估预测性能等。未来研究应在非亚洲队列中验证发现,使用原代人肝细胞确认内质网应激与CLEC18转运之间的机制联系,并鉴定与CLEC18相互作用的具体HBV蛋白及其调控CLEC18分泌的分子机制。 研究结论翻译:本研究证明CLEC18表达与HBV感染及免疫应答密切相关。血浆CLEC18水平在免疫清除和HBsAg血清学转换等关键阶段升高,但在免疫耐受期被抑制,可能由HBV诱导的内质网应激所致。这些发现表明CLEC18既是HBV恢复的标志物,也可能是免疫调节的潜在参与者,为HBV持续存在的研究和治疗策略提供了新途径。 研究背景:乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染是一项全球性健康问题,可导致慢性乙型肝炎、肝功能失代偿、肝硬化和肝细胞癌。内质网(ER)应激在HBV感染中发挥重要作用,乙型肝炎表面抗原(HBsAg)和乙型肝炎X抗原(HBxAg)均可在肝脏模型中诱导内质网应激,尤其是涉及HBsAg preS2缺失突变的情况。内质网应激由未折叠或错误折叠蛋白在内质网中蓄积所触发,可促进细胞内HBV DNA和HBsAg的滞留并抑制其分泌。PreS缺失突变在HBV中较为常见,可导致HBsAg在内质网中显著蓄积,从而放大内质网应激、延迟HBV DNA清除并加重肝细胞损伤。CLEC18是一种新型C型凝集素,定位于内质网,由N端多肽、C端C型凝集素结构域(CTLD)、EGF及EGF样结构域以及SCP/TAPS结构域组成,是一种可与岩藻聚糖、β-葡聚糖和半乳聚糖等聚糖结合的分泌蛋白。CLEC18在肝组织和免疫细胞中高表达,作为Toll样受体3(TLR3)的共受体增强干扰素(IFN)产生及干扰素刺激基因(ISG)表达,从而防御病毒感染。既往研究发现HBV感染可抑制肝组织和血浆中的CLEC18,CLEC18可作为预测接受NUC治疗患者HBeAg丢失、血清学转换(SC)及病毒学应答的潜在生物标志物。然而,接受和未接受NUC治疗的HBV患者血浆CLEC18水平的动态变化尚未被表征,且HBV感染下调CLEC18表达的机制尚不清楚。因此,研究人员旨在进一步阐明慢性HBV感染中CLEC18表达的时间动态,评估在有无NUC治疗的患者中HBeAg和HBsAg血清学转换期间CLEC18的变化,并探讨其与丙氨酸氨基转移酶(ALT)所反映的肝脏炎症的关系;同时探究内质网应激如何影响CLEC18的产生和释放。研究人员开展了以下研究:回顾性分析121例处于不同临床阶段的慢性HBV感染患者及17例健康对照,测定血浆CLEC18水平并在各HBV阶段间进行比较;同时以Huh7肝癌细胞为模型,转染野生型HBV及PreS2缺失型HBV质粒,并使用衣霉素(TM)和毒胡萝卜素(TG)诱导内质网应激,评估未折叠蛋白反应激活及细胞内与细胞外CLEC18水平。研究得出以下结论:慢性HBV感染似乎通过内质网应激介导的分泌受损来抑制循环CLEC18水平,而病毒控制的恢复则伴随血浆CLEC18的回升;CLEC18可作为慢性HBV感染中免疫恢复的生物标志物,靶向内质网应激以恢复CLEC18转运可能是一种潜在的治疗策略。这项研究的重要意义在于揭示了HBV感染中CLEC18下调的机制,并为HBV感染的免疫恢复监测和潜在治疗策略提供了新思路。关键技术方法:研究人员建立了一个回顾性临床队列(121例慢性HBV感染患者及17例健康对照,样本来源于中国医药大学附设医院,2005年8月至2016年8月),采用自行开发的酶联免疫吸附试验(ELISA)测定血浆CLEC18水平,并以Architect i2000系统检测HBeAg、抗-HBe抗体、HBsAg及抗-HBs抗体,以COBAS AmpliPrep-COBAS TaqMan HBV试验测定HBV DNA。在体外实验中,研究人员构建野生型及PreS2缺失型HBV表达质粒并转染Huh7细胞,使用衣霉素和毒胡萝卜素诱导内质网应激,通过Western blot检测磷酸化eIF2α、ATF4及XBP-1s等未折叠蛋白反应标志物,并以夹心ELISA定量细胞内和上清液中的CLEC18。研究结果:(1)HBsAg血清学转换期间血浆CLEC18表达:研究人员利用接受NUC治疗的慢性乙型肝炎患者纵向队列(n=21),观察到HBsAg血清学转换时血浆CLEC18水平显著升高,以血清学转换前1年水平为基线,血清学转换时平均升高11.4±4.5倍(p=0.031),HBsAg丢失后1年升高35.3±14.3倍(p=0.03),HBsAg血清学转换后2年升高76.9±26.4倍(p=0.009),表明血浆CLEC18分泌不仅在HBsAg丢失时反弹,且在血清学转换后早期持续上升。(2)患者招募及血浆CLEC18与临床参数的相关性:共纳入121例不同阶段慢性HBV感染患者及17例健康个体,血浆CLEC18在免疫耐受期最低(215.0±24.8 pg/mL),在免疫清除期升高(871.4±290.2 pg/mL),在实现HBsAg血清学转换的患者中无论是否接受NUC治疗均升高(接受NUC治疗者799.0±208.4 pg/mL,未接受NUC治疗者1538.0±863.0 pg/mL),健康个体血浆CLEC18水平显著高于免疫耐受期;相关性分析显示血浆CLEC18水平与ALT水平相关(Pearson相关,p=0.049),而与HBV DNA无显著关联(p=0.42),提示血浆CLEC18反映肝脏炎症而非病毒复制。(3)HBV诱导内质网应激并使CLEC18在肝细胞中蓄积:将野生型和PreS2缺失型HBV质粒转染Huh7细胞后,XBP-1s和ATF4表达较空载体对照明显增加,细胞内CLEC18水平在两种HBV转染后均升高,而上清液中CLEC18水平较对照组降低,表明HBV刺激后增加的细胞内CLEC18蓄积于Huh7细胞并抑制其分泌至上清液。(4)HBV介导的内质网应激增加细胞内CLEC18表达并减少细胞外CLEC18分泌:用衣霉素和毒胡萝卜素处理Huh7细胞24小时后,呈现剂量依赖性未折叠蛋白反应激活,磷酸化eIF2α、ATF4和XBP-1s上调,并伴随细胞内CLEC18增加;上清液中CLEC18随毒胡萝卜素处理剂量依赖性降低(0.5 μM时p=0.0115),表明内质网应激损害CLEC18向细胞外空间的分泌。讨论部分总结:与免疫耐受期相比,血浆CLEC18在免疫清除期更高,且在HBsAg血清学转换后持续上升,无论NUC治疗状态如何。在慢性HBV感染期间(排除HBsAg血清学转换期),CLEC18与ALT相关而与HBV DNA无关,提示血浆CLEC18反映肝脏炎症而非病毒载量;HBsAg血清学转换后,无论通过NUC治疗还是自发清除,血浆CLEC18水平逐渐升高,表明病毒控制恢复了CLEC18分泌。研究揭示CLEC18在HBV诱导的内质网应激后在细胞内蓄积而不被分泌,这与临床数据显示HBV患者血浆CLEC18水平低于健康对照相一致。机制上,HBV诱导和化学诱导的内质网应激下CLEC18在Huh7细胞中的蓄积提示内质网-高尔基体轴存在潜在检查点,错误折叠的病毒蛋白和凝集素货物竞争分泌机器。鉴于CLEC18作为内质体中的TLR3共受体,内质网滞留可能暂时隔离CLEC18直至稳态恢复,延迟其参与内质体抗病毒信号传导;HBsAg血清学转换后CLEC18分泌的恢复可能放大TLR3依赖的IFN产生,强化病毒控制并促进持续免疫监视。临床上HBV患者血浆CLEC18也较低,但由于细胞模型聚焦于肝细胞而临床数据来自血液样本,不能确定肝脏分泌受损完全解释血清水平降低,体外发现与体内观察之间仍存在差距。尽管血浆CLEC18在慢性HBV感染期间与ALT相关,但临床队列的回顾性和观察性设计不允许推断因果关系;体外发现表明HBV质粒转染和化学诱导的内质网应激损害CLEC18分泌,支持HBV相关细胞应激和肝细胞损伤导致循环CLEC18水平降低的可能性,但不能排除CLEC18表达或转运改变影响抗病毒免疫应答从而促进肝脏炎症的替代可能性,因此CLEC18与肝脏炎症之间的关系可能是双向的。研究局限性包括回顾性设计、单中心亚洲人群、使用肝癌细胞系而非原代人肝细胞、CLEC18也表达于免疫细胞群因此血浆CLEC18可能反映肝脏和免疫细胞两方面的贡献、HBsAg血清学转换患者数量有限不足以进行可靠的ROC分析确定截断值或评估预测性能等。未来研究应在非亚洲队列中验证发现,使用原代人肝细胞确认内质网应激与CLEC18转运之间的机制联系,并鉴定与CLEC18相互作用的具体HBV蛋白及其调控CLEC18分泌的分子机制。研究结论翻译:本研究证明CLEC18表达与HBV感染及免疫应答密切相关。血浆CLEC18水平在免疫清除和HBsAg血清学转换等关键阶段升高,但在免疫耐受期被抑制,可能由HBV诱导的内质网应激所致。这些发现表明CLEC18既是HBV恢复的标志物,也可能是免疫调节的潜在参与者,为HBV持续存在的研究和治疗策略提供了新途径。 supplementary_news.content: 吴超/黄睿教授团队:聚焦慢乙肝风险评估,探索抗病毒治疗获益|AASLD 2026 医脉通消化科 2026-11-19 20:02发布于北京 问AI · 低病毒血症群体治疗适应证会否就此拓宽? 2026年11月5日-9日,美国肝病研究学会年会(AASLD 2026)于美国科罗拉多州丹佛市召开。会上,南京大学医学院附属鼓楼医院感染性疾病科黄睿教授、王健博士和吴超教授团队四项研究成果入选大会壁报交流,其中一项获得Early Career Investigator奖。准确评估疾病风险与治疗应答,是优化慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)个体化治疗的重要依据。四项研究分别探讨了血清HBV RNA动态变化与抗病毒治疗应答的关系、不确定期CHB患者显著肝纤维化的无创预测,以及低乙型肝炎表面抗原(HBsAg)水平、低HBV DNA水平两类乙型肝炎e抗原(HBeAg)阴性CHB患者的抗病毒治疗获益,为CHB患者的疗效预测、风险评估及治疗决策提供了重要依据。 研究一:接受核苷(酸)类似物治疗的慢性乙型肝炎患者血清HBV RNA的动态变化与治疗应答 (4017) 01 研究背景 血清乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)RNA可反映CHB患者肝内共价闭合环状 DNA(cccDNA)的转录活性。本研究探讨了接受核苷(酸)类似物(NA)治疗的CHB患者血清HBV RNA的动态变化及治疗应答。 02 研究方法 本项研究纳入接受NA治疗的初治CHB患者。在基线及NA治疗期间检测血清HBV RNA,采用Cobas 6800系统及配套的Cobas HBV RNA实时PCR检测方法进行定量,定量下限为10 copies/mL。分析HBV RNA与病毒学应答(VR,HBV DNA不可检出)、血清学应答(SR,HBeAg清除)及联合应答(CR,HBeAg清除且HBsAg<3000 IU/mL)的关联。 03 研究结果 共纳入654例患者,其中51.8%为HBeAg阳性。HBeAg阳性患者的基线HBV RNA水平高于HBeAg阴性患者(6.3 vs. 2.3 log10 copies/mL,P<0.001)。基线HBV RNA水平(aOR:0.505,95% CI:0.355–0.719,P<0.001)和HBeAg阳性状态(aOR:0.346,95% CI:0.138–0.869,P=0.024)与治疗第48周HBV RNA不可检出显著相关。 图1 抗病毒治疗过程中HBV RNA水平的动态变化 在HBeAg阳性患者中,治疗第12、24和48周HBV RNA降幅较大(>1 log10 copies/mL)的患者,5年VR、SR及CR累积发生率均显著更高。在这些患者中,治疗第12、24和48周HBV RNA的下降均与实现VR、SR及CR的更高可能性独立相关。 图2 HBeAg阳性患者治疗12、24、48周时HBVRNA下降>1.0 log10 copies/mL和≤1.0 log10 copies/mL患者的VR (A)、SR (B)和CR (C)累积发生率比较 04 研究结论 在接受NA治疗的CHB患者中,较高的基线HBV RNA水平及HBeAg阳性的患者实现HBV RNA降至不可检出水平的可能性更低。在接受NA治疗的HBeAg阳性CHB患者中,治疗早期血清HBV RNA下降>1 log10 copies/mL与VR、SR及CR相关。血清HBV RNA可能有助于指导CHB患者的个体化治疗策略。 研究二:基于机器学习构建不确定期慢性乙型肝炎患者显著纤维化预测模型 (4030) 01 研究背景 尽管2025年AASLD乙型肝炎指南推荐采用共同决策方式管理不确定期CHB患者,但是否存在显著纤维化是制定抗病毒治疗决策的重要依据。本研究采用机器学习方法,开发并验证了一种无创模型,以准确预测不确定期CHB患者的显著纤维化。 02 研究方法 回顾性纳入中国5家医疗中心的751例接受肝活检的CHB患者,所有患者均符合2025年AASLD不确定期CHB标准。显著纤维化的诊断依据Scheuer分级标准,即肝纤维化分期≥S2。患者按7∶3的比例随机分为训练队列和验证队列。在训练队列中,采用LASSO逻辑回归和Boruta算法筛选候选变量。采用梯度提升机(GBM)结合10折交叉验证,比较具有临床相关性的特征集,并使用最终特征集训练多种机器学习算法,包括逻辑回归、随机森林、极端梯度提升(XGBoost)、GBM、支持向量机(SVM)和决策树。在验证队列中,通过受试者工作特征曲线下面积(AUROC)、校准及决策曲线分析,将最终模型与天冬氨酸氨基转移酶与血小板比值指数(APRI)及基于4项因子的肝纤维化指数(FIB-4)进行比较。 03 研究结果 训练队列和验证队列分别纳入522例和229例患者,其中分别有301例(57.7%)和132例(57.6%)存在显著纤维化。最终模型采用GBM构建,纳入5个变量:HBV DNA、血小板计数、凝血酶原时间、白蛋白和天冬氨酸氨基转移酶(AST)。在验证队列中,GBM模型的AUROC为0.755(95%CI:0.693–0.816),显著高于APRI(AUROC:0.681,95% CI:0.611–0.750,P=0.015)和FIB-4(AUROC:0.669,95% CI:0.599–0.738,P=0.012)。该模型还表现出可靠的校准性能(Brier评分为0.199,Hosmer–Lemeshow检验P>0.05),并在决策曲线分析中显示出更高的净获益。 表1 受试者工作特征曲线分析 图3 验证队列中的校准(A)和决策曲线分析(B) 04 研究结论 该新型机器学习模型纳入5个常规可获取的变量,性能优于APRI和FIB-4,可为不确定期CHB患者的显著肝纤维化提供可靠的风险预测。该模型或可作为此类人群治疗决策的实用工具。 研究三:抗病毒治疗对低HBsAg水平的HBeAg阴性CHB患者临床结局的影响 (4127) 01 研究背景 血清HBsAg水平较低(<100 IU/mL)与CHB患者不良结局风险降低相关。抗病毒治疗在低HBsAg水平CHB患者中的长期获益尚不明确。本研究比较了低HBsAg水平的HBeAg阴性CHB患者接受与未接受治疗的临床结局。 02 研究方法 回顾性纳入来自中国6家医疗中心的949例HBeAg阴性CHB患者,所有患者均符合HBsAg<100 IU/mL、HBV DNA可检出、ALT<正常值上限(40 U/L)的2倍,且无肝硬化。采用逆概率治疗加权(IPTW)和倾向评分匹配(PSM)平衡组间基线特征。本研究的临床结局为肝脏相关事件(LREs,包括肝细胞癌[HCC]和肝硬化)及HBsAg血清学清除。 03 研究结果 中位随访时间为2.9年,26例患者发生LREs,51例实现HBsAg血清学清除。41.3%的患者接受了NA治疗。经IPTW后,未治疗组的6年LREs累积发生率显著高于NA治疗组(10.4% vs. 2.4%,P=0.004)。多变量Cox回归分析显示,NA治疗与LREs风险降低相关(aHR:0.26,95%CI:0.09–0.77,P=0.015),而HCC或肝硬化家族史(aHR:5.43,95% CI:1.68–17.51,P=0.005)及ALT轻度升高(1–2×ULN)(aHR:2.85,95% CI:1.22–6.68,P=0.016)与LREs风险升高相关。排除基线存在显著肝纤维化的患者后,结果仍保持一致。然而,NA治疗与HBsAg血清学清除无显著关联。在PSM队列中也观察到了类似结果。 表2 IPTW和PSM后,治疗组和未治疗组肝脏相关事件的累积发生率 图 4 比较治疗组和未治疗组肝脏相关事件(A、B、C)和HBsAg血清清除(D、E、F)的累积发生率 04 研究结论 对于HBsAg水平较低、HBV DNA可检出且ALT轻度升高的HBeAg阴性CHB患者,NA治疗仍可能带来获益,降低LREs风险。 研究四:抗病毒治疗降低低HBV DNA水平且ALT无显著升高的HBeAg阴性慢性乙型肝炎患者的肝脏相关事件发生风险 (本研究入选Early Career Investigator奖) (4611) 01 研究背景 根据2025年AASLD乙型肝炎指南,通常不推荐对低水平病毒血症且ALT无显著升高的非肝硬化CHB患者进行抗病毒治疗。抗病毒治疗在低水平病毒血症且ALT无显著升高的CHB患者中的临床获益仍不明确。为弥补这一证据空白,本研究比较了接受与未接受治疗的低HBV DNA水平且ALT无显著升高的HBeAg阴性、非肝硬化CHB患者的肝脏相关事件(LREs)长期发生风险。 02 研究方法 本项多中心队列研究纳入了中国5家医疗中心的HBeAg阴性患者,所有患者均无肝硬化,HBV DNA水平较低(20–2000 IU/mL),且ALT无显著升高(<80 U/L)。采用IPTW和PSM平衡组间基线特征。比较接受与未接受治疗患者的LREs发生情况,包括HCC和肝硬化。 03 研究结果 共纳入2129例CHB患者,其中43.0%接受了NA治疗。在中位2.9年的随访期间,41例患者(1.9%)发生LREs,其中未治疗组33例,治疗组8例。在IPTW队列中,未治疗组的6年LRE累积发生率显著高于治疗组(5.8% vs. 1.6%,P=0.004)。多变量Cox回归分析显示,NA治疗与LRE发生风险降低相关(aHR:0.27,95%CI:0.12–0.61,P=0.002)。在排除基线存在显著肝纤维化患者的敏感性分析中,上述结果仍保持一致。PSM队列也得到了相同的结果。 表3 IPTW与PSM校正后,治疗组与未治疗组的肝脏相关事件累积发生率 图5 治疗组与未治疗组肝脏相关事件累积发生率比较。IPTW队列(A)和PSM 队列(B)全人群分析;IPTW队列(C)和PSM队列(D)排除基线显著纤维化患者的敏感性分析 04 研究结论 在低水平病毒血症且ALT无显著升高的HBeAg阴性、非肝硬化CHB患者中,抗病毒治疗与LREs风险显著降低相关,支持扩大此类患者的治疗适应证。 专家简介 黄睿 副教授 获江苏省科学技术奖三等奖1项,江苏医学科技奖二等奖3项,第十五届“江苏青年五四奖章”,南京市科技进步一等奖1项,南京预防医学科技奖一等奖1项。 发表SCI论文210余篇,包括Lancet Infectious Diseases,Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology,Lancet Public Health, Gut,Journal of supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 20, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Review Maps Critical Bidirectional Links Connecting Infectious Pathogens and Chronic Non-Communicable Diseases by November 19, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 5 mins read 0 Review Maps Critical Bidirectional Links Connecting Infectious Pathogens and Chronic Non-Communicable Diseases Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A comprehensive scoping review synthesising over two decades of published medical literature demonstrates extensive, bidirectional links between infectious diseases and chronic non-communicable conditions, challenging the traditional public health paradigm that manages them in isolation. Published in Infectious Diseases of Poverty, the investigation conducted by an international research team highlights how persistent infections directly initiate malignancies and organ damage, while pre-existing non-communicable diseases simultaneously increase patient susceptibility to severe infections. Historically, global health policy, clinical specialities, and health-care financing mechanisms have operated in separate vertical silos, treating communicable pathogens and chronic lifestyle disorders as independent domains. The authors emphasise that the growing coexistence of these health threats creates a complex double burden, particularly in low-income and middle-income nations where health systems face dual pressures from emerging infectious outbreaks and rising rates of chronic illness. The methodological framework of the investigation followed established guidelines for scoping reviews, systematically mapping global evidence published between January 1, 2000, and April 20, 2026. The researchers searched major scientific databases including PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus using broad combinations of terminology related to communicable conditions, chronic diseases, comorbidities, and biological interactions. Across the identified literature, the investigators prioritized English-language systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and population-level studies examining human cohorts, while intentionally excluding studies based exclusively on in vitro models, animal experiments, or non-peer-reviewed commentaries. From an initial pool of 5,799 retrieved bibliographic records, two reviewers independently conducted two-stage screening across titles, abstracts, and full texts to select eligible studies, resolving discrepancies through structured discussion to extract epidemiological effect estimates, relative risks, odds ratios, and corresponding confidence intervals. Discover more Track Biotech Tour Colleges Cancer research funding From the broader database search, 41 systematic reviews and meta-analyses, supplemented by 11 targeted observational studies including cohort and case-control investigations, satisfied all predefined inclusion criteria, yielding a total evidence synthesis of 52 publications. The collected evidence was categorized into two central thematic domains: the direct oncogenic role of specific infectious pathogens in malignant transformation, and the reciprocal impact of chronic metabolic, cardiovascular, and respiratory diseases on host vulnerability and infectious disease severity. The authors noted that global epidemiological data from authoritative international bodies, including the World Health Organization and the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021, demonstrate that non-communicable conditions accounted for 41 million global deaths in 2021 alone, representing 74% of all worldwide mortality, even as recurring and emerging viral threats continue to impose acute population health risks. Discover more Research assistant services Postdoc opportunities Research report templates Learn Engineering In their assessment of infectious precursors to chronic illness, the authors documented that pathogens account for a substantial fraction of global cancer incidence, reflecting 16.1% of incident malignancies in 2008 and 12.2% in 2018 based on carcinogenic classifications established by the International Agency for Research on Cancer. Established viral drivers of cancer featured prominently across the synthesized systematic reviews, notably hepatitis B virus and hepatitis C virus, which serve as primary infectious causes of hepatocellular carcinoma. Infected individuals exhibit a 12.5-fold higher risk of liver cancer when carrying hepatitis B and an 11.2-fold higher risk with hepatitis C compared to uninfected controls, with the two viruses accounting for global attributable fractions of 52% and 21% of hepatocellular carcinoma cases respectively in 2022. Similarly, high-risk strains of human papillomavirus account for an estimated 90% of cervical and anal cancers, 70% of vulvar and vaginal cancers, 60% of penile cancers, and 70% of oropharyngeal carcinomas, while Epstein-Barr virus is associated with over 95% of nasopharyngeal carcinomas in high-incidence zones of Eastern and Southeastern Asia. The review detailed major parasitic and bacterial infections that establish chronic oncogenic pathologies through sustained tissue inflammation and cellular damage. Chronic infection with the parasitic fluke Schistosoma haematobium is classified as a Group 1 human carcinogen, increasing the risk of bladder cancer by approximately 2-fold to 15-fold and detected in 82.4% of bladder cancer specimens in highly endemic regions, where up to 85% of squamous cell bladder carcinomas are attributed to infection. Food-borne liver flukes Clonorchis sinensis and Opisthorchis viverrini significantly increase the odds of cholangiocarcinoma by 4.49-fold and 3.69-fold, respectively, yielding an overall 4.24-fold elevated odds among infected cohorts. Among bacterial agents, Helicobacter pylori, which maintained a global prevalence of 43.1% between 2011 and 2022, increases the risk of non-cardia gastric cancer by 2.5-fold in Asian populations and 5.4-fold in European and North American populations, although eradication therapy achieves an estimated 36% relative reduction in gastric cancer incidence among patients without pre-existing neoplasia. Examining the reciprocal pathway, the scoping review demonstrated that non-communicable chronic conditions substantially weaken host defences, heightening susceptibility to infection and worsening acute clinical outcomes. Individuals diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus demonstrate an estimated 1.5-fold to 4-fold elevated risk of acquiring infections compared to populations without diabetes, driven in part by chronic hyperglycaemia that impairs both innate and adaptive immune responses. The authors noted consistent findings across meta-analyses linking diabetes to heightened vulnerability to pulmonary tuberculosis, severe influenza, and bacterial pneumonia. Cardiovascular disease and chronic respiratory conditions similarly compound the clinical severity of infectious diseases while suffering acute exacerbations triggered by infection. During the Omicron variant wave of SARS-CoV-2, pre-existing heart disease was associated with an approximate 27% increase in the risk of hospital admission, while pre-existing heart failure was linked to a 78% higher risk of death. Furthermore, synthesized meta-analyses revealed that patients suffering from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease were more than five times as likely to develop severe COVID-19 as patients without underlying lung pathology, while individuals with pre-existing cancer faced a 3.6-fold higher risk of severe coronavirus disease. The researchers contextualized these complex interactions within a multidimensional epidemiological triangle encompassing pathogen transmission, host immune competence, and social or environmental determinants. Host defence mechanisms undergo predictable shifts across the lifespan, maturing from childhood into early adulthood before progressively declining with advancing age, a physiological trajectory that intersects directly with the steep rise in chronic disease prevalence among older adults. In addition to age-related biological vulnerability, broader socioeconomic determinants—including poverty, overcrowded living environments, inadequate sanitation, and limited health-care access—jointly foster the transmission of infectious agents while promoting chronic metabolic disease through poor dietary nutrition and economic barriers to ongoing therapy, creating entrenched comorbidities such as coexisting tuberculosis and diabetes in resource-constrained communities. Public health disruptions documented during recent global outbreaks further underscore the practical consequences of fragmented health-care delivery and vertical disease financing. During the emergency response to COVID-19, widespread redirection of clinical personnel, hospital facilities, and diagnostic resources towards the acute viral outbreak severely interrupted routine chronic disease management. The authors conclude that addressing the dual burden of infectious and non-communicable conditions requires a decisive move away from isolated, disease-specific programmes towards integrated clinical and prevention frameworks. Clinical management models can achieve substantial public health benefits by coordinating childhood and adolescent vaccination programmes against oncogenic viruses like hepatitis B virus and human papillomavirus alongside routine screening, lifestyle modification support, and early medical intervention for metabolic and cardiovascular disorders. Systemic health policies that bridge traditional funding streams and combine primary prevention, infection control, and chronic disease surveillance represent essential strategies for mitigating synergistic health risks and building sustainable health systems worldwide.
